    fn dialog(ctx: &Context, state: &TodoApp) -> ActionResult {
        let shell = Context::for_action(ctx.inner().clone(), ctx.surface(), Some(DIALOG_ROOT));
        let local = ctx.get::<OnDevice>().is_some();
        let tree = if let Some(id) = state.delete_target {
            let confirm = if local {
                html! {<DestructiveButton value={id} on:tap={confirm_local_delete}>Confirm</DestructiveButton>}
            } else {
                html! {<DestructiveButton value={id} on:tap={confirm_delete}>Confirm</DestructiveButton>}
            };
            html! { <ConfirmationDialog>
                <SheetTitle>Delete this todo?</SheetTitle>
                {confirm}
                <CancelButton on:tap={close_dialog}>Cancel</CancelButton>
            </ConfirmationDialog> }
        } else if state.add_dialog {
            let input = if local {
                html! {<TextInput placeholder="Todo title" a11y_label="Todo title" on:submit={add_local_todo}/>}
            } else {
                html! {<TextInput placeholder="Todo title" a11y_label="Todo title" on:submit={add_todo}/>}
            };
            html! { <Modal a11y_label="New todo"><BottomSheet>
                <SheetTitle>New todo</SheetTitle>
                {input}
                <CancelButton on:tap={close_dialog}>Cancel</CancelButton>
                <SubmitButton>Add</SubmitButton>
            </BottomSheet></Modal> }
        } else {
            html! {<Stack/>}
        };
        render(&shell, ctx.receiver(), tree, None::<&()>)?;
        Ok(())
    }
    
    #[action(host)]
    async fn open_add_dialog(ctx: &Context, _event: Interaction<()>) -> ActionResult {
        dialog(
            ctx,
            &TodoApp {
                add_dialog: true,
                ..TodoApp::default()
            },
        )
    }
    #[action(host)]
    async fn open_delete_dialog(ctx: &Context, event: Interaction<()>) -> ActionResult {
        let id: u64 = event
            .input_value
            .parse()
            .map_err(|_| error("Invalid todo identifier"))?;
        dialog(
            ctx,
            &TodoApp {
                delete_target: Some(id),
                ..TodoApp::default()
            },
        )
    }
    #[action(host)]
    async fn close_dialog(ctx: &Context, _event: Interaction<()>) -> ActionResult {
        dialog(ctx, &TodoApp::default())
    }
    #[action(host)]
    async fn filter_todos(ctx: &Context, event: Interaction<()>) -> ActionResult {
        let filter = match event.input_value.as_str() {
            "all" => Filter::All,
            "open" => Filter::Open,
            "done" => Filter::Done,
            _ => return Err(error("Unknown filter")),
        };
        if ctx.get::<OnDevice>().is_some() {
            let store = todo_store(ctx)?;
            let mut guard = store
                .0
                .lock()
                .unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner);
            guard.filter = filter;
            return page(ctx, &guard.snapshot());
        }
        set_filter(ctx, &filter);
        Ok(())
    }
    
    fn todo_store(ctx: &Context) -> Result<Arc<TodoStore>, ErrorTrace<ActionError>> {
        ctx.get::<TodoStore>()
            .ok_or_else(|| error("Missing todo store"))
    }
    
    fn mutate(
        ctx: &Context,
        change: impl FnOnce(&mut u64, &mut Vec<Todo>) -> ActionResult,
    ) -> ActionResult {
        let store = todo_store(ctx)?;
        let mut guard = store
            .0
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner);
        let mut next = guard.clone();
        change(&mut next.last_id, &mut next.items)?;
        let state = next.snapshot();
        #[cfg(all(feature = "server", not(target_family = "wasm")))]
        if let Some(channels) = ctx.get::<crate::server::TodoFeed>() {
            dialog(ctx, &state)?;
            channels
                .publish(ctx.inner(), &state)
                .map_err(|failure| error(&failure.to_string()))?;
            *guard = next;
            return Ok(());
        }
        page(ctx, &state)?;
        dialog(ctx, &state)?;
        *guard = next;
        Ok(())
    }
    
    #[action(server)]
    async fn add_todo(ctx: &Context, event: Interaction<()>) -> ActionResult {
        add(ctx, &event.input_value)
    }
    
    fn add(ctx: &Context, input: &str) -> ActionResult {
        let title = input.trim();
        if title.is_empty() {
            return Err(error("Enter a todo title"));
        }
        mutate(ctx, |last, items| {
            *last = last
                .checked_add(1)
                .ok_or_else(|| error("No more todo identifiers"))?;
            items.push(Todo {
                id: *last,
                text: title.to_owned(),
                done: false,
            });
            Ok(())
        })?;
        if ctx.get::<OnDevice>().is_none() {
            // MessagePack fixstr for the page notification.
            ctx.receiver().data(PAGE_ROOT, b"\xabhost:notify".to_vec());
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    #[action(server)]
    async fn toggle_todo(ctx: &Context, event: Interaction<()>) -> ActionResult {
        toggle(ctx, &event.input_value)
    }
    
    fn toggle(ctx: &Context, input: &str) -> ActionResult {
        let id = todo_id(input)?;
        mutate(ctx, |_, items| {
            let item = items
                .iter_mut()
                .find(|item| item.id == id)
                .ok_or_else(|| error("Todo does not exist"))?;
            item.done = !item.done;
            Ok(())
        })
    }
    #[action(server)]
    async fn confirm_delete(ctx: &Context, event: Interaction<()>) -> ActionResult {
        delete(ctx, &event.input_value)
    }
    
    fn delete(ctx: &Context, input: &str) -> ActionResult {
        let id = todo_id(input)?;
        mutate(ctx, |_, items| {
            let index = items
                .iter()
                .position(|item| item.id == id)
                .ok_or_else(|| error("already deleted"))?;
            items.remove(index);
            Ok(())
        })
    }
    
    fn todo_id(input: &str) -> Result<u64, ErrorTrace<ActionError>> {
        input.parse().map_err(|_| error("Invalid todo identifier"))
    }
    
    #[action(host, mobile)]
    async fn add_local_todo(ctx: &Context, event: Interaction<()>) -> ActionResult {
        add(ctx, &event.input_value)
    }
    
    #[action(host, mobile)]
    async fn toggle_local_todo(ctx: &Context, event: Interaction<()>) -> ActionResult {
        toggle(ctx, &event.input_value)
    }
    
    #[action(host, mobile)]
    async fn confirm_local_delete(ctx: &Context, event: Interaction<()>) -> ActionResult {
        delete(ctx, &event.input_value)
    }
    
    #[action(host, mobile)]
    async fn initialize_todos(ctx: &Context, _event: Interaction<()>) -> ActionResult {
        use foundation_ui_wire::{CreateNodeT, NodeKind, OperationT, UiOperationT};
    
        let out = ctx.receiver();
        for root in [PAGE_ROOT, DIALOG_ROOT] {
            let mut create = CreateNodeT::default();
            create.node_id = root;
            create.kind = NodeKind::STACK;
            let mut op = OperationT::default();
            op.ui = UiOperationT::CreateNode(Box::new(create));
            out.render_op(op);
            out.render_op(foundation_ui_wire::ops::append_child(1, root));
        }
        app(ctx, &todo_store(ctx)?.snapshot())
    }
    
    /// Installs the on-device store and returns its action registry.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Returns an invalid or duplicate action declaration.
    pub fn local_registry(ctx: &Ctx) -> Result<ActionRegistry, RegistrationError> {
        let mut actions = host_registry()?;
        actions.register(initialize_todos)?;
        actions.register(add_local_todo)?;
        actions.register(toggle_local_todo)?;
        actions.register(confirm_local_delete)?;
        ctx.store(TodoStore::default());
        ctx.store(OnDevice);
        Ok(actions)
    }
    
    /// Builds the server action registry.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Returns an invalid or duplicate action declaration.
    pub fn server_registry() -> Result<ActionRegistry, RegistrationError> {
        let mut actions = ActionRegistry::new();
        actions.register(refresh_count)?;
        actions.register(add_todo)?;
        actions.register(toggle_todo)?;
        actions.register(confirm_delete)?;
        Ok(actions)
    }
    /// Builds the browser or native host action registry.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Returns an invalid or duplicate action declaration.
    pub fn host_registry() -> Result<ActionRegistry, RegistrationError> {
        let mut actions = ActionRegistry::new();
        actions.register(open_add_dialog)?;
        actions.register(open_delete_dialog)?;
        actions.register(close_dialog)?;
        actions.register(filter_todos)?;
        actions.register(notify)?;

    }

    //! Configure the host and publish the list and count after a successful change.
    use super::Error;
    use crate::{open_count_label, render_live_lists, TodoApp, TodoStore, PAGE_ROOT};
    use foundation_context::Ctx;
    use foundation_ui_http::ActionRequestPolicy;
    use foundation_ui_runtime::{

    #[derive(Clone)]
    pub(crate) struct TodoFeed(pub(super) LiveChannel);
    
    impl TodoFeed {
        pub(crate) fn publish(&self, ctx: &Ctx, state: &TodoApp) -> Result<(), Error> {
            let view = Context::for_render(ctx.clone());
            render_live_lists(&view, state)?;
            let count = state.items.iter().filter(|item| !item.done).count();
            html_swap! {"#open-count", &view, view.receiver(), <ListFooter id="open-count">{open_count_label(count)}</ListFooter>}?;
            self.0
                .sender()
                .push_messages(prepare_messages(ctx, view.into_receiver().drain())?)?;
            Ok(())
        }
    }
    
    struct BusinessActions;
    impl ActionRequestPolicy for BusinessActions {
        fn check(&self, _: &Ctx, action: ActionRequest<'_>) -> Result<(), ActionError> {
            if action.state().is_some() {
                return Err(ActionError::new(
                    ErrorCode::StateRejected,
                    "Business actions reject presentation state",
                ));
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    }
    
    pub(super) fn install(ctx: &Ctx, web: LiveChannel, store: TodoStore) -> Result<TodoFeed, Error> {
        if web.stream_id() != 1 {
            return Err("The todo page listens to stream 1".into());
        }
        crate::install_view_services(ctx, 100, (1 << 31) - 1)?;
        ctx.store(RenderTarget(PAGE_ROOT));
        ctx.store(store);
        ctx.store(Arc::new(BusinessActions) as Arc<dyn ActionRequestPolicy>);
        let channels = TodoFeed(web);
        let feed = channels.0.clone();
        ctx.store(foundation_ui_runtime::dispatch::SubscriptionReplay::new(
            move |_, _| vec![Arc::new(feed.clone())],
        ));
        ctx.store(channels.clone());
        Ok(channels)
    }
    
    pub(super) fn channel(id: u64) -> LiveChannel {
        LiveChannel::new(id, BacklogConfig::default(), WriterConfig::default())
    }

        module: &Path,
        items: Vec<crate::Todo>,
    ) -> Result<HttpApp<Arc<dyn Serve>>, Error> {
        let mut ids = std::collections::HashSet::with_capacity(items.len());
        if items
            .iter()
            .any(|item| item.id == 0 || !ids.insert(item.id))
        {
            return Err("Invalid restored todo identifiers".into());
        }
        app_with_store(module, services::channel(1), TodoStore::with_items(items))
    }
    
    /// Builds the application with a host-supplied stream for replay tests.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Returns an error when the channel, routes, signer or assets are invalid.
    pub fn app_with_channel(
        module: &Path,
        channel: LiveChannel,
    ) -> Result<HttpApp<Arc<dyn Serve>>, Error> {
        app_with_store(module, channel, TodoStore::default())
    }
    
    fn app_with_store(
        module: &Path,
        channel: LiveChannel,
        store: TodoStore,
    ) -> Result<HttpApp<Arc<dyn Serve>>, Error> {
        let mut app = HttpApp::new_serve();
        let ctx = app.context().clone();
        let channels = services::install(&ctx, channel, store)?;
        register(&mut app.router, &ctx, channels)?;
        assets::register(&mut app.router, module)?;
        Ok(app)
    }
    
    fn register(
        router: &mut Router<Arc<dyn Serve>>,
        ctx: &Ctx,
        channels: TodoFeed,
    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
        let actions = ActionRegistryRouteHandler::new(crate::server_registry()?);
        let mut rpc = foundation_connectrpc::Router::new();
        foundation_ui_connectrpc::v1::register_actions(
            &mut rpc,
            Arc::new(foundation_ui_connectrpc::ActionService::new(
                actions.dispatcher(),
            )),
        );
        crate::todo_rpc::register_todos(&mut rpc, Arc::new(services::Todos));
        let handler = Arc::new(rpc.into_handler());
        for path in [
            foundation_ui_connectrpc::v1::procedure::EXCHANGE,
            crate::todo_rpc::procedure::GET_TODO,
        ] {
            router.at(
                path,
                foundation_http::post(foundation_connectrpc::ConnectRpcServe::from_arc(
                    handler.clone(),
                )),
            )?;
        }
        router.mount(foundation_ui_http::ActionSocketRoute::new(
            actions.dispatcher(),
        ))?;
        let dispatcher = actions.dispatcher();
        router.mount(actions)?;
        router.mount(initial)?;
        router.mount(count_screen)?;
        let stream = StreamHandler::create(ctx).with_channel(channels.0);
        let events = foundation_ui_http::EventDelivery::new(dispatcher, stream);
        router.at("/live", get(events.clone()))?;
        router.at("/live", foundation_http::post(events))?;
        Ok(())
    }
    
    /// Starts the plain data service with one known todo. Only the generated data procedure is mounted.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Returns the route registration error.
    pub fn data_app() -> Result<HttpApp<Arc<dyn Serve>>, Error> {
        let mut app = HttpApp::new_serve();
        app.context().store(TodoStore::with_items(vec![crate::Todo {
            id: 42,
            text: "Buy milk".into(),
            done: false,
        }]));
        let mut rpc = foundation_connectrpc::Router::new();
        crate::todo_rpc::register_todos(&mut rpc, Arc::new(services::Todos));
        app.router.at(
            crate::todo_rpc::procedure::GET_TODO,
            foundation_http::post(foundation_connectrpc::ConnectRpcServe::new(
                rpc.into_handler(),
            )),
        )?;
        Ok(app)
    }

    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Returns a lowering, identifier allocation or state serialization error.
    pub fn render<S: Serialize + ?Sized>(
        ctx: &Context,
        out: &ActionReceiver,
        mut html: Html,
        state: Option<&S>,
    ) -> Result<Html, foundation_errstacks::ErrorTrace<crate::action::ActionError>> {
        let root = ctx.state_root();
        if ctx.is_action() && root.is_none() {
            return Err(LowerError::NoComponentRoot.into());
        }
        let tree = frame_tree(ctx, &html, root.unwrap_or(1), root)?;
        html.runtime_id = Some(tree.root);
        let placement = if let Some(root) = root {
            Some(table!(PlaceT {
                kind: PlacementKind::Swap,
                target: Some(Target::Node(root).wire()?),
                root_node: root
            }))
        } else {
            None
        };
        queue(out, tree, placement, state)?;
        Ok(html)
    }

## Assistant

**`local` answers one legitimate question: who owns the todo store?** An iPhone can use the server store or its own on-device store. Both versions display the same controls. The problem is that the page builder also uses `local` to choose the layout, action bindings, and update behavior. [Mobile setup](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe-resume-combined/examples/ui_todo/src/mobile.rs:21)

The flag predates the synchronization repair. It originally selected the toggle action for each row. Commit `b0215cfcf` expanded its role when it added live list updates. That is how a choice about storage reached the page layout. [Row rendering](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe-resume-combined/examples/ui_todo/src/shared/mod.rs:138)

### What happens today

| Operation | Server-backed Todo | On-device Todo |
|---|---|---|
| Open the page | `/initial` reads the store and its stream position together. It renders three filtered lists and subscribes to `/live`. | The host creates the page and dialog roots. It renders one list from the device store. |
| Change the filter | A host action changes section visibility and button selection on that client. | A host action saves the filter in the device store and renders the whole page again. |
| Add, complete, reopen, or delete | The server changes the records. The live stream sends all three lists and the count to subscribers. The action reply updates the caller’s dialog. | A device action calls the same mutation logic. It renders the whole page and updates the dialog. |

The three server-backed lists serve a purpose. Each client can select its own filter while every subscriber receives the same publication. The server never needs to know which filter an individual client selected. The cost is that each mutation rebuilds all three lists. Our Chrome, iPhone, and Android tests verified the visible changes and replay. [Page construction](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe-resume-combined/examples/ui_todo/src/shared/mod.rs:168) · [Live publication](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe-resume-combined/examples/ui_todo/src/server/services.rs:18)

### Where the responsibilities cross

`page_tree` returns the same `&TodoApp` that its caller supplies. The server caller immediately discards that return value with `.0`. The action caller passes it back to `render` for the presentation state. A page builder can return `Html` alone. The caller already has the state when it needs to attach it. [Server screen](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe-resume-combined/examples/ui_todo/src/server/screens.rs:8) · [Action render](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe-resume-combined/examples/ui_todo/src/shared/mod.rs:151)

Removing the Boolean parameter alone would leave most of the problem. `dialog()` checks the `OnDevice` marker to choose its submit action. `filter_todos()` checks the marker to choose its update strategy. `mutate()` checks for a `TodoFeed` to decide whether to publish or redraw. Reading one action therefore requires knowing which services the startup code installed. [Dialog bindings](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe-resume-combined/examples/ui_todo/src/shared/mod.rs:313) · [Mutation and delivery](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe-resume-combined/examples/ui_todo/src/shared/mod.rs:406)

### What the framework already supports

The framework can render an initial tree, dispatch host and server actions, and replace a named element. The count already demonstrates the desired pattern. The page declares `id="open-count"`. A later publication replaces `#open-count` on every client. The lists still use numeric anchors. The filter action constructs low-level instructions to set `hidden` and `checked` by node number. Named replacement works today. Named property updates need a separate check before the design relies on them. [Framework placement](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe-resume-combined/backends/foundation_ui_runtime/src/view/render.rs:262) · [Current filter update](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe-resume-combined/examples/ui_todo/src/shared/mod.rs:233)

### How I would untangle it

1. **Render one page.** Give `page_tree(&TodoApp) -> Html` one layout with named elements. Let server setup attach the live subscription.
2. **Choose action execution at startup.** The server-backed and on-device entry points already build different registries. Resolve mutation bindings there so rows and dialogs can each declare their controls once.
3. **Give actions specific updates.** Opening a dialog changes `#dialog`. Changing a filter affects only that client. A todo mutation updates the affected list content and count.
4. **Keep delivery outside the mutation.** Both stores can use the same add, toggle, and delete logic. The device delivers updates directly. The server publishes shared updates and sends dialog changes only to the caller.

The behavior worth preserving is that **another client can change a todo while my filter and unfinished dialog stay intact**. That requirement explains the current implementation. It also gives us a concrete test for a simpler one. This is a code review and design recommendation. The implementation remains unchanged.

## User

> local answers one legitimate question: who owns the todo store? An iPhone can use the server store or its own on-device store. Both versions display the same controls. The problem is that the page builder also uses local to choose the layout, action bindings, and update behavior

Having a local store for fast local caching is good, but your decision to create the same actions for local vs remote/server is the bad choice, we should keep a set going to the server, they prove the server action path, then local actions that do other things .e.g the game i asked to be ported from ewe_gamify to test our gpu rendering system, we can add a action that boots that up, and runs the process rendering that till the user closest the view via some wrapper rendering we add.

We create other local actions like searching locally on whats already rendered, so a search box that only uses the local store, and when updates come in, so when changes occur, the server makes it updates and sends the new update to us, we can also listen it for a new todo list addition data or add a data into the ui change message the server actions sends, e.g state, instead its not a full todo state but just an enum with differnt instructions so the app can update its own state, this proves also sending state update as well and even maybe an action sending state update only but i think your refresh action already covers that.

This also stops the switch statements of use local action here or if not local server action, thats a bad architecture, we need not duplicate same actions on both ends, but assign them roles for specific usecases.

We also need to be thoughtful for the rendering where we might still be in anwyay we creating situations where we render one thing for local or mobile or web, this is bad and a architectyure smell, we always build the tags and capabilities so one thing can work across, how it works in each maybe different but it provides the same concept, then the user might decide an action is only for web and only whatever is using web uses that, mobile does not need care, etc

    # Feature 36. Play Mathalley in a second todo view
    
    Status: Proposed for review. Implement this feature last, after every other feature in Specification 69 is complete.
    
    ## Glossary
    
    A view is an independently mounted content area.
    A graphics processing unit (GPU) draws the game into a surface supplied by the host.
    A hit region is the area where a tap selects a game action.
    
    ## User flow
    
    Open the todo application. Select **Play Mathalley**. The application opens a game view beside the existing todo view in the host’s navigation.
    Start a run. Play Gumball and Train. Return to Todos. The same list, filter, and stored items remain available.
    
    ```mermaid
    flowchart LR
        T[Todo view] -->|Play Mathalley| G[Game view]
        G -->|Local input| R[Rust game and scene]
        R -->|Draw| S[Game surface]
        G -->|Back| T
    ```
    
    The game owns its surface. The todo view keeps its own mount and subscriptions.
    
    ## Stage 1. Port the reference game
    
    Use the sibling ewe_gamify repository as the source reference. Inspect src/game.rs, scene.rs, gpu.rs, audio.rs, and lib.rs.
    Record the reference revision before starting. Keep the port inside the single ui_todo Rust package.
    Build from a clean ewe_platform checkout without a dependency on the sibling directory.
    
    Preserve the title, intro, round tally, lives, difficulty progression, game over, and restart flow.
    Preserve both mini-games, their hit regions, the procedural music, cues, and mute control.
    Reuse the pure Rust game and scene logic. Inject time and randomness through the host for deterministic tests.
    Use the reference’s 390 by 844 design space for drawing and input. Exclude the letterbox margins from hit tests.
    
    ## Stage 2. Use framework navigation and graphics
    
    - Add the game entry to browser, iOS, and Android todo screens, including the on-device and server-backed mobile examples.
    - Register separate todo and game views through the public framework. Use local actions to open and close the game.
    - Use Feature 32 for view targeting. Keep remote todo updates scoped to the todo view while the game is open.
    - Use Feature 34 to draw through wgpu. Exercise Feature 35 with a host-owned device in an integration configuration.
    - Keep game input, simulation, and drawing local. A server-backed todo screen can open the same local game.
    - Let the host schedule drawing and map pointer or touch coordinates to game coordinates.
    - Reconfigure on resize and rotation. Pause simulation and sound when hidden. Resume without charging time spent away.
    - On close, release the surface, audio, and frame callbacks. Keep the todo host and its graphics device available.
    - If graphics initialization fails, show a recoverable error in the game view and keep the todo view usable.
    
    ## Stage 3. Verify the integrated application
    
    1. Run deterministic tests for both mini-games and the complete run lifecycle.
    2. On each platform, enter a todo, select a filter, open the game, play, and return.
    3. Verify the same todo state after returning. Deliver a live count update while the game view is active.
    4. Verify that game input and graphics updates reach only the game view. Verify that the todo receives its count update.
    5. Repeat open, close, resize, and background transitions. Check for duplicate input, stale callbacks, and resource leaks.
    6. Verify an input hit and a known rendered scene on real graphics backends. Record hardware and simulator coverage separately.
    7. Capture the game and the return to Todos on web, iOS, and Android. Compare key scenes against the reference.
    8. Update the todo README with launch commands, controls, navigation, and graphics ownership for each platform.

    ## Stage 4. Use one endpoint for each screen
    
    | Route | Frame content | Callers |
    |---|---|---|
    | `GET /initial` | Full todo view with a dialog area and a live count subscription | Browser, iOS, and Android todo apps |
    | `GET /open-count` | Open count with a Refresh button bound to `refresh_count` | Browser, iOS, and Android starter clients |
    
    Build each screen once with shared controls and named targets. Both handlers return a frame.
    Use the same count subscription from the full view on each platform.
    Point every starter at the count screen. Declare its refresh action on the browser.
    Remove `/native-initial` and `/native-starter` from route registration, callers, tests, templates, and current setup guides.
    Keep action submission and live subscription endpoints available.
    Load both routes on all three platforms. Submit Refresh and verify that the displayed count matches the server.
    Check that an update after initial load reaches the correct count target on each platform.
    
    ## Acceptance checks
    
    1. Run common placement fixtures on web, Swift, and Kotlin. Check names on every shared element kind.
    2. Verify default append, initial replacement, named views, qualified targets, and every relative placement.
    3. Mount two views with identical child names. Deliver a reply to each. Check that its sibling stays unchanged.
    4. Reject duplicate names, wrong types, missing children, and ambiguous destinations before mutation.
    5. Replace a named subtree twice. Remove it, reuse its name, and verify cleanup when its view closes.
    6. Deliver one captured count frame unchanged to all three renderers. Verify the displayed count on each platform.
    7. Connect web and native subscribers to the same running endpoint. Publish once and verify independent resume.
    8. Update the framework and mobile package README files. Show default placement, explicit view selection, and a typed element target.
    
    Use the existing [mobile designs](../23-native-design-and-themes/feature.md) for the todo regression check.
    
    ## Remaining Todo targets
    
    Issue #714 tracks the application targets added during the synchronization repair.
    
    1. Give each addressed list, section, filter button, and notification an identifier in shared markup.
    2. Use the existing dialog identifier for dialog updates. Check page placement against the receiving view contract.
    3. Replace numeric list anchors with named placement. Keep names stable across replacement and replay.
    4. Check whether the framework supports named property updates for visibility and selection.
    5. If support is missing, resolve names in the framework before applying properties on each renderer.
    6. Keep todo record identifiers separate from view element names.
    7. Verify repeated updates, draft preservation, filter selection, and notifications on Chrome, iPhone, and Android.
    8. Inspect emitted targets as well as displayed rows. Use the existing mobile designs for visual comparison.

    # Feature 27. Build the todo application from one Rust package
    
    ## Glossary
    
    | Term | Meaning |
    |---|---|
    | Package | A set of Rust build targets with one Cargo manifest. |
    | Feature | A named Cargo option that selects code and dependencies for a build. |
    | WebAssembly (Wasm) | The compiled module format that the browser loads. |
    | Binding | Generated code that lets Swift or Kotlin call Rust functions. |
    
    ## Outcome
    
    An author edits the todo application in `examples/ui_todo`. One manifest builds the server, browser module, and mobile library.
    Today, the browser and mobile adapters each have their own manifest. Both already import the shared todo package.
    
    ```mermaid
    flowchart LR
        Server[Server executable] --> Shared[Shared todo code]
        Browser[Browser exports] --> Shared
        Mobile[Mobile exports] --> Shared
    ```
    
    Each entry point calls the same application code.
    
    ## Stage 1. Organize the package
    
    | Path under `examples/ui_todo` | Contents |
    |---|---|
    | `src/shared/` | Todo state, stores, views, action functions, and registry builders |
    | `src/lib.rs` | Module declarations and existing public exports |
    | `src/mobile.rs` | Both mobile core constructors and the initial frame function |
    | `src/web.rs` | The browser startup function, `init_todo_host` |
    | `src/server.rs` | Server implementation |
    | `src/bin/server.rs` | Server entry point. Keep the existing executable name, `ui_todo`. |
    
    Keep the Rust paths that callers use today. Move the native integration tests under the package's `tests/` directory.
    Keep the generated Swift and Kotlin constructors callable from the existing screens.
    Each screen selects local or remote execution when it creates its core.
    
    ## Stage 2. Select each output
    
    Declare one library with crate types `rlib`, `staticlib`, and `cdylib`. Select platform modules and optional dependencies with Cargo features.
    Keep the existing default server build. Use explicit features for cross-platform builds.
    Compile the web exports only for Wasm. Permit a desktop mobile-library build for binding generation.
    
    ```rust
    pub mod shared;
    
    #[cfg(all(feature = "web", target_arch = "wasm32"))]
    mod web;
    
    #[cfg(all(feature = "mobile", not(target_family = "wasm")))]
    mod mobile;
    
    #[cfg(all(feature = "server", not(target_family = "wasm")))]
    pub mod server;
    ```
    
    | Consumer | Build selection for package `ui_todo` | Output it uses |
    |---|---|---|
    | Server | `--bin ui_todo --features server` | Host executable |

## Assistant

I would revise points 2 and 4. Choosing mutation handlers at startup still gives `add_todo` two possible owners. Your design gives it one owner everywhere. A useful way to examine all four points is to follow one **Add** from the dialog to another client.

1. **Render one page.** Chrome, iPhone, and Android use the same page declaration. It contains the search field, filter controls, list, count, and dialog area. Each element that receives an update has a name. The dialog declares `on:submit={add_todo}` once. It only needs the dialog kind and, for deletion, the selected record.

2. **Give each action one owner.** Opening or cancelling the dialog runs on the host. Submitting a title runs on the server. Searching cached records runs on the host. Opening Mathalley also runs on the host, which owns the game loop until the view closes. Startup connects each action to its declared owner. It never chooses who owns Add.

3. **Give each result a destination.** When the server accepts an addition, its reply closes the submitting client’s dialog. The live publication carries a typed change such as `Added(todo)` to every subscriber, including the submitting client. That gives each client one ordered path for updating its cache. A rejected addition leaves the draft open and shows the error to its author.

4. **Give each visible element one writer.** This is the part I would settle before implementation. I propose that the server owns the records and publishes their changes. Each host owns the visible rows because each host knows its current search and filter. A host action applies the cache change and updates `#todo-list` using the shared row renderer. The server can continue updating `#open-count` directly while that count means *all open todos*.

For example, suppose my search is **milk** and my add dialog contains an unfinished draft. You add **Buy bread**. My cache receives the record, my visible list stays the same, and my open count increases. My draft stays open. When I clear the search, **Buy bread** appears immediately from my cache. That example also exposes a design conflict. A server publication that replaces my entire `#todo-list` could erase my search result.

The existing Refresh action renders the count screen again. To prove **state-only delivery**, I would test a publication carrying `Added(todo)` with zero rendering instructions. The test should verify that the host receives the change, updates its cache, and applies its active search.

**Would you give the host ownership of `#todo-list`, with the server publishing record changes and continuing to own `#open-count`?** That choice determines the contract between the Todo actions and the framework.

    Proposed instructions carry an added record, an updated record, or a removed record identifier.
    Updates carry the resulting values. Applying the same update twice must preserve the same result.
    Send the typed change with the shared view update in the same ordered publication.
    Use the existing frame and data paths where they support ordered delivery to the receiving view.
    Keep cache instructions separate from signed presentation state. The server validates mutations against its own records.
    Apply a change once per stream position. Restore the cache from a fresh snapshot when replay expires.
    Keep the search text, filter, and open draft on the client during live delivery.
    Give one action responsibility for updating the visible list from the cache and current search.
    The current wire property operation takes a numeric node handle.
    Replace a named control or add named property targeting in the framework. Keep that handle out of application code.
    A late action reply must never replace a newer list. Keep dialog confirmation feedback scoped to the requesting client.
    The current Refresh action renders the count screen again. A separate test must verify data-only delivery.
    
    ```mermaid
    flowchart LR
        D[Dialog submit] --> S[Server action and store]
        S --> P[Ordered publication with typed change]
        P --> C[Client cache]
        Q[Local search or filter] --> L[Render matching rows]
        C --> L
        H[Local open or cancel] --> A[Dialog area]
        G[Local Play Mathalley] --> V[Game view]
        V -->|Close| T[Return to Todos]
    ```
    
    The server publishes record changes. Each client applies its own search and filter.
    
    ### Acceptance checks for this revision
    
    1. Inspect the initial page and dialog bindings on Chrome, iPhone, and Android.
    2. Verify that each mutation invokes exactly one server action. Verify that opening and cancelling send no request.
    3. Search cached records with the network disconnected. Reconnect and check additions, completion changes, and deletions against the active query.
    4. Replay a duplicate update. Expire the replay history. Verify recovery without duplicate rows or lost local input.
    5. Deliver a cache instruction without any rendering operation. Verify the receiving client's cache independently of the count screen.
    6. Verify named targets and displayed rows on all three renderers. Inspect the outgoing frames for numeric application targets.
    7. Verify that platform-scoped actions respect their declared scope through framework dispatch.
    8. Use Feature 36 to verify game startup, continued todo delivery, and resource release when the game closes.

## Assistant

I agree with your revision. **Add should feel immediate.** The host can close the dialog and show a pending row as soon as it records the submission locally. The server still owns acceptance. That gives each action a clear role without duplicating the mutation.

Freezing search results also makes sense. Suppose I search for **milk** and another client adds **Buy milk**. My cache receives it immediately. My displayed results stay still until I edit or clear the query. That preserves the list I am reading and retains the update.

I see six cases worth settling before implementation.

| Case | Behavior I recommend |
|---|---|
| **The server accepts Add, but the reply gets lost.** | Generate one universally unique identifier (UUID) before sending. Retry with that same identifier. The server must recognize it and return the original outcome. A UUID alone does not make the operation idempotent. |
| **Messages arrive in a different order.** | A live addition can arrive before the action reply. Confirm the pending row once. A later timeout must never put **Try again** on a confirmed row. |
| **The app closes while Add is pending.** | Save the pending identifier and title before closing the dialog. On restart, reconcile them with the server snapshot. Two separate submissions with identical titles still need distinct identifiers. |
| **An action targets stale data.** | A frozen search result can still show a todo that another client deleted. Check its identifier before acting. A delayed retry of the original Add must never recreate that deleted todo. |
| **The server rejects the title.** | A temporary failure gets **Try again**. A validation failure gets **Edit** with the original title preserved. Give pending rows a text label and respect reduced-motion settings. |
| **The unblock message gets lost.** | Give each block an identifier and a server expiry. On reconnect or resume, fetch the current block. A late release for an older block must never dismiss a newer one. |

Two display decisions follow from this. First, I would keep the open count tied to **confirmed** records. Otherwise the pending row and the live update can increment it twice. Second, I would treat **my own submission** as explicit feedback during search. If it falls outside the frozen results, show its pending status separately and keep the results still.

The one-minute block is a better demonstration of server-driven dismissal than the Add dialog. I would scope it to the initiating client and start the blocking countdown after server acknowledgement. That prevents a lost request from trapping the user. The overlay should block application input while live updates continue underneath it.

I recorded these points in the proposed design. The implementation still awaits approval. [Feature 32 plan](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe-resume-combined/specifications/69-foundation-ui-v2/features/32-portable-view-targets/feature.md)

    ## Remaining Todo targets
    
    Issue #714 tracks the application targets added during the synchronization repair.
    
    ### Action ownership
    
    The server owns todo records. Each client keeps a local copy for display and search.
    Each action has one owner and one purpose.
    
    | Intent | Owner | Result |
    |---|---|---|
    | Open, cancel, or dismiss a dialog | Host | Update the named dialog area on this client. |
    | Submit a title or confirm deletion | Server | Validate the request and change the server store. |
    | Complete or reopen a todo | Server | Change the record and publish the resulting status. |
    | Search or filter | Host | Select matching cached records and update this client's list. |
    | Open or close Mathalley | Host | Start or release the game view described in Feature 36. |

## Assistant

Yes. **The server owns committed todo records. The local store owns what the user sees.** That gives pending, confirmed, and failed items one rendering path.

For **Add**, the flow becomes:

1. The host saves the title and its identifier in the local store as pending. It closes the dialog and renders the faded row immediately.
2. The server validates and commits the addition. Its action returns the committed change as data. The live stream publishes that same change to subscribers.
3. The submitting client can receive either delivery first. One local action applies the change once and marks the existing row as confirmed.
4. If submission fails, the host updates the local row to show **Try again**. Retry uses the original identifier.

I would keep one distinction around **re-rendering the page**. The initial request renders the whole page. Later, the same shared rendering code updates only the affected named regions. An incoming todo should never replace an open dialog, move keyboard focus, or erase a search query. While search is active, the store keeps receiving changes. Editing or clearing the query renders the latest matching records.

I also revise my earlier suggestion about the count. On the full Todo page, **the host should derive the open count from confirmed records in the same local store**. That keeps the rows and count consistent when a reply arrives before its live update. The separate count screen can still demonstrate a server action that returns rendered content.

I updated the [Feature 32 plan](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe-resume-combined/specifications/69-foundation-ui-v2/features/32-portable-view-targets/feature.md) with this flow. It remains a proposed design.

## Assistant

Yes. **One local store and one row renderer replace several competing update paths.** The server sends the same record change to every client. It never needs to know which client is searching, which filter is active, or which dialog is open.

Take a slow Add. The row starts as `Pending`. If the live update arrives first, the store changes it to `Confirmed`. A later timeout leaves it confirmed. If the request fails first, the same renderer shows **Try again** on that row. The dialog closes on submission and has no further role.

That also removes the reason to maintain three hidden lists for All, Open, and Done. The host can render one list from its cache and selected filter. During search, incoming changes update the cache. Clearing search renders the current records.

Retries and replay still need care, but their rules now live in two places with clear responsibilities. **The server prevents duplicate writes. The local store prevents duplicate display updates.** The one-minute block stays a separate example of a server response that dismisses a view.

    ## Repository migration
    
    1. Inventory callers in scripts, mise tasks, package scripts, documentation, and CI workflows.
    2. Give each operation a package owner, task name, typed arguments, output contract, and platform requirements.
    3. Port native UI operations first. Use Rust for orchestration and keep external tools for their specialized operations.
    4. Compare the old and new entry points against the same temporary workspace and candidate inputs.
    5. Switch existing callers after equivalent results. Keep compatibility launchers during the transition.
    6. Apply the same procedure to the remaining repository scripts. Record each caller before retiring its launcher.
    
    | Current inputs | Proposed task names in `native` | Behavior to preserve |
    |---|---|---|
    | `build-android.sh`, `build-ios.sh` | `build-android`, `build-ios` | Build the declared targets. Honor `--with-todo` on Android. Verify the Apple archive slices and checksum. |
    | `generate-bindings.sh`, `sync-*.sh`, `swift_metadata.py` | `bindings:generate`, `bindings:sync-android`, `bindings:sync-ios` | Match generated sources and the existing check modes. Keep metadata operations inside their owning task. |
    | Todo preparation and test scripts | `todo:prepare-ios`, `todo:test-ios`, `todo:test-android` | Preserve the visible count checks and temporary device cleanup. |
    | `stage_release.py`, release preparation, signing, and verification | `release:prepare`, `release:verify` | Validate the source revision, candidate files, signatures, and digests. Keep preparation local. |
    | Release starter scripts and seed helper | `release:test-ios-starter`, `release:test-android-starter` | Preserve local candidate and published package resolution modes. |
    | Release publication scripts | `release:publish` | Resume the same candidate. Preserve draft release, Maven receipt, validation, and Swift tag semantics. |
    
    Use staging directories for incomplete local artifacts. Promote only complete outputs.
    Honor the existing clean-checkout and source revision checks for release preparation.
    A publish task checks configuration, signatures, digests, source revision, and existing tags before remote writes.
    Keep the release timeout and poll interval configurable. Preserve the existing defaults of 1,800 seconds and 15 seconds.
    A retry must match the candidate and the remote receipt. Reject conflicting digests or tag revisions.
    After an ambiguous upload response, reconcile remote state before another upload. Report unresolved state for operator inspection.
    Serialize publication for a given release version through the existing release workflow and a local candidate lock where appropriate.
    Run publication tests against a fake registry. Reserve real publication for the existing release entry point and its credentials.
    A help command, a list command, and a verification task can never trigger publication.
    
    ## Acceptance and verification
    
    | Given | When | Then |
    cargo test -p foundation_tasks --profile uat
    cargo test -p foundation_macros --profile uat
    cargo test -p foundation_ui_native --features tasks --profile uat
    cargo test -p ewe_platform --profile uat
    cargo run -p ewe_platform -- task ls
    cargo run -p ewe_platform --bin platform -- task run native:build-android --help
    cargo run -p ewe_platform --bin ewe_platform -- generate --help
    ```

    - [ ] Implement directory discovery and verify incremental builds, diagnostics, and platform execution.
    - [ ] Port native UI tasks, verify release parity, and inventory the remaining repository migrations with owners.

        The owner requests complete migration. This revised plan awaits approval.
        A registered Rust task owns each build and deployment operation from validation through cleanup.
        A task can invoke native tools or use a native shell where the platform requires one.
        Starting a repository script from a task still leaves the operation outside the task.
        Move that logic into the owning task and remove the obsolete script.
        Keep workflow triggers, permissions, scheduling, and secret bindings in workflow configuration.
        
        ```mermaid
        flowchart LR
            D[Developer] --> T[Registered task]
            W[Workflow job] --> T
            T --> P[Task process backend]
            P --> N[Native tool or shell]
            T --> R[Result and artifacts]
        ```

    use foundation_tasks::{TaskContext, TaskError, TaskSet};
    
    use crate::BoxedError;
    
    type DirectHandler = fn(TaskContext, &ArgMatches) -> Result<(), BoxedError>;
    type GroupHandler = fn(&str, &ArgMatches) -> Result<(), BoxedError>;
    
    pub fn set() -> Result<TaskSet, TaskError> {
        let mut set = TaskSet::new("ewe_platform");
        let commands: [(&str, &str, fn(Command) -> Command, DirectHandler); 4] = [
            (
                "generate",
                "generate",
                crate::generate::register,
                |_, args| crate::generate::run(args),
            ),
            ("local", "local", crate::local::register, |ctx, args| {
                crate::local::run(args, ctx.context())
            }),
            (
                "tcp-capture",
                "tcp_capture",
                crate::tcp_capture::register,
                |_, args| crate::tcp_capture::run(args),
            ),
            (
                "gen-model-descriptors",
                "gen_model_descriptors",
                crate::models::register,
                |ctx, args| crate::models::run(args, ctx.context()),
            ),
        ];
        for (name, path, command, handler) in commands {
            let root = command(Command::new("platform"));
            let definition = root
                .find_subcommand(path)
                .expect("platform command registered")
                .clone();
            add(&mut set, name, &[path], definition, handler)?;
        }
        Ok(set)
    }

        use foundation_wasm_ui::cli;
        group(

    }
    
    fn group(
        owner: &'static str,
        namespace: &'static str,
        command: Command,
        path: &'static str,
        leaves: &[(&'static str, &'static str)],
        handler: GroupHandler,
    ) -> Result<TaskSet, TaskError> {
        let mut set = TaskSet::new(owner).with_namespace(namespace);
        set.describe_group(path, summary(&command));
        for &(name, leaf) in leaves {
            let definition = command
                .find_subcommand(leaf)
                .expect("package command registered")
                .clone();
            add(&mut set, name, &[path, leaf], definition, move |_, args| {
                handler(leaf, args)
            })?;
        }
        Ok(set)
    }
    
    fn summary(command: &Command) -> String {
        match command.get_about() {
            Some(text) => text.to_string(),
            None => "Run a platform command".to_owned(),
        }
    }

    # Linux, macOS and Windows. The macOS and Windows jobs are shards of several
    # packages each (`ci.py run-many`).
    #
    # On a pull request every package job also passes `--if-affected` to ci.py. The
    # runner then decides from the change and the dependency graph whether the
    # package must run, with the same rule as the plan job (`ci.py affected`).
    #
    # Each matrix sets `max-parallel` from ci/packages.toml ([defaults]
    # `max-parallel-*`), so jobs queue within the free GitHub plan and
    # do not stampede. GitHub allows 256 jobs per matrix; the workspace has about
    # 110 packages, so the full run fits in one matrix.
    
    # macOS and Windows tests run only on the full runs: a push to master or to
    # platform/release, a pull request into or from platform/release, the nightly
    # schedule and manual runs. Other pull requests run the Linux jobs only.
    on:
      pull_request:
        branches:
          - master
          - platform/release
      push:
        branches:
          - master
          - platform/release
      schedule:
        - cron: "17 2 * * *" # nightly full run, catches drift from dependencies
      workflow_dispatch:
        inputs:
          packages:
            description: "Packages to test: comma/space separated names, or 'all'"
            required: false
            default: "all"
    
    # A new push to a pull request cancels the old run of that pull request. Runs on
    # master, the nightly schedule and manual runs queue and never cancel each other.
    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    
    permissions:
      contents: read
    
    env:
      CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
      # Smaller target dirs and caches: no incremental state, no debuginfo.
      CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
      CARGO_PROFILE_UAT_DEBUG: "0"
      # `uat` is `dev` on LLVM — what the test docs use. (Locally, mise's env puts
      # `dev` on Cranelift, which CI does not install and which can't do
      # catch_unwind.)
      CI_PROFILE: uat
      # The pull request base commit. `ci.py run --if-affected` diffs against it, so
      # a package job skips itself when the change does not affect the package. It
      # is empty on master, nightly and manual runs, which test everything.
      CI_BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
    
    jobs:
      image:
        name: CI image
        uses: ./.github/workflows/platform-images.yaml
        with:
          config: ci/ewe-platform-image/config.toml
        secrets:
          registry-password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_EWESTUDIO_TOKEN }}
    
      plan:
        name: Plan
        # Only reads `cargo metadata`, so it runs on the runner, in parallel with
        # the image job.
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        outputs:
          matrix: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.matrix }}
          count: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.count }}
          # Every selected package that is not opted out of macOS in ci/packages.toml.
          macos-matrix: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.macos-matrix }}
          macos-count: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.macos-count }}
          macos-shard-count: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.macos-shard-count }}
          # Every selected package that is not opted out of Windows.
          windows-matrix: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.windows-matrix }}
          windows-count: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.windows-count }}
          windows-shard-count: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.windows-shard-count }}
          # Most jobs of one matrix that run at once (ci/packages.toml [defaults]).
          max-parallel-linux: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.max-parallel-linux }}
          max-parallel-macos: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.max-parallel-macos }}
          max-parallel-windows: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.max-parallel-windows }}
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    # Run the full CI pipeline (fmt, build, clippy, test, wasm) inside the Linux CI
    # image. Mounts the repository read-write so the image sees the latest code, and
    # drives the same `scripts/ci/ci.py` that GitHub Actions runs per package.
    #
    # Usage:
    #   scripts/ci/linux.sh <package>     one package (as CI runs it)
    #   PACKAGE=<package> scripts/ci/linux.sh
    #   scripts/ci/linux.sh               every package (like a full CI run)
    #
    # Env overrides:
    #   CI_IMAGE        image to run (default: ewestudios/ewe-platform-ci:latest)
    #   CI_PLATFORM     container platform (default: linux/amd64, matching CI)
    #   CI_TARGET_VOLUME cargo target volume (default: ewe-cargo-amd64 for amd64,
    #                    ewe-cargo otherwise) — keeps builds incremental across runs
    
    set -euo pipefail
    
    ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
    PACKAGE="${1:-${PACKAGE:-all}}"
    IMAGE="${CI_IMAGE:-ewestudios/ewe-platform-ci:latest}"
    PLATFORM="${CI_PLATFORM:-linux/amd64}"
    
    # Pick a target volume that matches the platform, so arm64 and amd64 artifacts
    # never share a cache (a mismatch aborts with "exec format error").
    if [[ -n "${CI_TARGET_VOLUME:-}" ]]; then
      TARGET_VOLUME="$CI_TARGET_VOLUME"
    elif [[ "$PLATFORM" == *amd64* ]]; then
      TARGET_VOLUME="ewe-cargo-amd64"
    else
      TARGET_VOLUME="ewe-cargo"
    fi
    
    # In a git worktree, `${ROOT}/.git` is a file that points at the main
    # repository's git directory, which lies outside the mount. Mount that
    # directory read-only at the same path, so the container can resolve it
    # (issue #590). A normal checkout keeps its git directory at `${ROOT}/.git`,
    # which the read-write mount already covers.
    EXTRA_MOUNTS=()
    GIT_COMMON_DIR="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [[ -n "$GIT_COMMON_DIR" && "$GIT_COMMON_DIR" != ".git" ]]; then
      GIT_COMMON_DIR="$(cd "$ROOT" && cd "$GIT_COMMON_DIR" && pwd)"
      EXTRA_MOUNTS=(-v "${GIT_COMMON_DIR}:${GIT_COMMON_DIR}:ro")
    fi
    
    docker run --rm --platform "$PLATFORM" \
      -v "${ROOT}:/w" -w /w \
      -v "${TARGET_VOLUME}:/target" \
      ${EXTRA_MOUNTS[@]+"${EXTRA_MOUNTS[@]}"} \
      -e CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/target \
      -e PACKAGE="$PACKAGE" \
      "$IMAGE" \
      bash -c '
        set -euo pipefail
        nu ci/platform-images/scripts/link-submodules.nu
        if [[ "$PACKAGE" == "all" ]]; then
          names=$(python3 scripts/ci/ci.py plan --packages all 2>/dev/null \
            | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(\" \".join(x[\"package\"] for x in d[\"include\"]))")
          failed=0
          for p in $names; do
            echo ""
            echo "=========== $p ==========="
            if ! python3 scripts/ci/ci.py run "$p" --profile uat; then
              echo "FAILED: $p"
              failed=1
            fi
          done
          exit $failed
        else
          python3 scripts/ci/ci.py run "$PACKAGE" --profile uat
        fi
      '
            return False
        print(f"{name}: not affected by {base}..{head}, skipping")
        return True
    
    
    def cmd_run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
        if args.if_affected and not_affected(args.package, args.base, args.head):
            return 0
        return run_package(args.package, args.step or list(STEPS), args.profile)
    
    
    def cmd_run_many(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
        return run_many(
            args.packages, args.step or list(STEPS), args.profile, args.if_affected, args.base, args.head
        )
    
    
    def main() -> int:
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
        sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    
        sub.add_parser("list", help="show every package and its CI settings").set_defaults(func=cmd_list)
    
        plan = sub.add_parser("plan", help="emit the GitHub Actions matrix")
        plan.add_argument("--packages", help="comma/space separated package names, or 'all'")
        plan.add_argument("--base", help="base commit for change detection (pull requests)")
        plan.add_argument("--head", help="head commit for change detection")
        plan.set_defaults(func=cmd_plan)
    
        aff = sub.add_parser("affected", help="list the packages a change affects, and why")
        aff.add_argument("--base", help="base ref (default: $CI_BASE_SHA, origin/$GITHUB_BASE_REF, or the merge base with origin/master)")
        aff.add_argument("--head", help="head ref (default: HEAD, plus uncommitted changes)")
        aff.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="print JSON")
        aff.set_defaults(func=cmd_affected)
    
        run = sub.add_parser("run", help="run fmt / clippy / tests for one package")
        run.add_argument("package")
        run.add_argument("--step", action="append", choices=STEPS, help="repeatable; default: all steps")
        run.add_argument("--profile", default=os.environ.get("CI_PROFILE", "uat"))
        run.add_argument(
            "--if-affected",
            action="store_true",
            help="skip the package, with exit 0, when the change since the base does not affect it",
        )
        run.add_argument("--base", help="base ref for --if-affected (default: see `affected`)")
        run.add_argument("--head", help="head ref for --if-affected (default: HEAD)")
        run.set_defaults(func=cmd_run)
    
        many = sub.add_parser("run-many", help="run several packages in turn, with one target directory")
        many.add_argument("packages", nargs="+", help="package names, or one space separated string")
        many.add_argument("--step", action="append", choices=STEPS, help="repeatable; default: all steps")
        many.add_argument("--profile", default=os.environ.get("CI_PROFILE", "uat"))
        many.add_argument("--if-affected", action="store_true", help="skip each package the change does not affect")
        many.add_argument("--base", help="base ref for --if-affected")
        many.add_argument("--head", help="head ref for --if-affected")
        many.set_defaults(func=cmd_run_many)
    
        # Cargo output and package names can hold non-ASCII text. The Windows
        # console code page cannot print it, so write UTF-8 on every host.
        for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
            if hasattr(stream, "reconfigure"):
                stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    
        args = parser.parse_args()
        if getattr(args, "command", None) == "run-many":
            # The shard matrix passes the names as one string.
            args.packages = [n for item in args.packages for n in item.replace(",", " ").split()]
        return args.func(args)
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        sys.exit(main())

    fn group(
        owner: &'static str,
        namespace: &'static str,
        command: Command,
        path: &'static str,
        leaves: &[(&'static str, &'static str)],
        handler: GroupHandler,
    ) -> Result<TaskSet, TaskError> {
        let mut set = TaskSet::new(owner).with_namespace(namespace);
        set.describe_group(path, summary(&command));
        for &(name, leaf) in leaves {
            let definition = command
                .find_subcommand(leaf)
                .expect("package command registered")
                .clone();
            add(&mut set, name, &[path, leaf], definition, move |_, args| {
                handler(leaf, args)
            })?;
        }
        Ok(set)
    }
    
    fn summary(command: &Command) -> String {
        match command.get_about() {
            Some(text) => text.to_string(),
            None => "Run a platform command".to_owned(),
        }
    }
    
    fn add(
        set: &mut TaskSet,
        name: &'static str,
        direct: &[&'static str],
        command: Command,
        handler: impl Fn(TaskContext, &ArgMatches) -> Result<(), BoxedError> + Send + Sync + 'static,
    ) -> Result<(), TaskError> {
        let handler = std::sync::Arc::new(handler);
        set.add_command(name, summary(&command), command, move |ctx, args| {
            let handler = handler.clone();
            async move {
                blocking::unblock(move || handler(ctx, &args))
                    .await
                    .map_err(TaskError::operation)
            }
        })?;
        set.expose(name, direct)
    }

    //! WHY: `js = "single-file"` apps want ONE file to ship — the WASM bytes ride
    //! inside the JS, no second network round trip (feature 10 §5).
    //!
    //! WHAT: [`bundle_single_file`] — replaces the wrapper's `__EWE_WASM_LOAD__`
    //! fetch block with embedded bytes, either a `Uint8Array` literal (default,
    //! zero decode cost) or base64 + `atob` (smaller source text).
    //!
    //! HOW: Pure string substitution against the marker `js_wrapper` emits — the
    //! wrappers and the bundler agree on exactly one seam.
    
    // Hosted-prelude import: this module is target-gated (native-only) inside a no_std crate.
    #[allow(unused_imports)]
    use std::prelude::rust_2021::*;
    
    use super::js_wrapper::load_marker;
    use super::Encoding;
    
    /// Embed `wasm_bytes` into `wrapper_js`, removing the fetch path entirely.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn bundle_single_file(wrapper_js: &str, wasm_bytes: &[u8], encoding: Encoding) -> String {
        let load = match encoding {
            Encoding::Uint8Array => {
                let mut literal = String::with_capacity(wasm_bytes.len() * 4 + 64);
                literal.push_str("  const wasmBytes = new Uint8Array([");
                for (i, byte) in wasm_bytes.iter().enumerate() {
                    if i > 0 {
                        literal.push(',');
                    }
                    literal.push_str(itoa(*byte));
                }
                literal.push_str("]).buffer;");
                literal
            }
            Encoding::B64 => {
                let encoded = base64_encode(wasm_bytes);
                format!(
                    "  const wasmBytes = Uint8Array.from(atob('{encoded}'), (c) => c.charCodeAt(0)).buffer;"
                )
            }
        };
        wrapper_js.replace(load_marker(), &load)
    }
    
    /// Tiny u8 → decimal str (avoids one million format! calls for big binaries).
    fn itoa(byte: u8) -> &'static str {
        // 256-entry lookup built once.
        static TABLE: std::sync::OnceLock<Vec<String>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
        let table = TABLE.get_or_init(|| (0u16..256).map(|v| v.to_string()).collect());
        &table[byte as usize]
    }
    
    /// Standard base64 (no external dep — 20 lines beats a crate here).
    #[must_use]
    pub fn base64_encode(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
        const ALPHABET: &[u8; 64] = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/";
        let mut out = String::with_capacity(bytes.len().div_ceil(3) * 4);
        for chunk in bytes.chunks(3) {
            let b = [
                chunk[0],
                *chunk.get(1).unwrap_or(&0),
                *chunk.get(2).unwrap_or(&0),
            ];
            let n = (u32::from(b[0]) << 16) | (u32::from(b[1]) << 8) | u32::from(b[2]);
            out.push(ALPHABET[(n >> 18) as usize & 63] as char);
            out.push(ALPHABET[(n >> 12) as usize & 63] as char);
            out.push(if chunk.len() > 1 {
                ALPHABET[(n >> 6) as usize & 63] as char
            } else {
                '='
            });
            out.push(if chunk.len() > 2 {
                ALPHABET[n as usize & 63] as char
            } else {
                '='
            });
        }
        out
    }
    }
    
    fn run_plan(args: &ArgMatches) -> Result<(), BoxedError> {
        let generator = generator(args)?;
        println!(
            "Discovered {} entrypoint(s):",
            generator.entrypoints().len()
        );
        for ep in generator.entrypoints() {
            println!("  {} ({:?}, {:?})", ep.name, ep.mode, ep.packaging);
        }
        println!();
        println!("Would generate:");
        for file in generator.plan() {
            println!("  {} ({})", file.path.display(), file.kind);
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    
    fn run_build(args: &ArgMatches) -> Result<(), BoxedError> {
        let generator = generator(args)?;
        let release = args.get_flag("release");
        let skip_runtimes = args.get_flag("skip_runtimes");
        let verbose = args.get_flag("verbose");
    
        if verbose {
            tracing::info!(
                "building {} entrypoint(s), release={release}, skip_runtimes={skip_runtimes}",
                generator.entrypoints().len()
            );
        }
        let written = generator.execute(release, skip_runtimes, &runtime_assets())?;
        for file in &written {
            tracing::info!("wrote {} ({})", file.path.display(), file.kind);
        }
        tracing::info!("done — {} file(s)", written.len());
        Ok(())
    }
    
    /// The owned runtime assets, resolved relative to the workspace layout.
    fn runtime_assets() -> Vec<(&'static str, &'static Path)> {
        let mut assets = vec![(
            "foundation-wasm.js",
            Path::new("backends/foundation_wasm/runtime/foundation-wasm.js"),
        )];
        macro_rules! browser_assets {
            ($($name:literal),+ $(,)?) => {
                $(assets.push(($name, Path::new(concat!("backends/foundation_wasm_ui/runtimes/", $name))));)+
            };
        }
        browser_assets!(
            "foundation-wasm-ui.js",
            "foundation-ui-frames.js",
            "foundation-ui-live.js",
            "foundation-ui-recovery.js",
            "foundation-ui-connections.js",
            "foundation-ui-vocab.js",
            "foundation-ui-wire.js",
            "foundation-ui-behaviours.js",
            "foundation-ui-bootstrap.js",
            "foundation-ui-actions.js",
            "platform-scheme-interceptor.js",
        );
        assets.push((
            "bundle.js",
            Path::new("backends/foundation_wasm_ui/runtimes/foundation-ui-runtime.js"),
        ));
        assets
    }
    {
      "type": "module"
    }

    pub fn run(args: &ArgMatches) -> Result<(), BoxedError> {
