    use std::fmt::Write;
    use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
    
    pub struct AppDistribution {
        pub name: String,
        pub crate_dir: PathBuf,
        pub route_prefix: String,
    }
    
    /// Scan the project for WASM app crates and generate platform glue code.
    ///
    /// # Panics
    ///
    /// Panics if `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` is not set.
    pub fn generate_platform_code() {
        let manifest_dir = PathBuf::from(std::env::var("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR").unwrap());
        let project_root = manifest_dir.parent().unwrap().to_path_buf();
    
        println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=src/");
        println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=build.rs");
    
        let mut apps = Vec::new();
        let app_dir = project_root.join("app");
        if app_dir.join("Cargo.toml").exists() {
            apps.push(AppDistribution {
                name: "app".into(),
                crate_dir: app_dir,
                route_prefix: "/app/".into(),
            });
        }
        if let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(&project_root) {
            for e in entries.filter_map(std::result::Result::ok) {
                let p = e.path();
                let n = p
                    .file_name()
                    .and_then(|n| n.to_str())
                    .unwrap_or("")
                    .to_string();
                if n.starts_with("app-") && p.is_dir() && p.join("Cargo.toml").exists() {
                    // Skip wasmtime shell crates (app-shell, app-shell-*) — handled separately
                    if n.starts_with("app-shell") {
                        continue;
                    }
                    apps.push(AppDistribution {
                        name: n.clone(),
                        crate_dir: p,
                        route_prefix: format!("/{n}/"),
                    });
                }
            }
        }
    
        if !apps.is_empty() {
            let public_dir = manifest_dir.join("public");
            build_all_wasm_apps(&apps, &public_dir);
            let generated_dir = manifest_dir.join("src").join("generated");
            std::fs::create_dir_all(&generated_dir).ok();
            generate_app_modules(&apps, &generated_dir);
        }
    
        // F33: Discover wasmtime shell apps (surface 3 — in-process WASM).
        // Only generates modules if foundation_wasmtime is in Cargo.toml deps.
        let has_wasmtime_dep = std::fs::read_to_string(manifest_dir.join("Cargo.toml"))
            .is_ok_and(|c| c.contains("foundation_wasmtime"));
        let mut shells: Vec<AppDistribution> = Vec::new();
        if has_wasmtime_dep {
            let shell_dir = project_root.join("app-shell");
            if shell_dir.join("Cargo.toml").exists() {
                shells.push(AppDistribution {
                    name: "app_shell".into(),
                    crate_dir: shell_dir,
                    route_prefix: "/shell/".into(),
                });
            }
            if let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(&project_root) {
                for e in entries.filter_map(std::result::Result::ok) {
                    let p = e.path();
                    let n = p
                        .file_name()
                        .and_then(|n| n.to_str())
                        .unwrap_or("")
                        .to_string();
                    if n.starts_with("app-shell-") && p.is_dir() && p.join("Cargo.toml").exists() {
                        shells.push(AppDistribution {
                            name: n.replace('-', "_"),
                            crate_dir: p,
                            route_prefix: format!("/{n}/"),
                        });
                    }
                }
            }
            if !shells.is_empty() {
                let shell_out = manifest_dir.join("shell_wasm");
                std::fs::create_dir_all(&shell_out).ok();
                for s in &shells {
                    build_wasmtime_app(&s.crate_dir, &shell_out);
                }
                let generated_dir = manifest_dir.join("src").join("generated");
                generate_wasmtime_modules(&shells, &generated_dir);
            }
        }
    
        // Patch tauri.conf.json BEFORE tauri_build reads it.
        // Sets the initial window URL to bypass WebViewAssetLoader.
        if let Some(first) = apps.first() {
            patch_tauri_conf_for_ewe(&manifest_dir, &first.route_prefix);
        } else {
            patch_tauri_conf_for_ewe(&manifest_dir, "/__platform__/");
        }
    
        tauri_build::build();
    }
    
    /// Build all discovered WASM app bundles.
    ///
    /// # Panics
    ///
    /// Panics if a WASM app build fails.
    pub fn build_all_wasm_apps(apps: &[AppDistribution], public_dir: &Path) {
        for app in apps {
            build_wasm_app(&app.crate_dir, &public_dir.join(&app.name));
        }
    }
    
    /// Build a single WASM app for wasmtime (Surface 3 — in-process WASM runtime).
    ///
    /// Scans for `#[wasm_app]` annotations, compiles the crate to `wasm32-wasip1`,
    /// and copies the `.wasm` binary to the output directory. Unlike
    /// `build_wasm_app` (which targets wasm32-unknown-unknown for the `WebView`),
    /// this targets wasip1 so the module runs in wasmtime with WASI support.
    ///
    /// # Panics
    ///
    /// Panics if `cargo build` fails or the output directory can't be created.
    pub fn build_wasmtime_app(app_dir: &Path, out_dir: &Path) {
        let apps: Vec<_> = scan_for_annotations(&app_dir.join("src"))
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|a| matches!(a.kind, AnnotationKind::WasmApp))
            .collect();
        if apps.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
    
        println!("cargo:warning=Building wasmtime app: {}", app_dir.display());
    
        let status = std::process::Command::new("cargo")
            .args(["build", "--target", "wasm32-wasip1", "--release"])
            .current_dir(app_dir)
            .status()
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| {
                panic!(
                    "cargo build failed for wasmtime app {}: {e}",
                    app_dir.display()
                )
            });
    
        if !status.success() {
            println!("cargo:warning=wasmtime app build failed (exit {status})");
            return;
        }
    
        let name = app_dir
            .file_name()
            .and_then(|n| n.to_str())
            .unwrap_or("wasm_app");
        let wasm_src = app_dir
            .join("target/wasm32-wasip1/release")
            .join(format!("{name}.wasm"));
        if wasm_src.exists() {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(out_dir).ok();
            let wasm_dst = out_dir.join(format!("{name}.wasm"));
            std::fs::copy(&wasm_src, &wasm_dst)
                .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("failed to copy wasmtime app to output: {e}"));
            println!(
                "cargo:warning=wasmtime app copied to {}",
                wasm_dst.display()
            );
        }
    }
    
    /// Build a single WASM app from its crate directory.
    ///
    /// # Panics
    ///
    /// Panics if the WASM build pipeline fails.
    pub fn build_wasm_app(app_dir: &Path, out_dir: &Path) {
        use foundation_wasm_ui::build_tools::WasmBundleGenerator;
    
        let wasm: Vec<_> = scan_for_annotations(&app_dir.join("src"))
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|a| {
                matches!(
                    a.kind,
                    AnnotationKind::WasmBin | AnnotationKind::WasmWorker | AnnotationKind::WasmService
                )
            })
            .collect();
        if wasm.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
    
        let pairs: Vec<(&str, &str)> = wasm
            .iter()
            .map(|a| (mode_str(a.kind), a.name.as_str()))
            .collect();
        let gen = match WasmBundleGenerator::from_annotations(app_dir, out_dir, &pairs, true) {
            Ok(g) => g,
            Err(e) => {
                println!("cargo:warning=WasmBundleGenerator: {e}");
                return;
            }
        };
    
        let repo_root = app_dir
            .parent()
            .unwrap()
            .parent()
            .unwrap()
            .parent()
            .unwrap();
        let wasm_js = repo_root.join("backends/foundation_wasm/runtime/foundation-wasm.js");
        let wasm_ui_js = repo_root.join("backends/foundation_wasm_ui/runtimes/foundation-wasm-ui.js");
        let interceptor =
            repo_root.join("backends/foundation_wasm_ui/runtimes/platform-scheme-interceptor.js");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(out_dir).ok();
        let _ = gen.execute(
            false,
            false,
            &[
                ("foundation-wasm.js", wasm_js.as_path()),
                ("foundation-wasm-ui.js", wasm_ui_js.as_path()),
                ("platform-scheme-interceptor.js", interceptor.as_path()),
            ],
        );
    }
    
    /// Generate per-app Rust module files inside `generated/`.
    ///
    /// Generates a `MobileDirectory`-derived struct with a `root: PathBuf` field.
    /// At runtime, `AppAssets::build(root)` receives the resolved resource directory
    /// from `PlatformSession`, enabling disk-backed asset serving for desktop dev
    /// and OTA updates without recompilation (F22).
    ///
    /// # Panics
    ///
    /// Panics if file I/O fails.
    fn generate_app_modules(apps: &[AppDistribution], generated_dir: &Path) {
        let mut mod_lines = String::from("// Auto-generated\n\n");
        for app in apps {
            let module_name = app.name.replace('-', "_");
            let content = format!(
                "// Generated \u{2014} AppAssets for \"{name}\" (F22)\n\
                 // Route prefix: {route_prefix}\n\
                 //\n\
                 // MobileDirectory: assets served from disk at runtime via `build(root)`.\n\
                 // The resolved resource dir comes from `PlatformSession.resource_root`.\n\
                 // On Android this is the Tauri-extracted resource path; on desktop\n\
                 // it is the app bundle resource dir.\n\n\
                 use foundation_macros::MobileDirectory;\n\
                 use foundation_platform::MobileApp;\n\
                 use std::path::PathBuf;\n\n\
                 #[derive(MobileDirectory)]\n\
                 #[source = \"$CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/public/{public_subdir}\"]\n\
                 pub struct AppAssets {{\n    pub root: PathBuf\n}}\n\n\
                 impl AppAssets {{\n\
                 \x20   pub fn build(root: PathBuf) -> MobileApp<AppAssets> {{ MobileApp::new(AppAssets {{ root }}) }}\n\
                 }}\n",
                name = app.name, route_prefix = app.route_prefix, public_subdir = app.name,
            );
            std::fs::write(generated_dir.join(format!("{module_name}.rs")), &content).ok();
            let _ = writeln!(mod_lines, "pub mod {module_name};");
        }
        std::fs::write(generated_dir.join("mod.rs"), &mod_lines).ok();
        println!("cargo:warning=generated {} app modules", apps.len());
    }
    
    /// Generate per-app Rust modules for wasmtime shell apps (F33).
    ///
    /// Produces `src/generated/shell/{name}.rs` with a `fn builder() -> WasmtimeBuilder`
    /// that uses `include_bytes!` to embed the compiled `.wasm` binary.
    fn generate_wasmtime_modules(apps: &[AppDistribution], generated_dir: &Path) {
        let shell_dir = generated_dir.join("shell");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&shell_dir).ok();
    
        let mut mod_lines = String::from("// Auto-generated (F33 — wasmtime shell)\n\n");
    
        for app in apps {
            let module_name = app.name.replace('-', "_");
            // Use the crate name directly for the wasm file lookup.
            let wasm_name = app
                .crate_dir
                .file_name()
                .and_then(|n| n.to_str())
                .unwrap_or(&app.name);
            let content = format!(
                "// Generated — wasmtime shell for \"{name}\" (F33, Surface 3)\n\
                 // Route prefix: {route_prefix}\n\
                 //\n\
                 // The compiled WASM binary lives in shell_wasm/{wasm_name}.wasm.\n\
                 // Loads via include_bytes! and wraps in a WasmtimeBuilder.\n\n\
                 use foundation_wasmtime::WasmtimeBuilder;\n\n\
                 #[must_use]\n\
                 pub fn builder() -> WasmtimeBuilder {{\n\
                 \x20   let wasm_bytes: &[u8] = include_bytes!(concat!(\n\
                 \x20       env!(\"CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR\"),\n\
                 \x20       \"/shell_wasm/{wasm_name}.wasm\"\n\
                 \x20   ));\n\
                 \x20   WasmtimeBuilder::new(wasm_bytes).with_name(\"{name}\")\n\
                 }}\n",
                name = app.name,
                route_prefix = app.route_prefix,
                wasm_name = wasm_name,
            );
            std::fs::write(shell_dir.join(format!("{module_name}.rs")), &content).ok();
            let _ = writeln!(mod_lines, "pub mod {module_name};");
        }
        std::fs::write(shell_dir.join("mod.rs"), &mod_lines).ok();
    
        // Declare `shell` in the parent `generated/mod.rs`. `generate_app_modules`
        // writes that file first and only knows about the WebView apps, so without
        // this append the whole `shell/` tree is unreachable — the F33 wasmtime
        // modules would be generated but never compiled in.
        let parent_mod = generated_dir.join("mod.rs");
        let existing = std::fs::read_to_string(&parent_mod).unwrap_or_default();
        if !existing.contains("pub mod shell;") {
            let updated = format!("{existing}pub mod shell;\n");
            std::fs::write(&parent_mod, updated).ok();
        }
    
        println!(
            "cargo:warning=generated {} wasmtime shell modules",
            apps.len()
        );
    }
    
    fn patch_tauri_conf_for_ewe(manifest_dir: &Path, route_prefix: &str) {
        let conf_path = manifest_dir.join("tauri.conf.json");
        if let Ok(content) = std::fs::read_to_string(&conf_path) {
            // Parse the JSON, add url to the first window, write back
            if let Ok(mut val) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&content) {
                let target_url = format!("ewe://localhost{route_prefix}");
                if let Some(windows) = val
                    .get_mut("app")
                    .and_then(|a| a.get_mut("windows"))
                    .and_then(|w| w.as_array_mut())
                    .and_then(|arr| arr.first_mut())
                {
                    windows["url"] = serde_json::Value::String(target_url);
                    if let Ok(patched) = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&val) {
                        if patched != content {
                            std::fs::write(&conf_path, &patched).ok();
                            println!("cargo:warning=patched tauri.conf.json url");
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    pub struct Annotation {
        pub name: String,
        pub kind: AnnotationKind,
        pub file: PathBuf,
        pub target: String,
    }
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub enum AnnotationKind {
        WasmBin,
        WasmWorker,
        WasmService,
        PlatformBin,
        /// Surface 3: WASM compiled to wasm32-wasip1, hosted in wasmtime.
        WasmApp,
    }
    fn mode_str(k: AnnotationKind) -> &'static str {
        match k {
            AnnotationKind::WasmBin => "wasm_bin",
            AnnotationKind::WasmWorker => "wasm_worker",
            AnnotationKind::WasmService => "wasm_service",
            AnnotationKind::PlatformBin => "platform_bin",
            AnnotationKind::WasmApp => "wasm_app",
        }
    }
    
    #[must_use]
    pub fn scan_for_annotations(dir: &Path) -> Vec<Annotation> {
        let mut v = Vec::new();
        let Ok(es) = std::fs::read_dir(dir) else {
            return v;
        };
        for e in es.filter_map(std::result::Result::ok) {
            let p = e.path();
            if p.is_dir()
                && p.file_name()
                    .is_some_and(|n| n != "target" && !n.to_string_lossy().starts_with('.'))
            {
                v.extend(scan_for_annotations(&p));
            } else if p.extension().is_some_and(|x| x == "rs") {
                if let Ok(c) = std::fs::read_to_string(&p) {
                    let ls: Vec<&str> = c.lines().collect();
                    for i in 0..ls.len() {
                        let t = ls[i].trim();
                        let kind = if t.starts_with("#[wasm_bin") {
                            Some(AnnotationKind::WasmBin)
                        } else if t.starts_with("#[wasm_worker") {
                            Some(AnnotationKind::WasmWorker)
                        } else if t.starts_with("#[wasm_service") {
                            Some(AnnotationKind::WasmService)
                        } else if t.starts_with("#[platform_bin") {
                            Some(AnnotationKind::PlatformBin)
                        } else {
                            None
                        };
                        if let Some(k) = kind {
                            let name = (i..ls.len()).find_map(|j| {
                                ls[j].find("fn ").map(|p2| {
                                    ls[j][p2 + 3..]
                                        .split(|c: char| !c.is_alphanumeric() && c != '_')
                                        .find(|s| !s.is_empty())
                                        .unwrap_or("unknown")
                                        .to_string()
                                })
                            });
                            // Parse annotation target: #[wasm_bin(target = "wasip1", ...)]
                            let target = t
                                .find("target")
                                .and_then(|pos| t[pos + 6..].trim_start().strip_prefix('='))
                                .map(|rest| rest.trim().trim_matches('"').trim_matches('#'))
                                .map_or_else(
                                    || String::from("wasm32-unknown-unknown"),
                                    |s| {
                                        s.split(',')
                                            .next()
                                            .unwrap_or(s)
                                            .trim_matches('"')
                                            .to_string()
                                    },
                                );
                            if let Some(n) = name {
                                v.push(Annotation {
                                    name: n,
                                    kind: k,
                                    file: p.clone(),
                                    target,
                                });
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        v
    }

        foundation_platform::codegen::generate_platform_code();
    }

## Assistant

I added a proposed **`build:install-hook`** task to Specification 90. A package can use it to install its build capability into another Cargo package.

The platform demo illustrates the intended result. Its `build.rs` calls `foundation_platform::codegen::generate_platform_code()`. The installer would create that entry for a new package. If the package already has the call, running the installer again would leave both files untouched. [Demo build script](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe-resume-combined/examples/platform_demo/build.rs)

For an existing package, the task would preserve its build logic, honor a custom script path, and add the required Cargo build dependency. Each provider owns its generator and input tracking. The JavaScript bundler would use the same installer as the platform generator.

The existing bundler work continues. **Do you approve the installer design for implementation?** [Feature 2 plan](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe-resume-combined/specifications/90-foundation-tasks/features/02-install-build-hooks/feature.md)

    //! `foundation_platform` — cross-platform application layer for native,
    //! desktop, mobile and web apps.
    //!
    //! On Tauri hosts it wraps `tauri::Builder` with a session backbone, route policy engine,
    //! capability registry, cache manager, transport lanes, and `WebView` stack
    //! manager. The platform extends Tauri's lifecycle — it doesn't replace it.
    //!
    //! # Wasm engine gate
    //!
    //! The Wasm engine (wasmtime) compiles WebAssembly (Wasm) with a just-in-time (JIT)
    //! compiler. iOS, tvOS and watchOS refuse executable memory outside a signed code region,
    //! so wasmtime cannot work there. This crate enables the engine by default, and it keeps
    //! the engine out of those targets. An app that names `WasmtimeResponder`, `WasmtimeShell`,
    //! `wasmtime_app`, `PlatformSession::register_wasmtime` or
    //! `PlatformSession::wasmtime_shell` does not compile for them. To run Wasm on iOS, use an
    //! interpreter runtime such as `wasmi`.

    /// Build and launch a `foundation_platform` app.
    ///
    /// Wraps `PlatformBuilder::build()` with `tauri::generate_context!()` called
    /// internally. The user never touches Tauri directly.
    ///
    /// ```ignore
    /// platform_run!(PlatformBuilder::new()
    ///     .ctx(Ctx::host())
    ///     .route("/app/*", webview_app())
    ///     .setup(|session| { session.capabilities().register(MyCap); }));
    /// ```
    #[macro_export]
    macro_rules! platform_run {
        ($builder:expr) => {{
            let __builder: $crate::PlatformBuilder = $builder;
            __builder
                .build(::tauri::generate_context!())
                .expect("failed to build foundation_platform app")
                .run(|_handle, event| {
                    if let ::tauri::RunEvent::Exit = event {
                        std::process::exit(0);
                    }
                })
        }};
        ($builder:expr, |$handle:ident, $event:ident| $body:block) => {{
            let __builder: $crate::PlatformBuilder = $builder;
            __builder
                .build(::tauri::generate_context!())
                .expect("failed to build foundation_platform app")
                .run(|$handle, $event| $body)
        }};
    }

## Assistant

No. The reverse-dependency loop makes sense. It records which packages depend on each crate. The next block mixes repository-specific build rules into package discovery.

`examples` and `wasm-tests` need explicit definitions because Cargo cannot discover all their targets from the root workspace. The problem is `is_some_and`. If someone renames `answerme-agent`, the lookup silently returns `false`. The runner then plans the examples build without its required `llama.cpp` support. [Current implementation](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_ci/src/workspace.rs:75)

I recommend declaring each group’s directory, build recipe, and package members in `ci/packages.toml`. The runner can then derive tool requirements from those members and report an unknown package by name. The tasks agent recorded this change in Specification 90. Implementation awaits your approval. [Proposed design](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/specifications/90-foundation-tasks/migration.md:74)

    //! Procedural audio: a cozy jazz loop, a wind breeze, and gentle cues.
    //!
    //! Everything here is synthesized at runtime. There are no audio files and no
    //! decoder. The note, chord and scheduler data are plain Rust and run under
    //! `cargo test` on the host; the Web Audio graph is wasm-only and lives in the
    //! `web` module below.
    
    /// Beats per minute of the jazz loop. Children prefer a clear, moving pulse;
    /// this is relaxed but still has a beat to tap to.
    pub const BPM: f32 = 92.0;
    pub const BEAT: f32 = 60.0 / BPM;
    pub const BAR: f32 = BEAT * 4.0;
    pub const BARS: usize = 8;
    
    /// How far ahead the scheduler writes notes, in seconds.
    pub const LOOKAHEAD: f64 = 0.2;
    
    pub const MASTER: f32 = 0.9;
    pub const MUSIC: f32 = 0.16;
    pub const SFX: f32 = 0.55;
    pub const AMBIENCE: f32 = 0.09;
    
    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub enum Cue {
        Correct,
        Wrong,
        Intro,
        Tally,
        GameOver,
    }
    
    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
    pub struct Note {
        pub midi: u8,
        pub at: f32,
        pub duration: f32,
        pub gain: f32,
    }
    
    impl Cue {
        /// Cue notes are pure data so their shape can be tested without a browser.
        pub fn notes(self) -> &'static [Note] {
            match self {
                Cue::Correct => &[
                    Note { midi: 88, at: 0.00, duration: 0.30, gain: 0.50 }, // E6
                    Note { midi: 95, at: 0.09, duration: 0.35, gain: 0.42 }, // B6
                ],
                Cue::Wrong => &[
                    Note { midi: 67, at: 0.00, duration: 0.28, gain: 0.45 }, // G4
                    Note { midi: 64, at: 0.12, duration: 0.36, gain: 0.40 }, // E4
                ],
                Cue::Intro => &[
                    Note { midi: 72, at: 0.00, duration: 0.28, gain: 0.40 }, // C5
                    Note { midi: 76, at: 0.09, duration: 0.30, gain: 0.42 }, // E5
                    Note { midi: 79, at: 0.18, duration: 0.42, gain: 0.46 }, // G5
                ],
                Cue::Tally => &[
                    Note { midi: 72, at: 0.00, duration: 0.22, gain: 0.38 }, // C5
                    Note { midi: 76, at: 0.08, duration: 0.22, gain: 0.40 }, // E5
                    Note { midi: 79, at: 0.16, duration: 0.24, gain: 0.42 }, // G5
                    Note { midi: 83, at: 0.24, duration: 0.50, gain: 0.48 }, // B5
                ],
                Cue::GameOver => &[
                    Note { midi: 76, at: 0.00, duration: 0.30, gain: 0.42 }, // E5
                    Note { midi: 72, at: 0.14, duration: 0.32, gain: 0.40 }, // C5
                    Note { midi: 67, at: 0.28, duration: 0.52, gain: 0.44 }, // G4
                ],
            }
        }
    }
    
    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub enum Voice {
        Keys,
        Bass,
        Melody,
        Brush,
    }
    
    impl Voice {
        /// Peak amplitude of one note inside the music bus.
        #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
        fn level(self) -> f32 {
            match self {
                Voice::Keys => 0.10,
                Voice::Bass => 0.12,
                Voice::Melody => 0.08,
                Voice::Brush => 0.018,
            }
        }
    }
    
    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]

    pub fn midi_to_freq(midi: u8) -> f32 {
        440.0 * 2.0_f32.powf((midi as f32 - 69.0) / 12.0)
    }

    ## Stage 2. Use framework navigation and graphics
    
    - Add the game entry to browser, iOS, and Android todo screens, through the same shared page declaration.
    - Register separate todo and game views through the public framework. Use host actions to open and close the game. The game view owns the running game loop.
    - Use Feature 32 for view targeting. Keep remote todo updates scoped to the todo view while the game is open.
    - Use Feature 34 to draw through wgpu. Exercise Feature 35 with a host-owned device in an integration configuration.
    - Keep game input, simulation, and drawing local. A server-backed todo screen can open the same local game.
    - Let the host schedule drawing and map pointer or touch coordinates to game coordinates.
    - Reconfigure on resize and rotation. Pause simulation and sound when hidden. Resume without charging time spent away.
    - On close, release the surface, audio, and frame callbacks. Keep the todo host and its graphics device available.
    - If graphics initialization fails, show a recoverable error in the game view and keep the todo view usable.
    
    ## Stage 3. Verify the integrated application
    
    1. Run deterministic tests for both mini-games and the complete run lifecycle.
    2. On each platform, enter a todo, select a filter, open the game, play, and return.
    3. Verify the same todo state after returning. Deliver a live count update while the game view is active.
    4. Verify that game input and graphics updates reach only the game view. Verify that the todo receives its count update.
    5. Repeat open, close, resize, and background transitions. Check for duplicate input, stale callbacks, and resource leaks.
    6. Verify an input hit and a known rendered scene on real graphics backends. Record hardware and simulator coverage separately.
    7. Capture the game and the return to Todos on web, iOS, and Android. Compare key scenes against the reference.
    8. Update the todo README with launch commands, controls, navigation, and graphics ownership for each platform.

    # Agent Configuration
    
    ## ⚡ Fast Rust Check Workflow
    
    **CRITICAL:** When doing Rust checks and you're not sure about something, use quick `cargo check` with `tee` to collect warnings rapidly. **5-6 minutes should be enough** for the initial pass. If after 5-6 minutes you see nothing, increase to 10 minutes on the next run. If it finishes with no issues — great. If you see issues early, collect enough in 5 minutes then go fix them. This increases iteration speed and reduces wasted wait time.
    
    ---
    
    ## Crate Hygiene: Check + Clippy Per Crate
    
    When you finish a crate, clear its warnings before you call the work done. You
    do the hard thinking; agents do the execution. Two phases:
    
    ### Phase 1 — Plan
    
    1. Spawn one fresh planner agent for the crate.
    2. The planner runs both commands from the workspace root:
       - `cargo check -p <crate> --profile uat`
       - `cargo clippy -p <crate> --profile uat --no-deps` (without `--no-deps`,
         clippy re-lints every workspace path-dependency and floods the log)
    3. The planner catalogues every warning and suggestion (file, line, message,
       lint name) and reasons about the right fix for each one. It sorts them into:
       - fix now (safe, mechanical, behaviour-preserving),

            /// Create the context and graph on the first gesture. Idempotent.
            pub fn unlock(&mut self) {
                if self.inner.is_some() {
                    return;
                }
                let Ok(inner) = Inner::build(self.seed, self.muted) else {
                    return;
                };
                let _ = inner.ctx.resume();
                self.inner = Some(inner);
            }
    
            /// Schedule the next lookahead window and drift the breeze. Call each
            /// animation frame.
            pub fn update(&mut self) {
                let Some(inner) = &mut self.inner else {
                    return;
                };
                let now = inner.ctx.current_time();
                inner.scheduler.resync(now);
                inner
                    .scheduler
                    .fill(now, now + LOOKAHEAD, self.seed, &mut inner.events);
                for index in 0..inner.events.len() {
                    let event = inner.events[index];
                    inner.play_event(event);
                }
                if now >= inner.next_breeze {
                    inner.drift_breeze(now);
                    inner.next_breeze = now + 8.0;
                }
            }
    
            pub fn cue(&mut self, cue: Cue) {
                let Some(inner) = &mut self.inner else {
                    return;
                };
                inner.play_cue(cue);
                inner.duck();
            }
    
            pub fn set_muted(&mut self, muted: bool) {
                self.muted = muted;

                };
                let target = if muted { 0.0 } else { MASTER };
                let now = inner.ctx.current_time();
                let gain = inner.master.gain();
                let current = gain.value();
                let _ = gain.cancel_scheduled_values(now);
                let _ = gain.set_value_at_time(current, now);
                let _ = gain.linear_ramp_to_value_at_time(target, now + if muted { 0.03 } else { 0.2 });
            }

    # Feature 32. Target views and elements by name
    
    The framework placement stages and count migration are complete. The Todo agent owns the remaining target migration under issue #714.
    
    ## Glossary
    
    A view is a content area that a host registers with a renderer.
    An identifier is a name that an author assigns with `id`.
    A target selects a view or an element for a rendering instruction.
    A frame carries instructions from a producer to a renderer.
    
    ## Framework contract
    
    Every application can use the same placement markup on web, iOS, and Android.
    Put target resolution in the framework. The todo example consumes the public contract.
    
    | Author intent | Target | Resolution |
    |---|---|---|
    | Render an initial page | Omitted | Fill the receiving view. |
    | Append content to a view | Omitted | Append to the receiving view. Preserve existing children. |
    | Select a registered view | `view#view-1` | Find the named view in this host. |
    | Select an element | `#open-count` | Find the name in the receiving view. |
    | Check the element type too | `sheet#editor` | Match the name and its declared sheet type. |
    
    A call or subscription carries its receiving view. Independent output can use the only registered view.
    If several views qualify, require an explicit view. Never guess from focus or registration order.
    Scope element lookup to that view. All shared element kinds support identifiers, including custom registered kinds.
    A qualified target checks the shared tag type. The platform widget name cannot change the result.
    Provide a common tag-name mapping. Accept `sheet` for the shared bottom sheet and document its canonical spelling.
    Reserve `view` for registered view roots.
    
    The author adds an identifier when another operation needs to address an element.
    Keep identifiers unique within one view. Different views can use the same element name.
    View names are unique within a host.
    Application code must never assign numeric anchors or send updates to hard-coded node handles.
    Use the receiving view or a named target for application updates.
    The framework may allocate numeric handles internally for node operations and event dispatch.
    Todo record identifiers identify records. They do not address rendering operations.
    
    ## Example
    
    ```rust
    // Initial content for the receiving view.
    let footer = html! { <Text id="open-count">0 open todos</Text> };
    
    // A later publication uses the same declaration on each platform.
    html_swap! {
        "#open-count", ctx, ctx.receiver(),
        <Text id="open-count">{count_label}</Text>
    }
    ```
    
    The replacement keeps the name so later publications can find it.
    
    ```mermaid
    flowchart LR
        P[Publisher] --> C[One live channel]
        C --> W[Browser view]
        C --> I[iOS view]
        C --> A[Android view]
    ```
    
    Each subscriber resolves the same named target inside its own view.
    
    ## Stage 1. Define the public syntax and wire contract
    
    - Support names in shared markup, initial rendering, and all targeted placement macros.
    - Add a target-free append form. Keep append and full-view replacement distinct.
    - Use the existing wire identifier selector for bare names. Encode a type check and view selection explicitly when required.
    - Specify name parsing, escaping, and malformed-input errors once. Use shared fixtures in every renderer.
    - Preserve existing wire field numbers. Regenerate affected bindings and document capability requirements.
    - Keep browser-specific selectors available through their existing path. Portable selectors must resolve identically on each platform.
    
    ## Stage 2. Implement placement in each framework renderer
    
    - Register view roots at host setup. Bind action replies and stream deliveries to the receiving view.
    - Index element names when mounting. Update the index on replacement, removal, and view disposal.
    - Apply this contract to append, swap, remove, insert before, and insert after.
    - For relative insertion, resolve the named child under the selected parent.
    - Validate names and targets before changing the displayed tree. Permit a replacement to reuse names from the outgoing subtree.
    - Report a missing target, duplicate name, wrong type, or ambiguous view. Preserve the affected view on failure.
    - Apply the same rules to direct rendering, action replies, and streamed updates.
    
    ## Stage 3. Use a single shared publication
    
    Publish shared instructions through one channel and one endpoint. All three renderers can apply the same portable frame.
    Keep each subscriber’s transport, cursor, and cancellation independent. Preserve replay after reconnect.
    Migrate the todo count to one named element and one publication on `/live`.
    Remove the example’s separate native count route and numeric count target.
    Keep shared selection and delivery logic in the framework. Example code supplies only the view and its business data.
    
    ## Stage 4. Use one endpoint for each screen
    
    | Route | Frame content | Callers |
    |---|---|---|
    | `GET /initial` | Full todo view with a dialog area and a live count subscription | Browser, iOS, and Android todo apps |
    | `GET /open-count` | Open count with a Refresh button bound to `refresh_count` | Browser, iOS, and Android starter clients |
    
    Build each screen once with shared controls and named targets. Both handlers return a frame.
    Use the same count subscription from the full view on each platform.
    Point every starter at the count screen. Declare its refresh action on the browser.
    Remove `/native-initial` and `/native-starter` from route registration, callers, tests, templates, and current setup guides.
    Keep action submission and live subscription endpoints available.
    Load both routes on all three platforms. Submit Refresh and verify that the displayed count matches the server.
    Check that an update after initial load reaches the correct count target on each platform.
    
    ## Acceptance checks
    
    1. Run common placement fixtures on web, Swift, and Kotlin. Check names on every shared element kind.
    2. Verify default append, initial replacement, named views, qualified targets, and every relative placement.
    3. Mount two views with identical child names. Deliver a reply to each. Check that its sibling stays unchanged.
    4. Reject duplicate names, wrong types, missing children, and ambiguous destinations before mutation.
    5. Replace a named subtree twice. Remove it, reuse its name, and verify cleanup when its view closes.
    6. Deliver one captured count frame unchanged to all three renderers. Verify the displayed count on each platform.
    7. Connect web and native subscribers to the same running endpoint. Publish once and verify independent resume.
    8. Update the framework and mobile package README files. Show default placement, explicit view selection, and a typed element target.

    ## Remaining Todo targets
    
    Issue #714 tracks the application targets added during the synchronization repair.
    The following revision supersedes the earlier full-page count publication. The separate count screen still demonstrates server rendering.
    
    ### Action ownership
    
    The server owns todo records. Each client keeps a local copy for display and search.
    Each action has one owner and one purpose.
    
    | Intent | Owner | Result |
    |---|---|---|
    | Open, cancel, or dismiss a dialog | Host | Update the named dialog area on this client. |
    | Submit a title or confirm deletion | Server | Validate the request and change the server store. |
    | Complete or reopen a todo | Server | Change the record and publish the resulting status. |
    | Search or filter | Host | Select matching cached records and update this client's list. |
    | Open or close Mathalley | Host | Start or release the game view described in Feature 36. |
    
    Build the initial page once. Give each addressed element a name in the shared markup.
    Use one dialog builder. Its inputs select the dialog kind and the affected todo record.
    Submitting a title records a pending row before sending the server action `add_todo`. Bind deletion confirmation to `confirm_delete`. Bind cancellation to `close_dialog`.
    Remove the duplicate device mutation handlers and their registrations.
    Remove the `local` argument and the `OnDevice` checks from page, row, dialog, filter, and mutation code.
    Update callers of the standalone mobile constructor. Its host actions use the cache. Record changes require a server connection.
    Declare any platform-specific action scope at its registration and binding boundary.
    Use the same shared page and controls on each supported host.
    
    ### Local cache and delivery
    
    The initial page request returns the shared page, its record snapshot, and the matching stream position.
    The host seeds its local store from that snapshot and retains outstanding submissions during recovery.
    One local rendering action owns the rows and the named open-count footer on the full Todo page.
    Keep the separate count screen as an example of a server action that renders a view.
    
    A server write returns a typed record change with its committed stream position.
    The server publishes that same change to subscribers.
    Both paths enter one local action that applies changes in stream order.
    Ignore a duplicate position. Request missing changes before advancing across a gap.
    Recover from an expired stream with a fresh snapshot and position.
    Match pending additions by record identifier. Keep local delivery status separate from confirmed records.
    Show pending and failed submissions from local state. Derive the open count from confirmed records in that same store.
    
    After applying a change, invoke the shared local rendering action for the affected named regions.
    Keep search input, focus, scroll position, and open dialogs during record updates.
    While search is active, keep its displayed rows fixed until the user changes or clears the query.

    117:## Stage 5. Verify the contract
    118-
    119-| Test | Expected result |
    120-|---|---|
    121-| Two default SSE mounts open `/live` | Each opens its own response. Removing either closes only that response. |
    122-| Two shared SSE mounts open `/live` concurrently | The first listener opens one response. Both receive new events. Final release closes it once. |
    123-| A listener joins an active shared SSE feed | The manager sends no resume request. Earlier listeners continue without interruption. |
    124-| Shared mounts use `/live` and `/live?before=42` | The manager opens two feeds. |
    125-| An action and a mount use the default WebSocket endpoint | Both use one socket. A different endpoint or an explicit dedicated mount gets a separate socket. |
    126-| One sender and two readers share a socket | Each release affects only its handle. Final release closes the default connection once. |
    127-| Rust requests keep-alive | The connection stays open with zero consumers. A later subscription reuses it. |
    128-| No listeners receive application data | The application decoder and screen store receive zero calls. |

    test("concurrent snapshots report the revision of their displayed count",{timeout:30000},async t => {
      const server = spawn(process.env.EWE_TODO_BIN ?? "target/uat/ui_todo",["127.0.0.1:0"]);
      t.after(() => server.kill());
      const [line] = await once(createInterface({input:server.stdout}),"line");
      const base = new URL(line.match(/http:\/\/\S+/)[0]);
      const registry = new JsActionRegistry();
      registry.declare("server","add_todo");
      const sender = new FetchActionTransport({url:new URL("/action",base),hello:() => actions.hello()});
      const actions = new WebActionManager({registry,server:sender,frames:{receive(){return true}},
        onError:error => assert.fail(JSON.stringify(error))});
      async function capture() {
        const res = await fetch(new URL("/initial",base),{headers:{"X-Ewe-Hello":base64urlEncode(actions.hello())}});
        const packet = wire.Frame.getRootAsFrame(new wire.ByteBuffer(await readViewResponse(res)));
        const place = packet.kind(new wire.FrameMessage()).messages(0).operation().ui(new wire.Place());
        let cursor, count;
        for (let i=0; i<place.operationsLength(); i++) {
          const op = place.operations(i);
          if (op.uiType() === wire.UiOperation.LiveMount) cursor = op.ui(new wire.LiveMount()).resumeFrom();
          if (op.uiType() === wire.UiOperation.SetText) {
            const label = op.ui(new wire.SetText()).text()?.match(/^(\d+) open todos?$/);
            if (label) count = BigInt(label[1]);
          }
        }
        assert.notEqual(cursor,undefined);
        assert.equal(count,cursor);
        return count;
      }
      const input = {value:"Revision",closest:() => null,getAttribute:() => null};
      assert.equal(await capture(),0n);
      await Promise.all([
        (async () => { for (let i=0;i<20;i++) await actions.trigger("server:add_todo",input,{type:"submit"}); })(),
        ...Array.from({length:3},async () => { for(let i=0;i<10;i++) await capture(); }),
      ]);
      assert.equal(await capture(),20n);
    });

    Swift or Kotlin implements the provider. Rust requests the handle once when it builds the screen.
    The native provider selects the account and endpoint for that service.
    
    For a ready action sender, adapt the native handle to the Rust action transport.
    For a Connect remote procedure call (RPC), request the native network client and build the Connect sender in Rust.
    Both paths end at the same builder method. This proposed example uses the adapters from [Feature 26](../26-connectrpc-transport/feature.md).
    
    ```rust
    let network = provider.http_client("todos").await?;
    let transport = Arc::new(PlatformHttpTransport::new(network));
    let client = ActionsClient::new(transport, base_url, options)?;
    let sender = Arc::new(ConnectActionTransport::new(client));
    let app = NetworkApp::builder(ctx, actions, caps, surface)
        .with_server_transport(sender)
        .build();
    ```

    [package]
    name = "foundation_signals"
    version = "0.0.7"
    edition.workspace = true
    rust-version.workspace = true
    license.workspace = true
    authors.workspace = true
    repository.workspace = true
    description = "Standalone reactive signal system: R3-style height-ordered graph, bucket-queue stabilize, version-based stale detection. No DOM, no WASM coupling."
    
    [dependencies]
    foundation_ui_traits = { path = "../foundation_ui_traits", version = "0.0.6" }
    # The reactive graph is `no_std + alloc`. These all turn `std` on by default,
    # so defaults are off here and `std` is forwarded from this crate's `std`.
    serde = { version = "1", default-features = false, features = ["alloc", "derive"] }
    serde_json = { version = "1.0.114", default-features = false, features = ["alloc"] }
    tracing = { version = "0.1", default-features = false }
    
    foundation_core = { path = "../foundation_core", version = "0.0.23", optional = true }
    foundation_context = { path = "../foundation_context", version = "0.0.4", optional = true }
    
    [features]
    default = ["std", "single_threaded"]
    # Select the original local runtime explicitly for existing callers.
    single_threaded = []
    # Native hosts can share a separate graph across worker threads.
    thread_safe = ["std"]
    # Links `std`. The reactive graph only needs `core + alloc`; `std` adds the
    # cross-thread `SignalHub` (mpsc channels, `Mutex`/`RwLock`; native only) and
    # forwards `std` to serde/serde_json/tracing. `no_std` consumers (the wasm UI
    # crates) use `default-features = false, features = ["single_threaded"]`.
    std = ["serde/std", "serde_json/std", "tracing/std"]
    # Feature 18: cross-thread signal access over the SignalHub actor (native
    # only — the hub module is cfg'd off wasm32). The hub and foundation_core
    # both need std.
    valtron = ["std", "dep:foundation_core", "dep:foundation_context"]
    
    [lints]
    workspace = true

    //! Check all published mobile project layouts through the command line.
    
    use std::{
        fs,
        path::Path,
        process::{Command, Output},
    };
    
    fn generate(root: &Path, platform: &str, name: &str, id: &str, host: Option<&str>) -> Output {
        let mut cli = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_ewe_platform"));
        cli.current_dir(root).args([
            "generate", "-t", platform, "-p", name, "-l", "plain", "--app-id", id,
        ]);
        if let Some(host) = host {
            cli.args(["--host", host]);
        }
        cli.output().unwrap()
    }
    
    #[test]
    fn mobile_projects_select_their_host_and_preserve_existing_files() {
        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("ewe-mobile-templates-{}", std::process::id()));
        fs::create_dir(&root).unwrap();
        for (platform, prefix) in [("ios-app", "Swift"), ("android-app", "Kotlin")] {
            for host in [None, Some("on-device")] {
                let local = host.is_some();
                let name = format!("{prefix}{}", if local { "Counter" } else { "Remote" });
                let id = format!("com.example.{}", name.to_lowercase());
                let out = generate(&root, platform, &name, &id, host);
                assert!(
                    out.status.success(),
                    "{}",
                    String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr)
                );
                let project = root.join(&name);
                assert_eq!(project.join("rust/Cargo.toml").is_file(), local);
                assert_eq!(project.join("build-rust.sh").is_file(), local);
                if platform == "android-app" {
                    assert_eq!(
                        fs::read(project.join("gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar")).unwrap(),
                        include_bytes!(
                            "../templates/android-app/common/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar"
                        )
                        .as_slice()
                    );
                    assert!(fs::read_to_string(project.join("app/build.gradle.kts"))
                        .unwrap()
                        .contains(&id));
                    let main = fs::read_to_string(
                        project.join("app/src/main/kotlin/ewe/starter/MainActivity.kt"),
                    )
                    .unwrap();
                    assert!(main.contains(&format!("package {id}")));
                    assert_eq!(main.contains("LocalEweScreen"), local);
                    assert_eq!(main.contains("RemoteEweScreen"), !local);
                } else {
                    let xcode = project.join(format!("{name}.xcodeproj"));
                    assert!(xcode
                        .join(format!("xcshareddata/xcschemes/{name}.xcscheme"))
                        .is_file());
                    let project = fs::read_to_string(xcode.join("project.pbxproj")).unwrap();
                    assert!(project.contains(&id));
                    assert_eq!(project.contains("CounterFFI.xcframework"), local);
                }
                fs::write(project.join("README.md"), "keep").unwrap();
                let again = generate(&root, platform, &name, &id, host);
                assert!(!again.status.success());
                assert!(String::from_utf8_lossy(&again.stderr).contains(&name));
                assert_eq!(
                    fs::read_to_string(project.join("README.md")).unwrap(),
                    "keep"
                );
            }
        }

    # Feature 26. Use ConnectRPC through the host network client
    
    ## Glossary
    
    | Term | Meaning |
    |---|---|
    | Remote procedure call (RPC) | A call to a function on another system. Connect is an RPC protocol. |
    | Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) | The request and response protocol that carries Connect messages. |
    | User interface (UI) frame | One complete Foundation wire message for a request or an update. |
    | Protocol Buffers (Protobuf) | The message format for this service. A schema defines the fields and procedures. |
    | Unary call | One request message followed by one reply message. |
    | Server stream | One request message followed by a sequence of reply messages. |
    | WebAssembly (Wasm) | The format that runs compiled Rust code inside the browser. |
    | UniFFI | The binding generator that connects Rust to Swift and Kotlin. |
    | Exchange | The HTTP request and response for one call. A host network client can serve many exchanges. |
    
    ## Primary outcome on mobile
    
    An iOS or Android application can call its own Connect service and receive typed application data.
    The application can make this call before it creates a screen. Only the optional UI action adapter handles Foundation frames.
    
    For example, an application defines this procedure in its service schema:
    
    ```protobuf
    message GetTodoRequest { uint64 id = 1; }
    message Todo { uint64 id = 1; string title = 2; }
    service Todos { rpc GetTodo(GetTodoRequest) returns (Todo); }
    ```
    
    Swift or Kotlin calls an application method exposed by its Rust library.
    That method calls the generated Rust client through the injected native network client.
    Rust decodes the service reply into a typed `Todo`. The native caller can read its title directly.
    The same transport can serve an application that uses only ordinary procedures.
    
    ## What works today
    
    A mobile screen can install a Rust core with local actions and a remote action sender.
    The native `HostTransport::send` method takes one UI request and returns an optional reply.
    Swift and Kotlin provide senders for the existing HTTP action endpoint.
    Browser JavaScript also sends Foundation requests directly. [Native callback](../../../../backends/foundation_ui_native/src/host.rs) · [Swift setup](../../../../mobile/ios/Sources/EweUI/ServerScreen.swift) · [Android setup](../../../../mobile/android/ui/src/main/kotlin/ewe/ui/compose/EweHost.kt) · [Browser sender](../../../../backends/foundation_wasm_ui/runtimes/foundation-ui-actions.js)
    
    Generated Rust RPC clients already accept an `Arc<dyn Transport>`, a base address, and client options.
    The transport opens an exchange with request bytes, response headers, response bytes, and optional trailing headers.
    Rust handles the protocol, message encoding, limits, deadlines, and cancellation.
    The crate supports Connect, gRPC, and gRPC-Web. It provides Protobuf and JSON codecs.
    The browser Fetch module declares capabilities for unary calls and server streams. It supplies no concrete Fetch transport.

    specifications/69-foundation-ui-v2/requirements.md:161:| D46 | **The WebView is a native control in the schema, and the app or a frame decides where it goes.** As Tauri does, the framework provides a control that makes it easy to load a WebView. A frame can place it: `MountWebView { node_id; parent_id; url }` is a member of `MobileOperation` and its own specific type (D43). It says where to mount and what to load; the normal typed properties on `node_id` (width, height, hidden) say how to display it. The native app takes it from there. The app's own code can also place the same control. The place is free: a full screen, a specific view or a component. The framework sets no rule for it. Inside the WebView, the web runtime works as it does in a browser: it points at the endpoint and loads the page. The transport is free: an HTTP server, a Rust backend in the app through an inter-process communication (IPC) socket, or another way. The messages are the same on every transport. On HTTP, the headers mark clearly which message is ours and which is generic. **The control is later work**, after the web and the native renderers. **We build our own control from the Tauri and wry source**: we take the code, change it to fit our design, or copy a part and make it better. It is not a small copy: the WebView control feature starts with a deep study of the Tauri and wry source and pulls out every good part that fits (the WebView setup on each platform, the custom URL scheme handling, the message bridge, the lifecycle). `research/14-webview-control.md` is the first step: it shows that Tauri as the app shell does not fit, because Tauri owns the root view on mobile. Each copied part and its source go in the `NOTICE` file, as the MIT and Apache-2.0 licences of Tauri and wry ask. | A4. `NativeControl` with `WEB_VIEW` in feature 01 becomes the specific type `MountWebView`. `WebViewControl` moves out of features 14 and 15 into its own later feature (18, "WebView control"), whose first step is the deep study of the Tauri and wry source. Features 10 and 11 state that a transport is any object with a `send` function, with an IPC socket as an example |

The host-owned dialog no longer needs that decision. `Either` belongs around the visible choice between Add and Confirm Delete. Each control needs one binding. Yes. We redesigned it. `if local` is still there because the implementation stopped after the live count migration. The dialog, rows, and mutation handlers kept the old store selection. I reported Feature 32 as complete too early.

The host owns the dialog on every platform. It opens, closes, and shows pending changes immediately. The server owns confirmed Todo changes. No control needs to inspect `OnDevice` to choose its action. Replacing `if local` with `<Either condition={local}>` would preserve the same mistake.

I corrected the status to **partial** and assigned the migration to the Todo agent. Issue 714 remains open.     For the unqualified todo action, the template produces `host:add_todo`. The input supplies the submitted text and its own attached bytes.
    

    The example uses the generated action input for `submit_input`.
    A client without the Rust implementation calls `registry.declare(None, "add_todo", Scope::All)?`.
    This declaration permits server fallback for that action. The server advertises its bare name through `ServerCaps.actions`.
    On success, the manager returns `Option<Vec<u8>>`. With `Some(frame)`, the host gives the immediate reply to its renderer.
    With `None`, the socket accepted the request. The receive path handles later frames.
    
    A page script can register a named web host action. A mobile surface cannot select it.
    The registry can hold separate web and mobile implementations of one name when their scopes do not overlap.
    
    ### Local execution applies to every client surface
    
    The surface identifies where the event starts: web or mobile. The execution origin identifies who handles it: host or server.
    Local means execution on the host handling that event. A browser and a mobile app can each run local actions.
    One registry can index entries by name, origin, and scope. Endpoints in the same process can share it.
    
    | Unqualified binding | Browser | Mobile app |
    |---|---|---|
    | A callable host entry matches this surface | Run in the browser. | Run on the device. |
    | Only an advertised server entry matches, and a server transport exists | Send once to the server. | Send once to the server. |
    | Neither route is available | Return a lookup or routing error. | Return a lookup or routing error. |
    
    Apply scope before selecting a candidate. A mobile-only host entry cannot execute in the browser.
    An explicit host declaration requires a local handler. An explicit server declaration uses the server route.
    Choose the route before execution. A local handler error must never trigger a second call on the server.
    Test each row on both surfaces. Include a disconnected device and a failing local handler.
    
    **Laws and tests.** A duplicate registration fails without changing the registry.
    An unknown name, wrong scope or unavailable required origin returns a typed error. Verify that no transport receives the rejected request.
    Use recording transports to test each row, including fallback and an explicit host action with no local implementation.

    /// Stores declarations and callable actions for a host.
    #[derive(Default)]
    pub struct ActionRegistry {
        entries: BTreeMap<String, Vec<Entry>>,
    }
    
    impl ActionRegistry {
        #[must_use]
        pub fn new() -> Self {
            Self::default()
        }
    
        /// Registers the Rust implementation for a declaration.
        ///
        /// # Errors
        /// Rejects an invalid name or an overlapping registration.
        pub fn register<A, E>(&mut self, action: A) -> Result<(), RegistrationError>
        where
            A: Action<E>,
            E: DeserializeOwned + 'static,
        {
            self.insert(
                A::origin(),
                A::NAME,
                A::scope(),
                Implementation::Rust(std::sync::Arc::new(Adapter(
                    action,
                    std::marker::PhantomData,
                ))),
            )
        }
    
        /// Registers a function provided by the page script transport.
        ///
        /// # Errors
        /// Rejects an invalid name or an overlapping registration.
        pub fn register_page(&mut self, name: &str) -> Result<(), RegistrationError> {
            self.insert(Some(Origin::Host), name, Scope::Web, Implementation::Page)
        }
    
        /// Declares an action whose implementation can live on another host.
        ///
        /// # Errors
        /// Rejects an invalid name or an overlapping declaration.
        pub fn declare(
            &mut self,
            origin: Option<Origin>,
            name: &str,
            scope: Scope,
        ) -> Result<(), RegistrationError> {
            self.insert(origin, name, scope, Implementation::Absent)
        }
    
        fn insert(
            &mut self,
            origin: Option<Origin>,
            name: &str,
            scope: Scope,
            implementation: Implementation,
        ) -> Result<(), RegistrationError> {
            if !valid_name(name) {
                return Err(RegistrationError::InvalidName);
            }
            let entries = self.entries.entry(name.to_owned()).or_default();
            for entry in entries.iter_mut() {
                let same_origin = origin == entry.origin || origin.is_none() || entry.origin.is_none();
                if same_origin && scope.overlaps(entry.scope) {
                    if origin == entry.origin
                        && scope == entry.scope
                        && matches!(entry.implementation, Implementation::Absent)

        fn entry(&self, origin: Origin, name: &str, surface: Surface) -> Result<&Entry, LookupError> {
            let entries = self.entries.get(name).ok_or(LookupError::UnknownAction)?;
            let mut error = LookupError::UnavailableOrigin;
            for entry in entries {
                if entry.origin.is_none() || entry.origin == Some(origin) {
                    if entry.scope.supports(surface) {
                        return Ok(entry);
                    }
                    error = LookupError::UnsupportedAction;
                }
            }
            Err(error)
        }
    
        /// Reads a declaration and reports whether this host has its implementation.
        ///
        /// # Errors
        /// Rejects unknown names, unavailable origins and unsupported surfaces.
        pub fn lookup(
            &self,
            origin: Origin,
            name: &str,
            surface: Surface,
        ) -> Result<Declaration, LookupError> {
            let entry = self.entry(origin, name, surface)?;
            Ok(Declaration {
                origin: entry.origin,
                scope: entry.scope,
                local: !matches!(entry.implementation, Implementation::Absent),
            })
        }

        pub fn server_actions(&self, surface: Surface) -> Vec<ServerActionT> {
            self.entries
                .iter()
                .filter_map(|(name, entries)| {
                    let entry = entries.iter().find(|entry| {
                        entry.origin != Some(Origin::Host)
                            && entry.scope.supports(surface)
                            && matches!(entry.implementation, Implementation::Rust(_))
                    })?;
                    let mut declaration = ServerActionT::default();
                    declaration.name = Some(name.clone());
                    declaration.hash = declaration_hash(entry.origin, name, entry.scope);
                    Some(declaration)
                })
                .collect()
        }

Yes. **Feature 05 describes the registration model you remember.** An action has a name, an execution origin (`Host` or `Server`), and a scope (`All`, `Web`, or `Mobile`). Two implementations can share a name when their scopes do not overlap. The registry checks the scope before selecting a handler. Feature 06 defines how authors declare those limits with `#[action(host, web)]` and `#[action(host, mobile)]`. [Feature 05](</Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/specifications/69-foundation-ui-v2/features/05-action-runtime/feature.md:193>) · [Feature 06](</Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/specifications/69-foundation-ui-v2/features/06-action-macro/feature.md:101>)

**The Todo startup code has drifted.** Mobile calls `local_registry`, which adds `initialize_todos` and declares three server actions. The browser calls `host_registry` directly and installs its cache separately. Those paths already produce different registrations for shared controls. [Mobile startup](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/mobile.rs:22) · [Browser startup](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/web.rs:14)

Separate processes still need their own registry instances. The server registers callable mutations. A client can declare those actions and send requests to the server. **That explains separate instances. It does not justify maintaining duplicate action lists.** Feature 32 explicitly requires removing duplicate device mutations and declaring platform scope at registration. [Feature 32](</Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/specifications/69-foundation-ui-v2/features/32-portable-view-targets/feature.md:143>)

I directed the Todo agent to use one shared set of action definitions, install the cache separately, and verify the registrations on both hosts.

`add_todo` needs a **server dispatcher**. It does not need a separately written `server_registry()` function. My earlier wording blurred those two things.

Here is the actual Todo action:

```rust
#[action(server)]
async fn add_todo(ctx: &Context, event: Interaction<()>) -> ActionResult {
    add(ctx, &event.input_value)
}
```

`#[action(server)]` declares who owns the write. The server route builds its dispatcher with `Origin::Server`. Before calling a handler, the dispatcher checks that the request origin matches its own. It then looks up the action by origin, name, and caller surface. A browser and an iPhone can therefore submit the same `server:add_todo` action. [Todo action](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/shared/mod.rs:365) · [Server route](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_ui_http/src/action_route.rs:34) · [Dispatch check](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_ui_runtime/src/dispatch/dispatcher.rs:144)

The current worktree now has `register_for`. Here is how one registration list can serve both endpoints:

```rust
fn todo_registry(endpoint: Origin) -> Result<ActionRegistry, RegistrationError> {
    let mut actions = ActionRegistry::new();
    actions.register_for(endpoint, add_todo)?;     // #[action(server)]
    actions.register_for(endpoint, close_dialog)?; // #[action(host)]
    Ok(actions)
}
```

| Startup call | `add_todo` | `close_dialog` |
|---|---|---|
| `todo_registry(Origin::Server)` | Registers the callable handler | Keeps the declaration |
| `todo_registry(Origin::Host)` | Keeps the declaration | Registers the callable handler |

Each process builds an instance in its own memory. **The application lists each action once.** The action attribute supplies ownership, and `register_for` uses it during startup. The helper is present in the working tree. The example above illustrates its intended use. [Registration helper](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_ui_runtime/src/action/registry.rs:325)

| Call for `#[action(server)] add_todo` | What the registry stores |
|---|---|
| `register_for(Origin::Server, add_todo)` | The callable Rust handler. |

An action declares one optional origin. `None` permits either endpoint to install the handler. Platform scope is separate. Registration preserves `All`, `Web`, or `Mobile`, and lookup checks that scope against the caller’s surface. Feature 27 implements compile-time selection. Rust compiles `ui_todo::web` only when the `web` feature is enabled and the target is `wasm32`. A native build skips that entire module. Feature 06 handles action scope differently. For `#[action(host, web)]` in shared code, the macro emits `Scope::Web` **and the handler body**. It preserves an explicit `#[cfg(...)]`, but it generates no compiler condition from `web`. The registry enforces the scope during dispatch. Linker optimization may remove unused code, so the annotation gives no guarantee about the final binary. The distinction matters for `#[action(server, web)]`. A browser calls that action, but a native server executes its handler. For a browser-only **host** action, placing its implementation in the gated `web` module gives the compile-time exclusion you mean.         ## Proposed extension. Select action implementations at build time
        
        An output role identifies the code that an artifact can execute.
        The framework build task selects the supported roles for each artifact.
        A development artifact can support several roles.
        The compiler target alone cannot distinguish a native server from a native client.
        
        Application authors declare each action once. They use the same action name in markup and registration on every output.
        They do not add Cargo feature conditions to action functions, registration calls, or markup.
        The generated declaration keeps the name, input contract, origin, and caller scope.
        Generate the callable adapter and function body only when the output can execute the action.
        The registry uses the declaration directly when the output excludes the implementation.
        Keep the existing duplicate and overlap checks.
        
        | Declaration | Outputs that compile the handler |
        |---|---|
        | `#[action(host, web)]` | Outputs with a browser host |
        | `#[action(host, mobile)]` | Outputs with a mobile host, including desktop binding generation when requested |
        | `#[action(server, web)]` | Server outputs. Only web callers qualify at dispatch. |
        | `#[action(server, mobile)]` | Server outputs. Only mobile callers qualify at dispatch. |
        | `#[action(host)]` | All host outputs |
        | `#[action(server)]` | Server outputs |
        | `#[action]` | Preserve existing unrestricted routing for the roles the output supports. |
        
        The framework supplies role selection to macro expansion in the consuming crate.
        Keep ordinary Cargo builds and multi-role tests working. Document the default for each supported build entry point.
        Keep platform-specific imports inside their gated implementation. Cargo must select platform-specific dependencies before macro expansion.
        Inventory the template and registration macros that reference action values. Each must work with a declaration alone.
        
        ```mermaid
        flowchart LR
            A[Action declaration] --> D[Descriptor on each output]
            R[Output roles] --> G[Generated compiler condition]
            G --> H[Handler on eligible outputs]
            D --> L[Shared registration list]
            H --> L
        ```
        
        The same registration list accepts a declaration or an available handler.
        
        1. Build an external consumer for browser, mobile, server, and combined roles with one registration list.
        2. Put a target-specific symbol inside each restricted handler. Compile each output without the other platform symbols.
        3. Inspect the release dependency graph and artifacts for excluded implementations and platform libraries.
        4. Call a native server handler from its allowed browser scope. Reject a mobile caller before execution.
        5. Exercise same-name handlers with disjoint scopes, plain actions, and existing runtime registration tests.
        
        This extension awaits owner approval.

## Assistant

Take `#[action(server)] add_todo`. In the approved design, browser and server builds both use `registry.register_for(endpoint, add_todo)?`.

- **The browser build** keeps the action’s name, server origin, and allowed caller scope. That declaration lets a button bind to `server:add_todo` and send the request. The browser build excludes the Rust handler body.
- **The server build** keeps the same declaration and compiles the handler body. Its dispatcher can execute `add_todo` when the request arrives.

**Duplicate and overlap checks** prevent two entries from claiming the same call. For example, suppose two handlers both use the name `pick_file`:

| First registration | Second registration | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Host, web | Host, mobile | Allowed. Each caller surface selects one handler. |
| Host, all surfaces | Host, web | Rejected. Both entries claim browser calls. |
| Host, web | Host, web | Rejected when both supply handlers. |
| Host, web | Server, web | Allowed. The execution origins differ. |

One existing rule permits an upgrade: when an entry contains only a declaration, a handler with the **exact same name, origin, and scope** can fill it. A second handler for that entry fails. These checks exist today. The approved extension adds compile-time exclusion of the handler body. [Registry implementation](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_ui_runtime/src/action/registry.rs:382)

## Assistant

`data_app()` builds a small, read-only service for Feature 26. The other constructors build the **full Todo server** with different starting conditions.

| Function | What it starts |
|---|---|
| `app(module)` | The full server with an empty Todo store and a fresh live stream. |
| `app_with_todos(module, items)` | The full server with restored todos. It preserves their identifiers and rejects zero or duplicate identifiers. |
| `app_with_channel(module, channel)` | The full server with an empty store and a supplied live stream. Replay tests use this to control stream history. |
| `data_app()` | A service exposing only `GetTodo`. Its store contains one record, `42`, “Buy milk”. The executable selects it with `--data-only`. |

The first three call `app_with_store()`, which installs the store, screens, actions, live updates, browser assets, and `GetTodo`. [Full server setup](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/server.rs:82)

**Both modes use the same `GetTodo` implementation.** The separate `data_app()` proves that Swift and Kotlin can fetch a typed Todo through a remote procedure call without starting a screen, negotiating a user interface session, or loading a browser module. That independence is an explicit Feature 26 acceptance check. [Data service](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/server.rs:139) · [Feature 26 acceptance check](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/specifications/69-foundation-ui-v2/features/26-connectrpc-transport/feature.md:151)

    #[derive(Clone)]
    pub(crate) struct TodoFeed(pub(super) LiveChannel);
    
    impl TodoFeed {
        pub(crate) fn publish(&self, ctx: &Ctx, change: &crate::RecordChange) -> Result<u64, Error> {
            self.0.sender().push_with(|position| {
                let view = Context::for_render(ctx.clone());
                TodoDelivery::Committed {
                    position,
                    change: change.clone(),
                }
                .send(&view)?;
                Ok(prepare_messages(ctx, view.into_receiver().drain())?)
            })
        }
    }
    
    struct BusinessActions;
    impl ActionRequestPolicy for BusinessActions {
        fn check(&self, _: &Ctx, action: ActionRequest<'_>) -> Result<(), ActionError> {
            if action.state().is_some() {
                return Err(ActionError::new(
                    ErrorCode::StateRejected,
                    "Business actions reject presentation state",
                ));
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    }
    
    pub(super) fn install(ctx: &Ctx, web: LiveChannel, store: TodoStore) -> Result<TodoFeed, Error> {
        if web.stream_id() != 1 {
            return Err("The todo page listens to stream 1".into());
        }
        crate::install_view_services(ctx, foundation_ui_runtime::action::Origin::Server)?;
        ctx.store(store);
        ctx.store(Arc::new(BusinessActions) as Arc<dyn ActionRequestPolicy>);
        let channels = TodoFeed(web);

            move |_, _| vec![Arc::new(feed.clone())],
        ));
        ctx.store(channels.clone());
        Ok(channels)
