## Assistant

Yes. A **prefilled `TodoStore` and a `LiveChannel`** are the right inputs for the full Todo server. The private `app_with_store(module, channel, store)` already has that shape. The three public constructors mostly choose values for it. I would expose one `app(module, store, channel)` and let startup supply those values. [Current constructors](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/server.rs:45)

- **Normal startup** supplies an empty store and a fresh channel.
- **Restore** supplies a validated, prefilled store and a fresh channel. The first `/initial` request already returns the stored items and the current stream position. Startup needs no synthetic update.
- **Replay tests** supply a channel with the desired history limit. A test that needs existing messages should seed them through the normal mutation and publication path. That keeps the store and replay history consistent. [Snapshot route](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/server.rs:23) · [Publication path](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/server/services.rs:15)

I would also define `GetTodo` registration once. The full app would include that route alongside its screens and actions. The `--data-only` entry point would use the same registration with a prefilled store. That preserves Feature 26’s requirement to run the data service independently and removes the repeated setup. [Feature 26 acceptance check](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/specifications/69-foundation-ui-v2/features/26-connectrpc-transport/feature.md:151)

One concrete benefit is that startup could restore todos **and** set a custom replay limit. Today, the `else if` means `--restore` bypasses `EWE_TODO_HISTORY`. [Executable startup](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/bin/server.rs:54)

    //! Start the example on a loopback address.
    use std::io::{self, Read};
    use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
    
    fn web_module() -> io::Result<PathBuf> {
        if let Some(configured) = std::env::var_os("EWE_TODO_MODULE") {
            let path = PathBuf::from(configured);
            validate_module(&path).map_err(|error| {
                io::Error::new(
                    error.kind(),
                    format!(
                        "EWE_TODO_MODULE '{}': {error}. Set it to the built ui_todo.wasm file.",
                        path.display()
                    ),
                )
            })?;
            return Ok(path);
        }
        let path = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("target/web/ui_todo.wasm");
        if !path.is_file() {
            eprintln!(
                "Browser module missing at '{}'. Run examples/ui_todo/build-module.sh or set EWE_TODO_MODULE. Native routes are available.",
                path.display()
            );
        }
        Ok(path)
    }
    
    fn validate_module(path: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
        if !path.metadata()?.is_file() {
            return Err(io::Error::other("expected a regular file"));
        }
        let mut header = [0; 8];
        std::fs::File::open(path)?.read_exact(&mut header)?;
        if &header != b"\0asm\x01\0\0\0" {
            return Err(io::Error::other("invalid WebAssembly module header"));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    
    fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync>> {
        let _pool = foundation_core::valtron::initialize_pool(0, None);
        let bind = std::env::args()
            .nth(1)
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "127.0.0.1:8180".to_owned());
        let listener = std::net::TcpListener::bind(bind)?;
        if !listener.local_addr()?.ip().is_loopback() {
            return Err("The single-user example requires a loopback address".into());

        let mode = std::env::args().nth(2);

                }
                ui_todo::server::app_with_todos(&module, serde_json::from_reader(file)?)?

    /// Builds the application with a fresh count stream.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Returns an error when route or asset setup fails.
    pub fn app(module: &Path) -> Result<HttpApp<Arc<dyn Serve>>, Error> {
        app_with_todos(module, Vec::new())
    }
    
    /// Starts the todo server with a supplied list and its existing identifiers.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Returns an error for duplicate or zero identifiers, or if route setup fails.
    pub fn app_with_todos(
        module: &Path,
        items: Vec<crate::Todo>,
    ) -> Result<HttpApp<Arc<dyn Serve>>, Error> {
        let mut ids = std::collections::HashSet::with_capacity(items.len());
        if items
            .iter()
            .any(|item| item.id == 0 || !ids.insert(item.id))
        {
            return Err("Invalid restored todo identifiers".into());
        }
        app_with_store(module, services::channel(1), TodoStore::with_items(items))
    }
    
    /// Builds the application with a host-supplied stream for replay tests.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Returns an error when the channel, routes, signer or assets are invalid.
    pub fn app_with_channel(
        module: &Path,
        channel: LiveChannel,
    ) -> Result<HttpApp<Arc<dyn Serve>>, Error> {
        app_with_store(module, channel, TodoStore::default())
    }
    
    fn app_with_store(
        module: &Path,
        channel: LiveChannel,
        store: TodoStore,
    ) -> Result<HttpApp<Arc<dyn Serve>>, Error> {
        let mut app = HttpApp::new_serve();
        let ctx = app.context().clone();
        let channels = services::install(&ctx, channel, store)?;
        register(&mut app.router, &ctx, channels)?;
        assets::register(&mut app.router, module)?;
        Ok(app)
    }

## Assistant

The Feature 26 assertions **already live in the native tests**. Swift and Kotlin each fetch todo `42`, check its title, then request `999` and check the error. [Swift test](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/ios/todo_server/UITests/TodoTests.swift:59) · [Kotlin test](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/android/todo_server/app/src/androidTest/kotlin/ewe/todo/ReplayCheck.kt:81)

**The misplaced piece is the fixture server.** `data_app()` hardcodes `42` and `"Buy milk"` in application source. The executable exposes `--data-only` so the device test runners can start that fixture. The fixture and its launcher belong under `examples/ui_todo/tests/`. The shared `GetTodo` implementation belongs in `src` because the full server also uses it. [Fixture](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/server.rs:139) · [Device test launcher](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_ui_native/src/tasks/device.rs:178)

The **replay test** is separate. It creates a channel, passes a clone to the server, then closes the channel to exercise reconnection. A public `app_with_store` would let the test supply its own store and channel directly. The executable also calls `app_with_channel` for its replay history setting. Both callers can use the same constructor. [Replay test](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/tests/todo_browser_tests.rs:20) · [Executable caller](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/bin/server.rs:77)

    use std::io::{self, Read};
    use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
    
    fn web_module() -> io::Result<PathBuf> {
        if let Some(configured) = std::env::var_os("EWE_TODO_MODULE") {
            let path = PathBuf::from(configured);
            validate_module(&path).map_err(|error| {
                io::Error::new(
                    error.kind(),
                    format!(
                        "EWE_TODO_MODULE '{}': {error}. Set it to the built ui_todo.wasm file.",
                        path.display()
                    ),
                )
            })?;
            return Ok(path);
        }
        let path = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("target/web/ui_todo.wasm");
        if !path.is_file() {
            eprintln!(
                "Browser module missing at '{}'. Run examples/ui_todo/build-module.sh or set EWE_TODO_MODULE. Native routes are available.",
                path.display()
            );
        }
        Ok(path)
    }
    
    fn validate_module(path: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
        if !path.metadata()?.is_file() {
            return Err(io::Error::other("expected a regular file"));
        }
        let mut header = [0; 8];
        std::fs::File::open(path)?.read_exact(&mut header)?;
        if &header != b"\0asm\x01\0\0\0" {
            return Err(io::Error::other("invalid WebAssembly module header"));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

        let _pool = foundation_core::valtron::initialize_pool(0, None);

            .unwrap_or_else(|| "127.0.0.1:8180".to_owned());
        let listener = std::net::TcpListener::bind(bind)?;
        if !listener.local_addr()?.ip().is_loopback() {
            return Err("The single-user example requires a loopback address".into());

        let mode = std::env::args().nth(2);

                let channel = LiveChannel::new(

                ui_todo::server::app_with_channel(&module, channel)?

## Assistant

The server currently knows where Cargo built the browser module, checks its header, and registers individual asset files. That build knowledge belongs in `build.rs`. The `platform_demo` pattern fits here: its build script calls one reusable helper. [Todo startup](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/bin/server.rs:5) · [Current asset routes](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/server/assets.rs:14) · [Demo build script](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/platform_demo/build.rs:1)

I updated Feature 27 with this design:

- The build produces `ui_todo` and a sibling `public/` directory containing everything the browser requests.
- The server mounts `public/` relative to its executable. Browser addresses such as `/module.wasm` stay stable when the directory moves.
- One server constructor accepts a prepared `TodoStore` and `LiveChannel`. The browser replay test supplies its own channel.
- The seeded `GetTodo` fixture moves under `tests/`. Swift and Kotlin keep their native assertions.

The acceptance check copies the executable and `public/` elsewhere, starts the server from another working directory, and exercises browser actions. That catches accidental dependencies on the source checkout. [Feature 27 revision](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/specifications/69-foundation-ui-v2/features/27-single-todo-package/feature.md#proposed-revision-build-the-deployable-todo-directory)

    /// Serves the embedded `index.html` at the application root.
    struct IndexHandler;
    
    impl ServeFactory for IndexHandler {
        fn create(_ctx: &Ctx) -> Self {
            Self
        }
    }
    
    impl Serve for IndexHandler {
        fn serve(
            &self,
            ctx: Ctx,
            _req: SimpleIncomingRequest,
            conn: SharedByteBufferStream<RawStream>,
        ) -> ConnectionResult {
            match Assets::get("static/index.html") {
                Some(html_data) => {
                    let content =
                        String::from_utf8(html_data.data.to_vec()).expect("should generate str");
                    send_html(conn, 200, &content, &ctx)
                }
                None => send_not_found(conn, &ctx),
            }
        }
    }

    pub fn generate_platform_code() {
        let manifest_dir = PathBuf::from(std::env::var("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR").unwrap());
        let project_root = manifest_dir.parent().unwrap().to_path_buf();
    
        println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=src/");
        println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=build.rs");
    
        let mut apps = Vec::new();
        let app_dir = project_root.join("app");
        if app_dir.join("Cargo.toml").exists() {
            apps.push(AppDistribution {
                name: "app".into(),
                crate_dir: app_dir,
                route_prefix: "/app/".into(),
            });
        }
        if let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(&project_root) {
            for e in entries.filter_map(std::result::Result::ok) {
                let p = e.path();
                let n = p
                    .file_name()
                    .and_then(|n| n.to_str())
                    .unwrap_or("")
                    .to_string();
                if n.starts_with("app-") && p.is_dir() && p.join("Cargo.toml").exists() {
                    // Skip wasmtime shell crates (app-shell, app-shell-*) — handled separately
                    if n.starts_with("app-shell") {
                        continue;
                    }
                    apps.push(AppDistribution {
                        name: n.clone(),
                        crate_dir: p,
                        route_prefix: format!("/{n}/"),
                    });
                }
            }
        }
    
        if !apps.is_empty() {
            let public_dir = manifest_dir.join("public");
            build_all_wasm_apps(&apps, &public_dir);
            let generated_dir = manifest_dir.join("src").join("generated");
            std::fs::create_dir_all(&generated_dir).ok();
            generate_app_modules(&apps, &generated_dir);
        }
    
        // F33: Discover wasmtime shell apps (surface 3 — in-process WASM).
        // Only generates modules if foundation_wasmtime is in Cargo.toml deps.
        let has_wasmtime_dep = std::fs::read_to_string(manifest_dir.join("Cargo.toml"))
            .is_ok_and(|c| c.contains("foundation_wasmtime"));
        let mut shells: Vec<AppDistribution> = Vec::new();
        if has_wasmtime_dep {
            let shell_dir = project_root.join("app-shell");
            if shell_dir.join("Cargo.toml").exists() {
                shells.push(AppDistribution {
                    name: "app_shell".into(),
                    crate_dir: shell_dir,
                    route_prefix: "/shell/".into(),
                });
            }
            if let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(&project_root) {
                for e in entries.filter_map(std::result::Result::ok) {
                    let p = e.path();
                    let n = p
                        .file_name()
                        .and_then(|n| n.to_str())
                        .unwrap_or("")
                        .to_string();
                    if n.starts_with("app-shell-") && p.is_dir() && p.join("Cargo.toml").exists() {
                        shells.push(AppDistribution {
                            name: n.replace('-', "_"),
                            crate_dir: p,
                            route_prefix: format!("/{n}/"),
                        });
                    }
                }
            }
            if !shells.is_empty() {
                let shell_out = manifest_dir.join("shell_wasm");
                std::fs::create_dir_all(&shell_out).ok();
                for s in &shells {
                    build_wasmtime_app(&s.crate_dir, &shell_out);
                }
                let generated_dir = manifest_dir.join("src").join("generated");
                generate_wasmtime_modules(&shells, &generated_dir);
            }
        }
    
        // Patch tauri.conf.json BEFORE tauri_build reads it.
        // Sets the initial window URL to bypass WebViewAssetLoader.
        if let Some(first) = apps.first() {
            patch_tauri_conf_for_ewe(&manifest_dir, &first.route_prefix);
        } else {
            patch_tauri_conf_for_ewe(&manifest_dir, "/__platform__/");
        }
    
        tauri_build::build();
    }

    # Feature 2. Install a capability in a Cargo build script
    
    Status: Proposed for approval.
    
    ## Terms
    
    A build hook is a Rust function that Cargo runs through a package build script.
    A provider is the package that supplies the hook function and its required build dependencies.
    
    ## User flow
    
    A capability task calls a reusable installer with a target package and a provider declaration.
    The provider supplies its stable name, Rust call, dependency specification, and required features.
    The installer configures the package once. Cargo calls the installed hook on subsequent builds.
    The provider owns code generation and input tracking.
    
    ```mermaid
    flowchart LR
        P[Package capability task] --> I[Shared installer]
        I --> M[Target Cargo.toml]
        I --> B[Target build script]
        B --> H[Provider build hook]
        H --> O[Generated build outputs]
    ```
    
    The installation task edits project files. The build hook produces outputs during a later Cargo build.
    
    ## Implementation contract
    
    1. Provide the installation operation through a reusable Rust library and an importable task set.
    2. Let existing runners register the task. Use the proposed name `build:install-hook`.
    3. Accept a target package manifest and a registered capability name. Resolve paths from that manifest.

        # Feature 3. Package application resources
        
        Status: Proposed for approval.
        
        ## Terms
        
        A resource is a file that the application reads by a stable relative name.
        A resource set lists files, directories, generated outputs, and the targets that use them.
        A staging directory holds generated packaging inputs. Each target owns its staging directory.
        
        ## Existing design
        
        The platform demo calls one function from its Cargo build script.
        The old generator discovers sibling applications, builds browser modules, and writes public files and generated Rust modules.
        The generated mobile asset type accepts a root from the host session.
        The session checks for a development public directory and otherwise uses its packaged root.
        Keep the stable logical names and the single build hook.
        Use explicit resource inputs and return errors for failed reads, writes, and packaging steps.
        
        ## Proposed interface
        
        Store application declarations in a package-relative `resources.toml`. Build providers can also supply generated inputs by logical name.
        Use the Feature 2 installer to add the hook to existing applications. Include it in new application templates.
        The proposed Cargo build script call is `foundation_resources::build::stage_from_cargo()?`.
        The package declares resources once. Target adapters supply packaging destinations and runtime readers.
        Expose a host resource service through the application context. Open a resource by name and return a readable stream or a typed error.
        Keep the build helper synchronous. Inject the host reader for runtime tests.
        
        ```mermaid
        flowchart LR
            Declarations[Resource set] --> Hook[Cargo build hook]
            Generated[Generated files] --> Hook
            Hook --> Web[Public tree]
            Hook --> Apple[Bundle resource folder]
            Hook --> Android[Packaged assets directory]
            Web --> Embed[Server asset derive]
        ```
        
        Each output preserves the same resource name.
        
        | Target | Build destination | Consumer |
        |---|---|---|
        | Web development | Sibling public directory for the server executable | Static handler reads files from disk. |
        | Web release | Staged public tree before macro expansion | The server asset derive embeds the tree. |
        | Apple mobile | Generated folder registered once in the application target resource build phase | The host opens the name in the application bundle. |
        | Android | Generated asset directory registered once in the application variant | The host opens the name with the Android asset manager. |
        
        For example, declare `art/train.png` once. Serve it at `/art/train.png` on the web.
        Open `art/train.png` through the native resource service on both phones.
        Allow target restrictions for files such as the browser bootstrap module.
        
        ## Build contract
        
        1. Resolve inputs against the declaring package or a registered generator output.
        2. Reject missing inputs, duplicate names, path escapes, and conflicting names on case-insensitive platforms.
        3. Track declared directories, files, generator outputs, and relevant environment values for Cargo rebuilds.
        4. Run producers before staging. Use the existing task graph for builds that require a different compiler target.

The platform demo has two ideas worth keeping. Its `build.rs` calls one helper, and its generated mobile asset type accepts a resource root from the host. This lets application code use a stable name such as `art/train.png` across platforms. [Demo build script](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/platform_demo/build.rs:1) · [Asset generation](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_platform/src/codegen.rs:247)

I wrote **Specification 90, Feature 3** for the reusable resource manager. An application declares its resources once. Its build hook stages them automatically.

| Target | What happens to `art/train.png` |
|---|---|
| Web development | The build copies it into `public/art/train.png`. The server reads it from disk. |
| Web release | The asset derive embeds it in the executable. The browser uses the same `/art/train.png` address. |
| iPhone | The build adds it to the application bundle. The host opens it by name. |
| Android | The build adds it to the application’s packaged assets. The host opens it by the same name. |

Mobile packaging needs one extra step: Xcode and Gradle must know which generated directory to package and when it becomes available. The proposed templates and installer own that setup. The acceptance test reads the file from each **installed application** and compares its bytes with the web response. This catches a build that copies files successfully but leaves them out of the package.

Todo is the first planned consumer. The manager is specified and awaits approval for implementation. [Resource manager plan](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/specifications/90-foundation-tasks/features/03-platform-resource-manager/feature.md)

        43    fn remote_core(
        44        platform: NativePlatform,
        45        transport: Arc<dyn HostTransport>,
        46        path: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
        47    ) -> Result<Arc<NativeCore>, CoreError> {
        48        let ctx = todo_context()?;
        49        if let Some(path) = path {
        50            crate::install_pending_storage(&ctx, Arc::new(pending::FileStorage(path)));
        51        }
        52        let registry = crate::host_registry().map_err(|e| CoreError::BadReference {
        53            detail: e.to_string(),
        54        })?;
        55        let sender = Arc::new(pending::Sender {
        56            ctx: ctx.clone(),
        57            transport,
        58            core: Default::default(),
        59        });
        60        let core = NativeCore::builder(platform, ctx, registry)
        61            .with_host_transport(sender.clone())
        62            .build();
        63        sender
        64            .core
        65            .set(Arc::downgrade(&core))
        66            .map_err(|_| CoreError::Write {
        67                detail: "Duplicate Todo sender".into(),
        68            })?;
        69        Ok(core)
        70    }

## Assistant

I checked both files with the Todo agent. **`mobile.rs` connects the phone app to the shared Todo runtime. `mobile_pending.rs` handles phone storage and shows pending changes before the network request completes.** The rules for Add, Delete, retry, and confirmation live in the shared `outbox.rs`. An *outbox* holds changes the user submitted that still await confirmation.

### What `mobile.rs` does at startup

Swift and Kotlin call Rust through this file. It exposes three constructors with different behavior. [Mobile entry points](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/mobile.rs:19)

| Constructor | What the caller gets |
|---|---|
| `create_persistent_todo_core` | The iPhone and Android Todo Server apps supply a network transport and a private file path. Pending submissions survive an app restart. |
| `create_todo_core` | Existing callers supply a network transport. Pending submissions stay in memory and disappear when the process exits. |
| `create_local_todo_core` | The on-device example gets a display cache and host actions. It has no network transport for server mutations. |

The first two call `remote_core`. It installs the shared host registry, wraps the supplied transport in `pending::Sender`, and builds the native core. The file also exports the theme and `get_todo`. That last function serves the separate Feature 26 data example. [Core setup](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/mobile.rs:43) · [Data example](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/mobile.rs:136)

### What happens when you add “Buy milk”

1. **You tap Add.** The control sends `server:add_todo`. The native sender passes the request to the shared outbox. [Sender](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/mobile_pending.rs:81)
2. **The outbox prepares the pending item.** It creates a stable identifier and saves the submission. On a phone, `FileStorage` writes a temporary file, syncs it, then replaces the previous file. [Shared preparation](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/shared/outbox.rs:134) · [File storage](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/mobile_pending.rs:25)
3. **The pending row appears before the network send.** The sender delivers the local rendering update to the open screen. It then calls the phone’s supplied transport. The confirmed open count stays unchanged. [Send order](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/mobile_pending.rs:82)
4. **Confirmation or failure updates the row.** A committed server change resolves the pending item. A transport failure offers Retry. A validation error preserves the title for editing. After restart, Retry uses the original identifier, so resending can resolve the same submission. [Shared reconciliation](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/shared/outbox.rs:275) · [Restart and retry test](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/tests/mobile.rs:240)

Two gaps remain. If the transport accepts a send for later delivery and the reply disappears, the native sender has no timeout callback to offer Retry. Also, `FileStorage::load` reads the whole pending file without a size limit. [Reply handling](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/mobile_pending.rs:89) · [File read](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/mobile_pending.rs:15)

## Assistant

Yes. The server can own the confirmed list, the host can keep that list in memory, and disk storage can hold only unresolved changes. The current implementation puts too much Todo behavior inside the network sender.

### Why `HostTransport` and `Sender` exist

`HostTransport` lets Rust ask the phone’s network client to send an action request. That interface makes sense. The extra `Sender` wrapper exists because the Add button currently binds directly to `server:add_todo`. The agent intercepted that outgoing request to save the pending item and show it before the network call. The wrapper also inspects the reply for errors. [Native sender](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/mobile_pending.rs:80)

I would move that sequence into one shared host action, `submit_todo`. It saves the pending item, updates the cache, renders the row, and calls `server:add_todo`. The server action still owns the write. Retry calls the same submission path with the saved identifier. **The network sender then has no reason to understand a Todo or inspect its title.**

### Where live updates go today

Your proposed incoming path **already exists**. The server sends a typed `TodoDelivery` as MessagePack data in a frame. Chrome receives `ewe:data` and invokes `host:apply_todo_delivery`. Both mobile hosts register that same action for incoming view data. The action applies the snapshot or change to the cache and updates the affected named elements. The extra frame inspection happens on the outgoing submission path. [Server encoding and shared action](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/shared/mod.rs:517) · [Browser delivery](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/web/app.js:156) · [iPhone registration](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/ios/todo_server/App/App.swift:27) · [Android registration](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/android/todo_server/app/src/main/kotlin/ewe/todo/MainActivity.kt:31)

### How storage can work

The existing Rust `KeyValueStore` supports `get`, `set`, `delete`, and **`list_keys(prefix)`**. The repository also has a JSON file implementation. Native Rust already writes directly to an application-private path supplied by the phone. For this use, the host can install one store in its context. `thread_local!` would tie the handle to a thread. The file provides persistence across restarts. [Storage interface](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_db/src/core/storage_provider.rs:341) · [JSON file storage](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_db/src/native/json_file.rs:26)

1. **Open the screen.** Load the server snapshot into memory. List pending keys for this account and server.
2. **Submit Add.** Create one universally unique identifier (UUID). Save the pending record under its own key, render it, then send it.
3. **Receive confirmation.** Apply the committed record to memory and remove its pending key. Either the reply or the live update can arrive first.
4. **Retry.** Send the saved record with the same UUID. Automatic retry can enumerate the same keys. A batch action is optional.

One detail matters on reload: a pending Add missing from the snapshot might still be in flight. Keep it until the server confirms its outcome. Also, the current record has a numeric `id` and a separate `creation_id`. Moving to one UUID requires a migration for existing backups and clients. [Current record](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/shared/mod.rs:31)

    //! Call a selected action with the services and component root supplied by the host.
    
    use std::fmt;
    
    use foundation_context::Ctx;
    use foundation_errstacks::ErrorTrace;
    use foundation_ui_wire::{ActionRequestT, ErrorCode, MountSurface};
    
    use super::{ActionError, Context, ErasedAction, RawInput, RawInteraction, ReceiverItem};
    use crate::state::{verify_state, StateError};
    
    /// The host can distinguish a failed signature check from a handler or decode error.
    #[derive(Debug)]
    pub enum InvokeError {
        State(StateError),
        Action(ErrorTrace<ActionError>),
    }
    
    impl fmt::Display for InvokeError {
        fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            match self {
                Self::State(error) => error.fmt(formatter),
                Self::Action(error) => error.fmt(formatter),
            }
        }
    }
    
    impl std::error::Error for InvokeError {}
    
    /// Verifies the request state, calls the selected handler and returns its pending output.
    /// The caller authenticates the request and selects the entry before this call.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns the verification error or the full action trace. A failed call discards its receiver.
    pub async fn invoke_action(
        ctx: &Ctx,
        entry: &dyn ErasedAction,
        surface: MountSurface,
        state_root: Option<u32>,
        request: ActionRequestT,
    ) -> Result<Vec<ReceiverItem>, InvokeError> {
        let state_body = request
            .state
            .as_deref()
            .map(|signed| verify_state(ctx, signed))
            .transpose()
            .map_err(InvokeError::State)?;
        let input = request.input.unwrap_or_default();
        let event = RawInteraction {
            node_id: request.node_id,
            event_name: input.event_name.unwrap_or_default(),
            input_value: match (input.value, input.json) {
                (Some(value), None) => RawInput::Text(value),
                (None, Some(bytes)) => RawInput::Json(bytes),
                (None, None) => RawInput::Missing,
                (Some(_), Some(_)) => {
                    return Err(InvokeError::Action(ErrorTrace::new(ActionError::new(
                        ErrorCode::InvalidInput,
                        "The event supplied two input encodings",
                    ))))
                }
            },
            state_body,
        };
        let call = Context::for_action(ctx.clone(), surface, state_root);
        entry
            .call_raw(&call, event)
            .await
            .map_err(InvokeError::Action)?;
        Ok(call.into_receiver().drain())
    }
    /// Services, render target and output for one call.
    pub struct Context {
        inner: Ctx,
        surface: MountSurface,
        state_root: Option<u32>,
        is_action: bool,
        receiver: ActionReceiver,
    }
    
    impl Context {
        /// Starts a web render with the supplied host services.

                receiver: ActionReceiver::default(),
            }

            Self {
                inner,
                surface,
                state_root,

                receiver: ActionReceiver::default(),
            }
        }

        }

        }

        pub async fn trigger(

        ) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, ManagerError> {

That line asks the browser to display **“Todo added”** after the server accepts a new Todo.

- `b"\xabhost:notify"` manually encodes the string `host:notify` in MessagePack. `0xab` means the next 11 bytes contain a string.
- `data_in_view(...)` sends those bytes to the receiving view. It does not call `notify` itself.
- The browser listener checks for `0xab`, compares the text with `"host:notify"`, and calls `registry.hostFunction("notify")()`. That function sets the notice to “Todo added”. [Browser listener and handler](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/web/app.js:154)

The preceding `delivery.send(ctx)?` already sends the committed Todo change. This extra line creates a second, application-specific convention for one notification. A reader needs both the Rust byte literal and the JavaScript listener to understand it. [Server action](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/shared/mod.rs:700)

I would remove the byte marker and show the notice when the host confirms **its own pending Add**. That preserves the feedback and avoids showing “Todo added” when another client creates a Todo.

## Assistant

1. **How do I trigger an action directly today?** In Rust, call `manager.trigger("server:add_todo", event).await`. Use `trigger_structured` for typed input. The manager checks the origin and caller scope, selects the transport, and sends the request. Swift and Kotlin can use the corresponding `NativeCore` methods. [Rust action manager](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_ui_runtime/src/action/manager.rs:234) · [Native entry points](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_ui_native/src/core.rs:304)

2. **Can one action call another today?** A handler receives a `Context`. That context currently exposes no `trigger` method or built-in action manager. The framework has `invoke_action`, but it requires an already-selected handler and does not route a request to the server. **The missing operation is a routed call from inside a handler.** A host action should be able to write `ctx.trigger_structured("server:add_todo", …).await`. That is a proposed interface. [Action context](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_ui_runtime/src/action/context.rs:21) · [Internal invocation](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_ui_runtime/src/action/invoke.rs:36)

3. **Does Todo need to intercept the transport?** No. The wrapper exists because the button currently targets the server action directly. Bind the button to `host:submit_todo`. That action saves the pending item, updates the cache, publishes the visible row, and calls `server:add_todo`. The preview must reach the screen **before** the remote call finishes. Retry uses the same submission path and Todo identifier.

4. **Can a send report failure to a named action?** The current `trigger` call returns an immediate error to its caller. It has no built-in per-request registration such as “deliver failure to `host:submission_failed`”. I would add that option to the action manager. The failure event should carry the request identifier, action name, endpoint, and typed reason. The transport reports what happened. The manager delivers the event to the originating view. [Current return contract](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_ui_runtime/src/action/manager.rs:252)

5. **Can I attach a callback for success or failure across transports?** I would make a per-request Rust completion handle the common mechanism. A caller could await it, attach a callback, or name a host action to receive its result. For Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) and remote procedure calls (RPC), a reply can complete the request immediately. For WebSocket, sending bytes only means the socket accepted them. A later reply, failure, cancellation, or timeout completes the handle once. Where native code owns the connection, it reports that outcome to Rust using the request identifier. This common completion interface is **proposed**, not implemented.

6. **What if the request times out and the live update arrives afterward?** The send attempt and the Todo have different identifiers. The timeout can offer Retry. A later committed change still confirms the same Todo and clears Retry. The callback reports the attempt’s outcome. The server’s committed data determines the row’s state.

I recorded the child-action call, preview ordering, and completion contract in [Feature 32](</Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/specifications/69-foundation-ui-v2/features/32-portable-view-targets/feature.md#action-composition-and-delivery-outcomes>).

    pub(super) async fn reconcile(
        ctx: &Context,
        snapshot: bool,
    ) -> Result<bool, ErrorTrace<ActionError>> {
        let store = todo_store(ctx)?;
        let (changed, deleted) = change_pending(ctx, |entries| {
            let state = store
                .0
                .lock()
                .unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner);
            let before = entries.len();
            let mut deleted = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
            entries.retain(|_, pending| {
                let accepted = confirmed(&state, &pending.change, snapshot);
                if let PendingChange::Delete { id } = pending.change {
                    if accepted {
                        deleted.insert(id);
                    }
                }
                !accepted
            });
            let changed = entries.len() != before;
            Ok((changed, (changed, deleted)))
        })
        .await?;
        if !deleted.is_empty() {
            let mut state = store
                .0
                .lock()
                .unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner);
            if let Some(rows) = &mut state.search_rows {
                rows.retain(|row| !deleted.contains(&row.id));
            }
        }
        Ok(changed)
    }
    
    fn confirmed(state: &StoreState, change: &PendingChange, snapshot: bool) -> bool {
        match change {
            PendingChange::Add { id, .. } => {
                state.retired_ids.contains(id) || state.items.iter().any(|row| row.id == *id)
            }
            PendingChange::Delete { id } => {
                state.removed.contains_key(id)
                    || (snapshot && !state.items.iter().any(|row| row.id == *id))
            }
        }
    }

    async fn apply_todo_delivery(ctx: &Context, event: Interaction<(), Vec<u8>>) -> ActionResult {
        // The view can also receive data for other applications.
        if !event.input_value.starts_with(b"\x92\xabewe.todo.v1") {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let (_, delivery): (String, TodoDelivery) =
            rmp_serde::from_slice(&event.input_value).map_err(|e| error(&e.to_string()))?;
        let store = todo_store(ctx)?;
        let snapshot = matches!(delivery, TodoDelivery::Snapshot { .. });
        let changed = {
            let mut state = store
                .0
                .lock()
                .unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner);
            match &delivery {
                TodoDelivery::Deleted { id } => {
                    if state.delete_target == Some(*id) {
                        state.delete_target = None;
                        dialog(ctx, &state.snapshot())?;
                    }
                    return Ok(());
                }
                _ => {}
            }
            state.ingest(delivery)
        };
        let reconciled = outbox::reconcile(ctx, snapshot).await?;
        if changed || reconciled {
            let state = store
                .0
                .lock()
                .unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner);
            if state.search_rows.is_none() || snapshot || reconciled {
                state.render_rows(ctx)?;
            }
            replace(
                ctx,
                "#open-count",
                open_count(state.items.iter().filter(|r| !r.done).count()),
            )?;
            if snapshot {
                if !state.query.is_empty() {
                    replace(ctx, "#todo-search", search_input(&state.query))?;
                }
                replace(ctx, "#todo-filter", filters(&state.filter))?;
                if state.add_dialog || state.delete_target.is_some() {
                    dialog(ctx, &state.snapshot())?;
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    | Action | Owner | Effect |
    |---|---|---|
    | `open_add_dialog` | Host | Shows the form and focuses the title field. |
    | `open_delete_dialog` | Host | Opens a confirmation dialog for the selected identifier. |
    | `close_dialog` | Host | Closes the dialog. |
    | `search_todos` | Host | Filters cached titles when the query changes. |
    | `edit_draft` | Host | Saves the current title while the dialog is open. |
    | `filter_todos` | Host | Renders selected rows from the local cache. |
    | `add_todo` | Server | Checks the submitted title, appends one item and sends a notification. |
    | `toggle_todo` | Server | Finds the item in the current list and changes its completion status. |
    | `confirm_delete` | Server | Removes the item. A retry returns the original removal position. |
    | `notify` | Web page or mobile host | Announces a successful add. |
    | `scroll_to_top` | Web page | Scrolls to the list header. |
    
    The browser boots its local dispatcher before it requests the initial frame.
    The server advertises its callable actions during the hello exchange.
    An action carries the triggering element's value and its own optional signed bytes.
    All three platforms render the same `<Modal><BottomSheet>…</BottomSheet></Modal>` tree. The input owns the submit action and supplies its current value.
    
    Only presentation actions consume signed state. The demo signer protects snapshots used by the local dispatcher.
    Its demo key is present in the module. The server rejects any attached presentation snapshot at its business endpoint.
    The server looks up each item in its own store. Each mutation returns a record change and publishes it at the same stream position.
    Each host applies the change once and updates its named list and count.
    Server and browser allocate node identifiers in separate ranges. Each producer keeps both page roots stable.

## User

> 4. Can a send report failure to a named action? The current trigger call returns an immediate error to its caller. It has no built-in per-request registration such as “deliver failure to host:submission_failed”. I would add that option to the action manager. The failure event should carry the request identifier, action name, endpoint, and typed reason. The transport reports what happened. The manager delivers the event to the originating view. Current return contract

if we can return an immediate failure with the transoport failure info,that is also good and better and lets us work with normal rust result

## Assistant

I’ll update the action contract to use Rust’s `Result` for known transport failures and distinguish socket acceptance from server confirmation.

Yes. The host action should be able to use ordinary Rust error handling: `send(...).await?`. If the transport knows the request failed, it returns `Err` with the cause, action name, and endpoint when available. No callback or named failure action is necessary.

For a socket, a successful write means the transport accepted the request. The Todo stays pending until the server confirms it. That distinction prevents a successful write from marking an item as saved too early.

I updated Feature 32 and passed this contract to the Todo agent. I also removed the notification byte marker and direct JavaScript action call. The new browser test checks that only the submitting client sees “Todo added.” JavaScript syntax passed. The browser regression run is pending. Both changes are pushed in `2fc68c85a`.

## Assistant

We need the **injected random source** and a **stable storage format**. We do not need to implement UUID bit handling in the Todo example.

`foundation_compact` already exports `Uuid`. Its `new_v4()` reads platform randomness directly and uses `Builder::from_random_bytes` to set the version and variant. `TodoId::generate` reads randomness from the host context so tests can supply predictable bytes. It then sets those same bits by hand. **That last step is duplication.** [Framework generator](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_compact/src/uuid.rs:23) · [Todo generator](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/shared/id.rs:17)

The rest of `id.rs` adds two behaviors: it rejects identifiers outside version four, and it serializes identifiers as strings. Its display implementation simply forwards to `Uuid`. Those details matter because existing backups and messages use string identifiers. The shared crate currently declares its UUID dependency without serialization support. [Todo parser and conversions](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/shared/id.rs:30) · [Dependency declaration](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_compact/Cargo.toml:22)

I would use `foundation_compact::uuid::Uuid` directly for `Todo.id`. The shared UUID module should expose a constructor that accepts 16 supplied random bytes. The app can fill those bytes from its injected source. Keep canonical text encoding at the storage and wire boundaries. Feature 32 asks for one stable UUID; it gives no reason to maintain a second UUID type solely to reject other versions on input.

I made no code changes.

[Conversion branch](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/bin/server.rs:44)

The bundling migration is also **incomplete**. `build.rs` generates the JavaScript bundles and stages the declared resources. But `resources.toml` lists only `art`, `app.js`, and the version file. At startup, the launcher still searches for the WebAssembly module, checks its header, and passes its path to the app. The server still registers many assets individually. I overstated how much of the Todo packaging had moved into the build. [Build script](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/build.rs:23) · [Resource list](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/resources.toml) · [Module lookup](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/bin/server.rs:8) · [Asset routes](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/server/assets.rs:13)

The intended boundary is simple: the build prepares every browser asset. Development reads the staged files. Release serves the embedded files. The launcher binds an address, constructs one app with its store and channel, and serves requests. Backup conversion belongs in a task. The seeded data fixture belongs in test support.

I updated Feature 27 to make those boundaries explicit. Only the specification changed in this turn. Commit `09347b3b1` is verified on `origin/resume/combined`. **The build helper reads `resources.toml`. The running app and the embed macro do not.** Todo’s `build.rs` calls `stage_from_cargo()`. That helper reads the manifest to select files, give them output paths, and filter them by platform. [Build call](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/build.rs:37) · [Manifest reader](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_resources/src/build.rs:507)

I introduced the manifest in Feature 3 to express three cases: copy an entire directory, include a browser-only file, and place a generated file at `app/version.txt`. That was my design choice. Your requirement was automatic packaging. It did not require application authors to maintain a separate manifest. [Feature 3 proposal](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/specifications/90-foundation-tasks/features/03-platform-resource-manager/feature.md:22) · [Todo manifest](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/resources.toml)

For the directory layout you described, **the directory itself can be the declaration**. Put `art/train.png` under the shared resource directory and preserve that path on each platform. Put browser files under `public/`. Have each generator write its output at its final relative path. The build helper stages those directories, and the server’s asset struct serves the resulting public tree.

That also addresses the current duplication: Todo lists some files in `resources.toml` and registers others individually in `assets.rs`. One directory convention and one asset handler would remove both lists. [Current asset registration](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/server/assets.rs:13)

`resources.toml` is already part of the build. `build.rs` calls the JavaScript bundler, then the resource stager. The stager reads `resources.toml`. The server’s `main()` never reads it. [Build pipeline](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/build.rs:23)

What **does** remain in `main()` is `web_module()`. It finds `ui_todo.wasm` and checks its header. That code predates the resource stager. When we added staging, we left the browser module on its old loading path. That was an incomplete migration. [Launcher code](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/bin/server.rs:8)

The build should compile the browser module, validate it, and stage it as `public/module.wasm`. The server should mount the asset handler once. Then `/module.wasm` works in development and release without `main()` knowing where Cargo produced the file.

    fn write_changed(path: &std::path::Path, contents: &str) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        match std::fs::metadata(path) {
            Ok(info)
                if info.len() == contents.len() as u64
                    && std::fs::read(path)? == contents.as_bytes() =>

                return Ok(())

            Ok(_) => {}
            Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {}

## Assistant

`prepare` exists because the Todo code intercepts the request **after the framework has already encoded it**. To show a pending Add or Delete, it opens the frame, reads the action input, saves the pending change, and rebuilds the request. That work belongs in the host action, before encoding. [Current implementation](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/shared/outbox.rs:128)

**Feature 32 now explicitly requires removing `prepare`.** The host action creates a typed value, saves the pending change, renders with `html!`, and submits that value. The framework serializes it. On receipt, the framework validates and deserializes the payload before calling the registered handler. Todo code should never inspect a frame header or a MessagePack byte prefix.

Only the specification changed. Commit `f7c64f777` is verified on `origin/resume/combined`. [Feature 32 contract](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/specifications/69-foundation-ui-v2/features/32-portable-view-targets/feature.md#action-composition-and-delivery-outcomes)

    fn list(state: &TodoApp) -> Html {
        let rows = state
            .items
            .iter()
            .filter(|item| match state.filter {
                Filter::All => true,
                Filter::Open => !item.done,
                Filter::Done => item.done,
            })
            .map(
                |item| match state.pending.get(&format!("delete:{}", item.id)) {
                    Some(pending) => pending_row(&item.text, "Deleting…", pending),
                    None => row(item),
                },
            );
        let additions = state
            .pending
            .values()
            .filter_map(|pending| match &pending.change {
                PendingChange::Add { title, .. } if state.filter != Filter::Done => {
                    Some(pending_row(title, "Pending", pending))
                }
                _ => None,
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        html! { <InsetList id="todo-list">{rows}{additions}</InsetList> }
    }
    
    fn pending_row(title: &str, status: &str, pending: &Pending) -> Html {
        let validation = pending.validation.as_deref();
        let retry = if validation.is_some() {
            match &pending.change {
                PendingChange::Add { id, .. } => Some(
                    html! {<Button value={format!("correct-add:{id}")} on:tap={open_add_dialog}>Edit title</Button>},
                ),
                PendingChange::Delete { .. } => None,
            }
        } else if pending.retry {
            Some(match &pending.change {
                PendingChange::Add { id, .. } => {
                    html! {<Button value={format!("retry-add:{id}")} on:tap={add_todo}>Try again</Button>}
                }
                PendingChange::Delete { id } => {
                    html! {<Button value={id.to_string()} on:tap={confirm_delete}>Try again</Button>}
                }
            })
        } else {
            None
        };
        let status = validation.unwrap_or(status);
        html! {<ChecklistRow class="animate-pulse opacity-70"><Text>{title}</Text><Text>{status}</Text>{retry}</ChecklistRow>}
    }

                    {cancel.clone()}
                </ConfirmationDialog>
            }
        });
        let tree = html! { <Stack id="dialog">
            <Either condition={state.add_dialog}>
                <Left>{confirmation}</Left>
                <Right><Modal a11y_label="New todo"><BottomSheet>
                    <SheetTitle>New todo</SheetTitle>
                    <TextInput placeholder="Todo title" a11y_label="Todo title" value={state.draft.as_str()} on:change={edit_draft} on:submit={add_todo}/>
                    {cancel.clone()}
                    <SubmitButton>Add</SubmitButton>
                </BottomSheet></Modal></Right>
            </Either>
        </Stack> };
        replace(ctx, "#dialog", tree)
    }
    
    #[action(host)]
    async fn open_add_dialog(ctx: &Context, event: Interaction<()>) -> ActionResult {
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    
    fn mutate(
        ctx: &Context,
        plan: impl FnOnce(&StoreState) -> Result<RecordChange, ErrorTrace<ActionError>>,
    ) -> ActionResult {
        let store = todo_store(ctx)?;
        let mut state = store
            .0
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner);
        let change = plan(&state)?;
        if let RecordChange::Remove(id) = &change {
            if let Some(&position) = state.removed.get(id) {
                return TodoDelivery::Committed { position, change }.send(ctx);
            }
        }
        commit(ctx, &mut state, change)?.send(ctx)
    }
    
    fn commit(
        ctx: &Context,
        state: &mut StoreState,
        change: RecordChange,
    ) -> Result<TodoDelivery, ErrorTrace<ActionError>> {
        let position = state
            .position
            .checked_add(1)
            .ok_or_else(|| error("Todo stream position exhausted"))?;
        #[cfg(all(feature = "server", not(target_family = "wasm")))]
        let position = match ctx.get::<crate::server::TodoFeed>() {
            Some(feed) => feed
                .publish(ctx.inner(), &change)
                .map_err(|e| error(&e.to_string()))?,
            None => position,
        };
        state.apply_change(&change);
        if let RecordChange::Remove(id) = &change {
            state.removed.insert(*id, position);
        }
        state.position = position;
        Ok(TodoDelivery::Committed { position, change })
    }

## Assistant

The clearest problem is `StoreState`. It holds server retry receipts alongside the client’s search results, dialog state, draft, and pending rows. Its `snapshot()` then copies items and pending entries for rendering. A reader tracing Add must understand both server history and screen state. [Current state model](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/shared/mod.rs:52)

I updated Feature 32 to cover the **whole shared directory**. The intended Add flow has three steps:

1. The host saves the pending Todo, renders the row, and sends typed input.
2. The server commits the Todo once and publishes the typed change.
3. The host applies the change, clears the pending entry, and updates the row and count.

The plan also calls for one dialog state, typed retry inputs, and removal of the custom outbox and frame handling. It preserves snapshots where they serve a specific purpose, such as keeping search results fixed during a peer update.

Only the specification changed. Commit `d2c1993e1` is verified on `origin/resume/combined`. [Shared Todo simplification criteria](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/specifications/69-foundation-ui-v2/features/32-portable-view-targets/feature.md#review-the-whole-shared-todo-example)

## Assistant

**`include_str!(env!("EWE_RESOURCE_NAMES"))` embeds a list of filenames.** The build helper writes one declared resource name per line and sets `EWE_RESOURCE_NAMES` to that file’s path. At compile time, `include_str!` reads the list into a string. At startup, `register` loops over those names and registers a route for each file. The asset bytes come from disk or the `embedded` callback. [Build helper](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_resources/src/build.rs:534) · [Registration loop](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_resources/src/server.rs:35)

**`#[always_embed]` exists because the application and the procedural macro can use different build profiles.** The outer `#[cfg(not(debug_assertions))]` selects the struct using the application’s settings. The derive checks its own `debug_assertions`. `#[always_embed]` forces the derive to include the bytes when those settings differ. The `None` argument disables the optional `/` alias for an index document. [Macro selection](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_macros/src/embedders.rs:720)

The design problem is that `register` asks the application for five pieces of information when the **resource instance should own the lookup**. The intended application call is as small as this:

```rust
router.mount(StaticFileHandler::from_resources(PackagedResources))?;
```

That is a proposed interface. The framework should select disk or embedded storage, resolve the packaged names, and serve binary content with the correct media type. Todo should declare the resource type and mount it once.

I updated both features to require that boundary. Only documentation changed. Commit `aaee8a8c5` is verified on `origin/resume/combined`. ## Assistant

We don’t need a separate filename list. It exists because the current `register` function creates one route per file. That was an implementation choice. [Registration loop](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_resources/src/server.rs:42)

The simpler design mounts one static handler after the application routes. When a browser requests `/bundle.js`, the handler asks `PackagedResources` for `bundle.js`. In development, the provider reads the file from the staged public directory. In release, it looks up the embedded bytes. An unknown name returns `404`.

`resources.toml` still tells the **build** what to package. The **server** needs only the resulting resource provider. That removes `EWE_RESOURCE_NAMES`, `include_str!`, and the per-file registration loop from the serving path.

- **One build hook and one asset handler.** The framework builds and stages the browser assets. The launcher loses module discovery and per-file registration.
- **Typed actions and simple pending storage.** Host actions save pending changes and call the server. The redesign removes the custom outbox, transport interception, and application frame parsing.

Feature 37 names the functions and flags to remove. Its twelve acceptance checks cover both behavior and removal from production code. Features 26, 27, and 32 now point to it.

## Assistant

The example exposes framework internals because we built the Todo browser startup by joining several low-level interfaces. We left that integration in the app.

**`web.rs` does two jobs.** It installs Todo’s cache and actions. It also translates action scopes into numbers, passes names through raw pointers, and defines storage callbacks for JavaScript. Only the first job describes Todo. The framework can register action declarations and install the selected storage provider for every browser app. [Rust startup](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/src/web.rs:8)

**`app.js` does three jobs.** It loads the module, starts the rendering and action runtimes, then replaces transport methods to support optimistic submissions. That last step explains the frame parsing and acknowledgement map. Todo intercepts requests after encoding, then tries to recover which user operation each reply belongs to. A typed host submission action and framework-owned request tracking remove the reason for that code. [Browser startup](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/web/app.js:35) · [Transport override](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/web/app.js:127)

I updated Feature 37 around the three operations you described. The proposed application code is:

```js
const module = await loadWasm("/module.wasm");
const app = createApp({ module, mount, initialRoute, storage });
await app.boot();
```

The loader checks the response status before compilation. A missing module reports its address and status. An invalid binary reports the compiler cause. The app can register a custom transport before boot. The runtime owns the handshake, framing, socket replies, and recovery. Application code sends ordinary JavaScript objects or typed Rust values.

`foundation_db` owns the proposed browser storage adapters for `localStorage` and IndexedDB, alongside the existing memory provider. `foundation_wasm_ui` installs the selected provider. Todo supplies its storage choice and namespace.

Only the specification changed. Commit `7e74ac879` is verified on `origin/resume/combined`. [Feature 37 browser startup contract](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/specifications/69-foundation-ui-v2/features/37-todo-server-build-and-state/feature.md#browser-startup-and-storage)

            let prefixed = self.prefixed_key(key);

## Assistant

Yes. `foundation_db` has **Rust implementations of storage traits that call JavaScript** through `wasm-bindgen`. For example, `KVWasmStorage` implements `KeyValueStore` using Cloudflare’s `KVNamespace`. `D1WasmStorage` also implements `KeyValueStore`. These providers run in Cloudflare Workers. I found no `localStorage` or IndexedDB provider in the crate. [Cloudflare key-value provider](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_db/src/wasm/wasm_storage/kv_wasm.rs:25) · [D1 provider](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_db/src/wasm/wasm_storage/d1_wasm.rs:314)

**I would keep the browser providers in `foundation_db`.** It already owns the contract that a caller needs: `get`, `set`, `delete`, and prefix-based `list_keys`. A browser app should be able to use that contract without depending on the user interface runtime. [Key-value storage trait](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_db/src/core/storage_provider.rs:341)

I would give each crate a clear job:

- **`foundation_db`** implements `LocalStorage` and `IndexedDb` as optional browser backends. Their browser bindings, serialization, and storage errors belong beside those implementations.
- **`foundation_wasm_ui`** installs the selected provider and namespace during `app.boot()`.
- **`ui_todo`** reads and writes typed pending records through the installed store. It needs no JavaScript storage callbacks.

For Todo specifically, I would use **IndexedDB** for persistent pending writes because separate tabs can update records transactionally. The memory provider fits temporary sessions and tests. `localStorage` remains useful for simple settings.

## Assistant

`App.swift` has **one Todo screen and three ways to send its actions**. Each launch selects one branch. The iPhone tests pass those settings into the app so the same screen can exercise different transports. [App.swift:23](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/ios/todo_server/App/App.swift:23) · [Test launch settings](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/ios/todo_server/UITests/TodoTests.swift:200)

| Launch setting | How the screen sends actions |
|---|---|
| `EWE_TODO_RPC=1` | Uses Connect remote procedure calls (RPC) at the server address. |
| `EWE_TODO_SOCKET=1` | Sends actions over WebSocket at `/socket`. |
| Neither setting | Uses the default Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) action transport. |

**The transport choice explains the branch. It does not require repeating the setup.** All three branches load `initial`, create the same persistent Todo core, install `BundleResourceSource`, and register `host:apply_todo_delivery`. Even the pending storage path is already computed once before the branch. [App.swift:19](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/ios/todo_server/App/App.swift:19)

The duplication comes from calling three `ServerScreen` initializers and copying the same setup closure into each call. The cleaner interface would let the app select one transport configuration, then construct `ServerScreen` once with one core factory. That preserves all three test paths and gives future setup changes one place to land. [ServerScreen initializers](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/mobile/ios/Sources/EweUI/ServerScreen.swift:39)

Yes. I would let the app select its action transport once at startup. The iPhone framework already has a `ConnectionManager` that manages connections. The duplication comes from `App.swift`: it selects among three `ServerScreen` constructors and repeats the same Todo setup in each branch. [App.swift](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/examples/ui_todo/ios/todo_server/App/App.swift:22) · [ConnectionManager.swift](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/mobile/ios/Sources/EweUI/ConnectionManager.swift:23)

**For a Todo action**, selecting WebSocket already uses the native networking stack. Rust sends the action through `HostTransport`. Swift’s `SocketActionConnection` uses the connection manager, and `URLSession` opens the WebSocket to the server. The initial page still loads through Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP). The selection controls how the app sends **actions**. [ServerScreen.swift](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/mobile/ios/Sources/EweUI/ServerScreen.swift:60) · [SocketActionConnection.swift](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/mobile/ios/Sources/EweUI/SocketActionConnection.swift:8) · [Channels.swift](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/mobile/ios/Sources/EweUI/Channels.swift:91)

**For an independent connection**, such as a game talking to its own server, I would expose a native WebSocket service to Rust. The game could open its endpoint, send and receive its own messages, and close the connection. The Todo action connection expects framework messages. The `HostTransport` passed to Todo exposes action requests. It gives Todo no general-purpose socket handle.

**Remote procedure call (RPC) and WebSocket answer different questions.**

| Term | What it gives the app |
|---|---|
| RPC | A way to call a named operation on a server, such as adding a todo, and receive a result or error. |
| WebSocket | An open connection where either side can send messages. The application protocol defines what each message means. |

RPC can run over WebSocket. In this app, the option called “RPC” specifically selects **Connect RPC over HTTP**. The WebSocket option sends framework action messages over a native socket. Both can carry the same Todo action. [ServerScreen.swift](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/mobile/ios/Sources/EweUI/ServerScreen.swift:39)

I would give `ServerScreen` one transport setting and one Todo setup function. The framework would select the sender. Then `submit_todo` could call `server:add_todo` the same way with every transport.

                    override suspend fun send(request: ByteArray): ByteArray? = rpc.exchange(request)
                }
            }
            val binding = host.attach(createCore(sender), factory, manager, viewDataAction)
            val hello = socket?.let { binding.helloFor(it.requestTag) } ?: binding.hello()
            connection.configure(hello)
            host.apply(requireNotNull(sender.send(hello)) { "Missing server capabilities" }, "capabilities")
            host.loadView { connection.initial(initialPath) }
        }
    }
    
    /** Render a local screen. The factory transfers ownership of the new core to this host. */
    @Composable
    fun LocalEweScreen(
        createCore: () -> NativeCore,
        initialFrame: suspend (NativeCore) -> ByteArray,
        modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
        theme: EweTheme = EweTheme(),
    ) {
        EweHost(emptyList(), "Loading…", modifier, theme) { host ->
            val core = createCore()
            host.attach(core, null)
            host.applyInitial(initialFrame(core))
        }
    }
    
    @Composable
    private fun EweHost(
        config: List<Any>,
        loading: String,
        modifier: Modifier,
        theme: EweTheme,
        start: suspend (ScreenHost) -> Unit,
    ) {
        val view = LocalView.current
        val registry = remember { BehaviourRegistry.standard }
        val setup by rememberUpdatedState(start)
        var current by remember { mutableStateOf<ScreenHost?>(null) }
        DisposableEffect(view, config) {
            val store = NodeStore(
                MainGapTimer(), commands = SystemCommandHost(view), supportsBehaviour = registry::supports,
            )
            val host = ScreenHost(store, loading)
            current = host
            host.start(setup)
            onDispose { host.close() }
        }
        Surface(modifier.fillMaxSize()) {
            Column {
                val host = current
                val status = host?.status ?: loading
                if (status.isNotEmpty()) {
                    Text(status)
                    if (host?.store?.recovery != null && status != loading) {
                        androidx.compose.material3.TextButton(onClick = { host.start { it.retryView() } }) { Text("Retry") }
                    }
                }
                host?.bridge?.let { EweScreen(host.store, it, behaviours = registry, theme = theme, graphics = host.graphics) }
            }
        }
    }
    
    private class ScreenHost(val store: NodeStore, private val loading: String) : AutoCloseable {
        private val scope = CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.Main.immediate)
        private val cleanup = mutableListOf<() -> Unit>(store::close)
        var status by mutableStateOf(loading)
            private set
        var graphics: (() -> io.github.ewe_studios.ewe.core.NativeGraphics)? = null
            private set
        var bridge by mutableStateOf<EventBridge?>(null)
            private set
    
        init {
            store.onError = { code, message -> status = "$code $message" }
        }
    
        fun start(setup: suspend (ScreenHost) -> Unit) {
            scope.launch {
                try {
                    setup(this@ScreenHost)
                } catch (cancel: CancellationException) {
                    throw cancel
                } catch (error: Exception) {
                    status = error.message ?: "Screen setup failed"
                }
            }
        }
    
        fun onClose(clean: () -> Unit) {
            cleanup.add(clean)
        }

    fn write_changed(path: &std::path::Path, contents: &str) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        match std::fs::metadata(path) {
            Ok(info)
                if info.len() == contents.len() as u64
                    && std::fs::read(path)? == contents.as_bytes() =>
            {
                return Ok(())
            }
            Ok(_) => {}
            Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {}
            Err(error) => return Err(error),
        }
        std::fs::write(path, contents)
    }

    fn expand(attr: TokenStream, item: TokenStream, is_test: bool) -> TokenStream {
        let args = match parse_args(attr) {
            Ok(args) => args,
            Err(err) => return err.to_compile_error(),
        };
        let func = match syn::parse2::<syn::ItemFn>(item) {
            Ok(func) => func,
            Err(err) => return err.to_compile_error(),
        };
        // An `async fn` body is accepted (feature 00-F3): it is driven to completion
        // via `block_on_future` (from_future + run-to-completion), so the body's
        // `.await` points park on the valtron engine (Decision 00 Level 1). A sync fn
        // keeps today's expansion byte-for-byte.
        let is_async = func.sig.asyncness.is_some();
        if !func.sig.inputs.is_empty() {
            return syn::Error::new_spanned(&func.sig.inputs, "#[valtron] functions take no arguments")

        }

        //
        // NOTE: this only catches `#[test]` when it sits immediately on the fn with
        // no other proc-macro attr between it and `#[valtron_test]`. Outer attrs
        // (e.g. `#[serial]`) expand first and hoist `#[test]` into a wrapper before
        // we run, so we never see it. The real guarantee is the usage contract in
        // the module docs: `#[valtron_test]` REPLACES `#[test]`; never stack them.
        let attrs: Vec<&syn::Attribute> = func
            .attrs
            .iter()

            .collect();

        // drives the (possibly async) body to completion. Strip `async` from the

    fn rejects_ambiguous_or_malformed_records() {
        let dir = tempdir().unwrap();
        let input = dir.path().join("input");
        let output = dir.path().join("new");
        let row = |id: Value| json!({"id":id,"text":"title","done":true});
        let duplicate_creation = |id| json!({"id":id,"text":"","done":false,"creation_id":EXISTING});
        for data in [
            json!([row(json!(0))]),
            json!([row(json!(1)), row(json!(1))]),
            json!([row(json!(1)), row(json!(EXISTING))]),
            json!([duplicate_creation(1), duplicate_creation(2)]),
            json!([{"id":1,"text":"","done":false,"creation_id":"invalid"}]),
            json!([{"id":1,"text":"","done":false,"other":true}]),
        ] {
            fs::write(&input, data.to_string()).unwrap();
            assert!(!convert(&input, &output).status.success());
            assert!(!output.exists());
            rejects_restore(&input);
        }
        for invalid in [
            json!([row(json!(EXISTING)), row(json!(EXISTING))]).to_string(),
            json!([{"id":EXISTING,"creation_id":EXISTING,"done":true,"text":""}]).to_string(),
            String::from("[] trailing data"),
        ] {
            fs::write(&input, invalid).unwrap();
            rejects_restore(&input);
            assert!(!convert(&input, &output).status.success());
            assert!(!output.exists());
        }
        fs::write(&input, "[]").unwrap();
        assert!(convert(&input, &output).status.success());
