    /** Send action bytes and deliver later replies to the originating screen. */
    class SocketActionConnection(
        connections: ConnectionManager, endpoint: String, private val onReply: (ByteArray) -> Unit,
        private val onFailure: (Throwable) -> Unit, private val handshakeTimeoutMillis: Long = 60_000,
    ) : HostTransport, AutoCloseable {
        val requestTag = connections.nextTag()
        @Volatile private var stream: ULong? = null
        @Volatile private var caps: CompletableDeferred<ByteArray>? = null
    
        private fun packet(bytes: ByteArray): Frame {
            val input = ByteBuffer.wrap(bytes).order(ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN)
            require(Frame.FrameBufferHasIdentifier(input))
            return Frame.getRootAsFrame(input)
        }
    
        private var hello: ByteArray? = null
        private var reconnect = false
        private fun negotiateAgain() { hello?.let { handle.send(it) } }
        private val handle: ewe.ui.runtime.ConnectionHandle = connections.acquire(LiveTransport.WebSocket, endpoint,
            accept = { bytes ->
                val frame = packet(bytes)
                val body = frame.kind(FrameMessage()) as FrameMessage
                val control = if (body.messagesLength > 0) body.messages(0)?.control?.caps else null
                if (control == null) body.ack != 0uL && frame.streamId == stream
                else control.requestTag == requestTag
            },
            onOpen = { if (reconnect) { reconnect = false; negotiateAgain() } },
            onError = { cause -> reconnect = true; stream = null; caps?.completeExceptionally(cause); onFailure(cause) },
            receive = { bytes ->
                val frame = packet(bytes)
                val body = frame.kind(FrameMessage()) as FrameMessage
                val control = if (body.messagesLength > 0) body.messages(0)?.control?.caps else null
                if (control == null) onReply(bytes) else {
                    stream = if (control.status == CapsStatus.Ok) control.streamId else null
                    if (caps?.complete(bytes) != true) onReply(bytes)
                }
            })
    
        override suspend fun send(request: ByteArray): ByteArray? {
            val frame = packet(request)
            val body = frame.kind(FrameRequest()) as FrameRequest
            if (body.hello == null) {
                if (stream != frame.streamId) throw IOException("Action connection needs a handshake")
                handle.send(request)
                return null
            }
            val result = CompletableDeferred<ByteArray>()
            synchronized(this) {
                check(caps == null && body.hello?.requestTag == requestTag)
                caps = result
                hello = request.copyOf()
            }
            return try {
                handle.send(request)
                withTimeout(handshakeTimeoutMillis) { result.await() }
            } finally { caps = null }
        }
    
        override fun close() {
            caps?.completeExceptionally(IOException("Action socket closed"))
            handle.close()
        }
    }
        return body.ack != 0 && stream == frame.streamId
      }
    
      private func receive(_ bytes: Data) {
        guard let frame = try? packet(bytes), let body = frame.kind(type: ewe_ui_FrameMessage.self) else { return }
        if body.messagesCount > 0, let caps = body.messages(at: 0)?.control?.caps {
          stream = caps.status == .ok ? caps.streamId : nil
          if waiting == nil { onReply(bytes) } else { finish(.success(bytes)) }
        } else { onReply(bytes) }
      }
    
      private func finish(_ result: Result<Data, Error>) {
        let reply = waiting
        waiting = nil
        reply?.resume(with: result)
      }
    
      public func send(request: Data) async throws -> Data? {
        let frame = try packet(request)
        guard let handle, frame.kindType == .framerequest,
          let call = frame.kind(type: ewe_ui_FrameRequest.self) else { throw ConnectionError.closed }
        guard let hello = call.hello else {
          guard stream == frame.streamId else { throw ConnectionError.closed }
          try await handle.send(request)
          return nil
        }
        guard waiting == nil, hello.requestTag == requestTag else { throw ConnectionError.invalidEndpoint }
        self.hello = request
        let deadline = Task {
          try await Task.sleep(for: timeout)
          finish(.failure(URLError(.timedOut)))
        }
        defer { deadline.cancel() }
        return try await withTaskCancellationHandler {
          try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { reply in
            waiting = reply
            Task {
              do { try await handle.send(request) } catch { finish(.failure(error)) }
            }
          }
        } onCancel: { Task { @MainActor in self.finish(.failure(CancellationError())) } }
      }
    
      public func close() {
        finish(.failure(ConnectionError.closed))
        handle?.close()
        handle = nil
        stream = nil
      }
    }
    #endif

    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Returns a view or serialization error.
    pub fn starter_view(ctx: &Context, count: usize) -> ActionResult {
        full_view(ctx, ctx.receiver(), &starter_tree(count), None::<&()>)
    }
    
    pub(crate) fn starter_tree(count: usize) -> Html {
        html! { <Stack><Text>Open todos</Text><Text id="open-count">{count}</Text>
        <Button on:tap={refresh_count}>Refresh</Button></Stack> }
    }
    
    #[action(server)]
    async fn refresh_count(ctx: &Context, _event: Interaction<()>) -> ActionResult {
        let store = ctx
            .get::<TodoStore>()
            .ok_or_else(|| error("Missing todo store"))?;
        starter_view(
            ctx,
            store
                .snapshot()
                .items
                .iter()
                .filter(|item| !item.done)
                .count(),
        )
    }

        internal suspend fun verifyIndependentSocket(base: String, echo: String) = withContext(Dispatchers.Main) {
            System.setProperty("uniffi.component.foundation_ui_native.libraryOverride", "ui_todo")
            val client = OkHttpClient()
            val manager = OkHttpChannelFactory(client, base.toHttpUrl()).connectionManager()
            val reply = CompletableDeferred<ByteArray>()
            try {
                SocketActionConnection(manager, "/socket", { reply.complete(it) }, { reply.completeExceptionally(it) }).use { sender ->

                        core.applyCapsFrame(requireNotNull(sender.send(core.helloFor(sender.requestTag))))
                        core.installWebSockets(AppWebSockets(client))
                        core.openWebSocket(echo).use { socket ->

                            socket.send(text)
                            check(socket.receive() == text)
                            val bytes = byteArrayOf(0, -1)
                            socket.send(SocketMessage.Binary(bytes))
                            check((socket.receive() as SocketMessage.Binary).value.contentEquals(bytes))
                            socket.closeSocket()
                        }
                        core.trigger("server:refresh_count", EventInput(0u, "tap", "", false, 0u, byteArrayOf()))
                        val store = NodeStore(GapTimer { _, _ -> Cancel {} })
                        check(store.receive(reply.await()))
                        check(store.nodes.any { it.text == "Open todos" })
                    }
                }
            } finally { manager.close() }
        }

## User

but rust could if it wanted open it on its own or does it need native context? just a question? in general with emvedded rist lib?

## Assistant

Yes. A Rust library embedded in an iPhone or Android app can open its own WebSocket. It runs inside the app’s process and uses the app’s network permissions. It does not need Swift, Kotlin, or a framework context to open the connection.

The project already has a Rust client in `foundation_netio`. Rust code can use that client to connect, send messages, receive replies, and close the socket. [Rust WebSocket connector](/Volumes/Outside/Dev/ewe_platform/.worktrees/combined/backends/foundation_netio/src/websocket/native/http_client_connector.rs)

The new `AppWebSocket::open` needs a context **because that interface asks the host to open the socket**. On iPhone, the host uses `URLSession`. On Android, it uses `OkHttp`. That is a framework design choice. For a Rust caller, the context also lets a test supply a fake connection.

        ## Independent native WebSocket service
        
        Rust actions can open a host WebSocket through `AppWebSocket::open`.
        Swift uses URLSession. Kotlin uses OkHttp. Each socket has its own lifetime.
        The iPhone simulator and Android emulator pass the independent socket test.

    //! Identity of a Todo record across hosts, storage, and retries.
    use foundation_compact::uuid::Uuid;
    use foundation_context::{env::Env, Ctx};
    use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    use std::{fmt, str::FromStr};
    
    /// A version four universally unique identifier (UUID).
    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    #[serde(try_from = "String", into = "String")]
    pub struct TodoId(Uuid);
    
    impl TodoId {
        /// Generate an identifier using the entropy source installed by the host.
        ///
        /// # Errors
        /// Returns an error if the entropy source is missing or fails.
        pub fn generate(ctx: &Ctx) -> Result<Self, String> {
            let mut bytes = [0; 16];
            ctx.get::<Env>()
                .ok_or("Missing Todo entropy source")?
                .entropy()
                .fill(&mut bytes)
                .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
            bytes[6] = bytes[6] & 0x0f | 0x40;
            bytes[8] = bytes[8] & 0x3f | 0x80;
            Ok(Self(Uuid::from_bytes(bytes)))
        }
    }
    
    impl FromStr for TodoId {
        type Err = &'static str;
    
        fn from_str(value: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
            let invalid = "Expected a version four Todo UUID";
            let id = Uuid::try_parse(value).map_err(|_| invalid)?;
            if id.get_version_num() != 4 || id.as_bytes()[8] & 0xc0 != 0x80 {
                return Err(invalid);
            }
            Ok(Self(id))
        }
    }
    
    impl fmt::Display for TodoId {
        fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            self.0.fmt(f)
        }
    }
    
    impl TryFrom<String> for TodoId {
        type Error = &'static str;
        fn try_from(value: String) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
            value.parse()
        }
    }
    
    impl From<TodoId> for String {
        fn from(value: TodoId) -> Self {
            value.to_string()
        }
    }

    //! Version-4 Universally Unique Identifier (UUID) generation.
    //!
    //! This module wraps the `uuid` crate's formatting API only. The 16 random bytes
    //! come from [`crate::entropy`] (the native OS random source, or
    //! `crypto.getRandomValues` on wasm), never from the `uuid` crate's own
    //! `getrandom`/`js`/`rng` backends. Callers that need a UUID use this module so
    //! the entropy source stays in one place (rule 11).
    
    use ::uuid::Builder;
    
    pub use ::uuid::Uuid;
    
    /// Generate a random version-4 UUID from the platform entropy source.
    ///
    /// The 16 bytes come from [`crate::entropy::fill`]; [`Builder::from_random_bytes`]
    /// sets the version-4 and RFC 4122 variant bits. The result is a plain value, so
    /// callers that need the canonical string call `.to_string()`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns [`crate::entropy::Error`] if the platform entropy source is
    /// unavailable.
    pub fn new_v4() -> Result<Uuid, crate::entropy::Error> {
        let mut bytes = [0u8; 16];
        crate::entropy::fill(&mut bytes)?;
        Ok(Builder::from_random_bytes(bytes).into_uuid())
    }

    //! Cross-platform substrate: time + vendored entropy + RNG + scru128 IDs.
    //!
    //! On `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `std::time` panics — this crate provides drop-in
    //! replacements backed by JavaScript's `Performance.now()` and `Date.now()`.
    //! On all other targets (native, emscripten, WASI), re-exports `std::time`.
    //!
    //! On `wasm32-unknown-unknown` the JavaScript calls (time and entropy) go through
    //! one of two backends: `wasm-bindgen` glue (the default feature) or, with the
    //! `host-abi` feature, plain `abi` host imports that `foundation_wasm`'s
    //! `foundation-wasm.js` runtime implements, so the module carries no wasm-bindgen
    //! imports. `host-abi` wins when both are enabled.
    //!
    //! Also provides:
    //! - **`entropy`** — vendored OS entropy (getrandom backends for all targets)
    //! - **`rng`** — ChaCha-based CSPRNG seeded from entropy (no external rand/getrandom)
    //! - **`ids`** — scru128 monotonic IDs (folded from `foundation_rng`)
    //! - **`hash`** — deterministic, wasm-safe content hashing (foldhash, no getrandom)
    //!
    //! # Usage
    //!
    //! ```
    //! use foundation_compact::Instant;
    //!
    //! let now = Instant::now();
    //! let elapsed = now.elapsed();
    //! ```
    
    // ─── Time ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    [target.'cfg(all(target_family = "wasm", target_os = "wasi", target_env = "p3"))'.dependencies]

    #
    # `tracing` + `tracing-subscriber` power the wasm `console` trace writer (see

    [target.'cfg(all(target_family = "wasm", any(target_os = "unknown", target_os = "none")))'.dependencies]
    wasm-bindgen = { workspace = true, optional = true }

    //! The entropy effect: random bytes for keys, tokens and seeds.
    //!
    //! The entropy source is not the shared random number generator (RNG) of
    //! [`Ctx`](crate::Ctx). A caller can draw from that stream too, so a key must
    //! not come from it.
    
    use foundation_compact::entropy;
    use foundation_compact::rng::{ChaCha12Rng, Rng, SeedableRng};
    
    use crate::sync::Mutex;
    
    /// The source of random bytes for keys, tokens and seeds.
    pub trait EntropySource: Send + Sync + 'static {
        /// Fills `dest` with random bytes.
        ///
        /// # Errors
        /// The platform source failed. A caller must not continue with a
        /// half-filled buffer.
        fn fill(&self, dest: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), entropy::Error>;
    }
    
    /// The operating-system source. Native: `getrandom`/`getentropy`. wasm:
    /// `crypto.getRandomValues`.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
    pub struct OsEntropy;
    
    impl EntropySource for OsEntropy {
        fn fill(&self, dest: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), entropy::Error> {
            foundation_compact::entropy::fill(dest)
        }
    }
    
    /// A seeded source. The same seed gives the same bytes on every run and every
    /// platform.
    ///
    /// The type is available in every build, so a test crate needs no extra
    /// feature. Use it only in a test or in the deterministic simulation harness.
    pub struct SeededEntropy {
        seed: u64,
        rng: Mutex<ChaCha12Rng>,
    }
    
    impl SeededEntropy {
        /// A source from `seed`. It cannot fail.
        #[must_use]
        pub fn new(seed: u64) -> Self {
            Self {
                seed,
                rng: Mutex::new(ChaCha12Rng::seed_from_u64(seed)),
            }
        }

        }

    impl EntropySource for SeededEntropy {
        fn fill(&self, dest: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), entropy::Error> {
            // A poisoned lock still holds a valid generator. Recover it; the wasm
            // lock error type differs from the std one, so a `match` serves both.
            let mut rng = match self.rng.lock() {
                Ok(guard) => guard,
                Err(poisoned) => poisoned.into_inner(),
            };
            rng.fill_bytes(dest);
            Ok(())
        }
    }
    //! The optional `Env` typed entry of [`Ctx`](crate::Ctx).
    //!
    //! `Ctx` carries three engine-minimum elements: the clock, the config and the
    //! seeded random number generator. This module adds the three remaining ambient
    //! effects in one optional entry:
    //!
    //! - the [`timer`], which waits until a deadline on the clock of the `Ctx`;
    //! - the [`entropy`] source, which gives random bytes for keys and tokens;
    //! - the [`ids`] source, which gives new sortable IDs.
    //!
    //! One bundle gives one `get` and one error. A `Ctx::get::<T>()` keys on one
    //! `TypeId`, so a trait object cannot be an entry on its own.
    //!
    //! The `Env` holds no clock. The clock is an engine-minimum element of `Ctx`
    //! (spec 76), and a second clock would break the deterministic simulation law
    //! "one clock per run". The `Env` also holds no `Ctx`, so the map cannot close
    //! an `Arc` cycle.
    
    pub mod entropy;
    pub mod ids;
    pub mod timer;
    
    use std::sync::Arc;

    /// The side-effect sources that are not engine-minimum elements of
    /// [`Ctx`](crate::Ctx).
    ///
    /// Clone is cheap: each field is an `Arc`. The `Ctx` holds one `Env` as a typed
    /// entry.
    #[derive(Clone)]
    pub struct Env {
        timer: Arc<dyn Timer>,
        entropy: Arc<dyn EntropySource>,
        ids: Arc<dyn IdSource>,
    }
    
    impl Env {
        /// An `Env` from three sources.
        #[must_use]
        pub fn new(
            timer: Arc<dyn Timer>,
            entropy: Arc<dyn EntropySource>,
            ids: Arc<dyn IdSource>,
        ) -> Self {
            Self {
                timer,
                entropy,
                ids,
            }
        }
    
        /// The timer.
        #[must_use]
        pub fn timer(&self) -> Arc<dyn Timer> {
            Arc::clone(&self.timer)
        }
    
        /// The entropy source.
        #[must_use]
        pub fn entropy(&self) -> Arc<dyn EntropySource> {
            Arc::clone(&self.entropy)
        }
    
        /// The ID source.
        #[must_use]
        pub fn ids(&self) -> Arc<dyn IdSource> {
            Arc::clone(&self.ids)
        }
    
        /// A copy with a different timer. The other two members stay shared.
        #[must_use]
        pub fn with_timer(self, timer: Arc<dyn Timer>) -> Self {
            Self { timer, ..self }

    //! Version-4 Universally Unique Identifier (UUID) generation.
    //!
    //! This module wraps the `uuid` crate's formatting API only. The 16 random bytes
    //! come from [`crate::entropy`] (the native OS random source, or
    //! `crypto.getRandomValues` on wasm), never from the `uuid` crate's own
    //! `getrandom`/`js`/`rng` backends. Callers that need a UUID use this module so
    //! the entropy source stays in one place (rule 11).
    
    use ::uuid::Builder;

    /// Generate a random version-4 UUID from the platform entropy source.
    ///
    /// The 16 bytes come from [`crate::entropy::fill`]; [`Builder::from_random_bytes`]
    /// sets the version-4 and RFC 4122 variant bits. The result is a plain value, so
    /// callers that need the canonical string call `.to_string()`.

    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns [`crate::entropy::Error`] if the platform entropy source is
    /// unavailable.
    pub fn new_v4() -> Result<Uuid, crate::entropy::Error> {
        Ok(UuidV4::from_entropy(crate::entropy::fill)?.0)
    }

    //! Check version four identifiers with caller-supplied entropy.
    use foundation_compact::uuid::UuidV4;
    
    #[test]
    fn injected_entropy_sets_the_version_and_variant() {
        let id = UuidV4::from_entropy(|bytes| {
            bytes.fill(0xff);
            Ok::<_, ()>(())
        })
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(id.to_string(), "ffffffff-ffff-4fff-bfff-ffffffffffff");
        assert_eq!(id.to_string().parse(), Ok(id));
        assert!(
            "ffffffff-ffff-1fff-bfff-ffffffffffff"
                .parse::<UuidV4>()
                .is_err()
        );
        assert!(
            "ffffffff-ffff-4fff-ffff-ffffffffffff"
                .parse::<UuidV4>()
                .is_err()
        );
        assert_eq!(
            UuidV4::from_entropy(|_| Err("unavailable")),
            Err("unavailable")
        );
    }
    
    #[cfg(feature = "serde")]
    #[test]
    fn wire_format_uses_text() {
        let value = "ffffffff-ffff-4fff-bfff-ffffffffffff";
        serde_test::assert_tokens(
            &value.parse::<UuidV4>().unwrap(),
            &[serde_test::Token::Str(value)],
        );
    }

    async fn change_pending<T>(
        ctx: &Context,
        change: impl FnOnce(&mut Entries) -> Result<(bool, T), ErrorTrace<ActionError>>,
    ) -> Result<T, ErrorTrace<ActionError>> {
        let store = todo_store(ctx)?;
        let outbox = ctx
            .get::<Outbox>()
            .ok_or_else(|| error("Missing Todo pending storage"))?;
        let mut initialized = outbox.initialized.lock().await;
        let mut entries = if *initialized {
            store
                .0
                .lock()
                .unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner)
                .pending
                .clone()
        } else {
            let bytes = outbox.storage.load().await.map_err(|e| error(&e))?;
            if bytes.is_empty() {
                Entries::new()
            } else {
                let mut entries: Entries =
                    serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).map_err(|e| error(&e.to_string()))?;
                for entry in entries.values_mut() {
                    entry.retry = true;
                }
                entries
            }
        };
        let (changed, result) = change(&mut entries)?;
        if changed {
            outbox
                .storage
                .save(serde_json::to_vec(&entries).map_err(|e| error(&e.to_string()))?)
                .await
                .map_err(|e| error(&e))?;
        }
        store
            .0
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner)
            .pending = entries;
        *initialized = true;
        Ok(result)
    }

    pub(super) struct Reconciled {
        pub(super) changed: bool,
        pub(super) added: bool,
    }
    
    pub(super) async fn reconcile(
        ctx: &Context,
        snapshot: bool,
    ) -> Result<Reconciled, ErrorTrace<ActionError>> {
        let store = todo_store(ctx)?;
        let (result, deleted) = change_pending(ctx, |entries| {
            let state = store
                .0
                .lock()
                .unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner);
            let before = entries.len();
            let mut added = false;
            let mut deleted = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
            entries.retain(|_, pending| {
                let accepted = confirmed(&state, &pending.change, snapshot);
                if let PendingChange::Delete { id } = pending.change {
                    if accepted {
                        deleted.insert(id);
                    }
                }
                if let PendingChange::Add { id, .. } = pending.change {
                    added |= accepted && !state.retired_ids.contains(&id);
                }
                !accepted
            });
            let changed = entries.len() != before;
            Ok((changed, (Reconciled { changed, added }, deleted)))
        })
        .await?;
        if !deleted.is_empty() {
            let mut state = store
                .0
                .lock()
                .unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner);
            if let Some(rows) = &mut state.search_rows {
                rows.retain(|row| !deleted.contains(&row.id));
            }
        }
        Ok(result)
    }
    
    fn confirmed(state: &StoreState, change: &PendingChange, snapshot: bool) -> bool {
        match change {
            PendingChange::Add { id, .. } => {
                state.retired_ids.contains(id) || state.items.iter().any(|row| row.id == *id)
            }
            PendingChange::Delete { id } => {
                state.removed.contains_key(id)
                    || (snapshot && !state.items.iter().any(|row| row.id == *id))
            }
        }
    }

    /// Services, render target and output for one call.
    pub struct Context {
        inner: Ctx,
        surface: MountSurface,

    impl Context {

        /// Starts a render on the selected surface.
        #[must_use]
        pub fn for_render_on(inner: Ctx, surface: MountSurface) -> Self {
            Self {
                inner,
                surface,
                state_root: None,
                is_action: false,
                receiver: ActionReceiver::default(),
            }

        /// Starts an action with the component root supplied by the host.

                inner,
                surface,
                state_root,
                is_action: true,
                receiver: ActionReceiver::default(),

        pub(crate) fn is_action(&self) -> bool {
            self.is_action
        }

            &self.inner

        pub fn surface(&self) -> MountSurface {
            self.surface

        #[must_use]

    /// One pending update from the receiver.
    pub struct ReceiverItem(Output);
    
    enum Output {
        View(OperationT),
        State(PendingState),
        Placement {
            place: PlaceT,
            state: Option<PendingState>,
        },
        Data {
            target: u32,
            bytes: Vec<u8>,
        },
    }
    
    struct PendingState {
        targets: Vec<u32>,
        body: Vec<u8>,
    }
    
    impl PendingState {
        fn new<T: Serialize + ?Sized>(
            targets: &[u32],
            value: &T,
        ) -> Result<Self, ErrorTrace<ActionError>> {
            if targets.is_empty() {
                return Err(output_error("Component state needs at least one target"));
            }
            let body = serde_json::to_vec(value)
                .map_err(|e| output_error("Cannot encode component state").attach(e))?;
            let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
            let targets = targets
                .iter()
                .copied()
                .filter(|id| seen.insert(*id))
                .collect();
            Ok(Self { targets, body })
        }
    
        fn attachments(self, ctx: &Ctx) -> Result<Vec<OperationT>, ErrorTrace<ActionError>> {
            let signed = sign_state(ctx, &self.body)
                .map_err(|e| output_error("Cannot sign component state").attach(e))?;
            Ok(self
                .targets
                .into_iter()
                .map(|target| {
                    let mut attachment = AttachStateT::default();
                    attachment.root_node = target;
                    attachment.state = Some(signed.clone());
                    let mut operation = OperationT::default();
                    operation.ui = UiOperationT::AttachState(Box::new(attachment));
                    operation
                })
                .collect())
        }
    }
    
    /// Stores pending updates in the order of their calls.
    #[derive(Default)]
    pub struct ActionReceiver {
        items: Mutex<Vec<ReceiverItem>>,
    }
    
    impl ActionReceiver {
        /// Queues the next state for one node.
        ///
        /// # Errors
        ///
        /// Returns an action error if serialization fails.
        pub fn state<T: Serialize + ?Sized>(&self, target: u32, value: &T) -> ActionResult {
            self.state_for(&[target], value)
        }
    
        /// Queues one state value for the root and each marked node in a render.
        /// Each distinct target receives the same signed bytes.
        ///
        /// # Errors
        ///
        /// Returns an action error if the target list is empty or serialization fails.
        pub fn state_for<T: Serialize + ?Sized>(&self, targets: &[u32], value: &T) -> ActionResult {
            self.push(Output::State(PendingState::new(targets, value)?));
            Ok(())
        }
    
        /// Queues application data encoded in the `MessagePack` format.
        pub fn data(&self, target: u32, bytes: Vec<u8>) {
            self.push(Output::Data { target, bytes });
        }
    
        /// Send MessagePack data to the view that receives this action or subscription.
        pub fn data_in_view(&self, bytes: Vec<u8>) {
            self.data(0, bytes);
        }
    
        /// Records an operation from the template renderer.
        #[doc(hidden)]
        pub fn render_op(&self, operation: OperationT) {
            self.push(Output::View(operation));
        }
    
        pub(crate) fn render_tree<S: Serialize + ?Sized>(
            &self,
            ops: Vec<OperationT>,
            placement: Option<PlaceT>,
            targets: &[u32],
            state: Option<&S>,
        ) -> ActionResult {
            let state = state.map(|s| PendingState::new(targets, s)).transpose()?;
            let mut items = self.items.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner);
            if let Some(mut place) = placement {
                place.operations = Some(ops);
                items.push(ReceiverItem(Output::Placement { place, state }));
            } else {
                items.extend(ops.into_iter().map(|op| ReceiverItem(Output::View(op))));
                if let Some(s) = state {
                    items.push(ReceiverItem(Output::State(s)));
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    
        fn push(&self, output: Output) {
            self.items
                .lock()
                .unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
                .push(ReceiverItem(output));
        }
    
        /// Takes all updates after the call finishes.
        #[must_use]
        pub fn drain(self) -> Vec<ReceiverItem> {
            self.items
                .into_inner()
                .unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
        }
    }
    
    /// Signs pending state and writes one frame with the supplied client capabilities.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns an action error if the signer or frame writer rejects any item.
    pub fn encode_updates(
        ctx: &Ctx,
        items: Vec<ReceiverItem>,
        caps: &ClientCaps,
        header: FrameHeader,
        config: &WriterConfig,
    ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ErrorTrace<ActionError>> {
        write_messages(prepare_messages(ctx, items)?, caps, header, config)
            .map(|(bytes, _report)| bytes)
            .map_err(|error| output_error("Cannot write the update frame").attach(error))
    }
    
    /// Signs queued state and builds ordered messages for the delivery handler.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns an action error if signing fails or a view operation contains a state attachment.
    pub fn prepare_messages(
        ctx: &Ctx,
        items: Vec<ReceiverItem>,
    ) -> Result<Vec<MessageT>, ErrorTrace<ActionError>> {
        let mut messages = Vec::with_capacity(items.len());
        for ReceiverItem(output) in items {
            match output {
                Output::View(operation) => {
                    if contains_state_attachment(&operation) {
                        return Err(output_error("Use the receiver to attach component state."));
                    }
                    messages.push(operation_message(operation));
                }
                Output::State(state) => {
                    messages.extend(state.attachments(ctx)?.into_iter().map(operation_message));
                }
                Output::Placement { mut place, state } => {
                    let ops = place.operations.get_or_insert_with(Vec::new);
                    if ops.iter().any(contains_state_attachment) {
                        return Err(output_error("Use the receiver to attach component state."));
                    }
                    if let Some(state) = state {
                        ops.extend(state.attachments(ctx)?);
                    }
                    let mut operation = OperationT::default();
                    operation.ui = UiOperationT::Place(Box::new(place));
                    messages.push(operation_message(operation));
                }
                Output::Data { target, bytes } => {
                    let mut blob = MessagePackBlobT::default();
                    blob.target_node = target;
                    blob.bytes = Some(bytes);
                    let mut data = DataT::default();
                    data.target_node = target;
                    data.msgpack = Some(Box::new(blob));
                    let mut message = MessageT::default();
                    message.data = Some(Box::new(data));
                    messages.push(message);
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(messages)
    }
    
    fn contains_state_attachment(operation: &OperationT) -> bool {
        if operation
            .columnar
            .as_deref()
            .and_then(|batch| batch.op_codes.as_deref())
            .is_some_and(|codes| codes.contains(&UiOperation::AttachState.0))
        {
            return true;
        }
        match &operation.ui {
            UiOperationT::AttachState(_) => true,
            UiOperationT::Place(place) => place
                .operations
                .as_deref()
                .is_some_and(|ops| ops.iter().any(contains_state_attachment)),
            UiOperationT::ReplaceSubtree(tree) => tree
                .operations
                .as_deref()
                .is_some_and(|children| children.iter().any(contains_state_attachment)),
            _ => false,
        }
    }
    
    fn operation_message(operation: OperationT) -> MessageT {
        let mut message = MessageT::default();
        message.operation = Some(Box::new(operation));
        message
    }
    
    fn output_error(detail: impl Into<String>) -> ErrorTrace<ActionError> {
        ErrorTrace::new(ActionError::new(ErrorCode::ActionFailed, detail))
    }

    /// The renderer reads these values from the control that triggered the action.
    #[derive(Debug)]
    pub struct TriggerEvent {
        pub node_id: u32,
        pub input: ActionInputT,
        /// Copy the control's signed bytes. An empty vector means that the control has no state.
        pub state: Vec<u8>,
    }
    
    /// Some transports return one reply. Others deliver the reply on a separate receive path.
    #[cfg(not(target_family = "wasm"))]
    pub type TransportFuture<'a> =
        Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, ManagerError>> + Send + 'a>>;
    
    #[cfg(target_family = "wasm")]
    pub type TransportFuture<'a> =
        Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, ManagerError>> + 'a>>;
    
    /// An adapter for the selected runtime.
    pub trait ActionTransport {
        /// Submit requests in call order. The returned future waits for a reply or a socket handoff.
        /// Queue ordered streams here, before the future can yield. Return promptly.
        fn send(&self, frame: Vec<u8>) -> TransportFuture<'_>;
    }
    
    #[cfg(not(target_family = "wasm"))]
    pub type Transport = dyn ActionTransport + Send + Sync;
    #[cfg(target_family = "wasm")]
    pub type Transport = dyn ActionTransport;
    
    /// Reports a routing, encoding or transport failure to the caller.
    #[derive(Debug)]
    pub enum ManagerError {
        Lookup(LookupError),
        Wire(WireError),
        SequenceExhausted,
        Transport(String),
        SubmissionPoisoned,
        InvalidInput(String),
        UnsupportedInput,
    }
    
    impl fmt::Display for ManagerError {
        fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            match self {
                Self::Lookup(error) => fmt::Display::fmt(error, f),
                Self::Wire(error) => fmt::Display::fmt(error, f),
                Self::SequenceExhausted => f.write_str("The stream used its last request number."),
                Self::Transport(detail) => write!(f, "Action transport failed. {detail}"),
                Self::InvalidInput(detail) => write!(f, "Invalid action input. {detail}"),
                Self::UnsupportedInput => {
                    f.write_str("The peer did not negotiate structured action input.")
                }
                Self::SubmissionPoisoned => {
                    f.write_str("An earlier request panicked during submission.")
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    impl std::error::Error for ManagerError {
        fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {
            match self {
                Self::Lookup(error) => Some(error),
                Self::Wire(error) => Some(error),
                _ => None,
            }
        }
    }
    
    impl From<LookupError> for ManagerError {
        fn from(error: LookupError) -> Self {
            Self::Lookup(error)
        }
    }

        registry: Arc<ActionRegistry>,

    impl ActionManager {
        #[must_use]
        pub fn new(
            registry: Arc<ActionRegistry>,

        ) -> Self {
            Self {
                registry,
                surface,

        #[must_use]

        /// Replace the names advertised by the server for this surface.
        pub fn apply_caps(&self, caps: &ServerCapsT) {
            let mut names = BTreeSet::new();
            if caps.status == CapsStatus::Ok {
                names.extend(
                    caps.actions
                        .iter()
                        .flatten()
                        .filter_map(|action| action.name.clone()),
                );
            }
            *self
                .server_actions
                .write()
                .unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner) = Some(ServerActions {
                names,
                stream_id: caps.stream_id,
                structured: caps.status == CapsStatus::Ok
                    && caps.vocabulary_version >= foundation_ui_wire::vocab::STRUCTURED_INPUT_VERSION,
            });
        }
    
        fn route(
            &self,
            reference: &ActionRef<'_>,
        ) -> Result<(Origin, &Transport, bool, u64), LookupError> {
            let advertised = self
                .server_actions
                .read()
                .unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner);
            let available = advertised
                .as_ref()
                .map(|caps| caps.names.contains(reference.name));
            let declaration = self
                .registry
                .lookup(reference.origin, reference.name, self.surface);
            let origin = match (reference.origin, declaration) {
                (Origin::Host, Ok(entry)) => {
                    if entry.local {
                        Origin::Host
                    } else if entry.origin.is_none() && available == Some(true) {
                        Origin::Server
                    } else {
                        return Err(LookupError::UnavailableOrigin);
                    }
                }
                (Origin::Server, Ok(_)) if available != Some(false) => Origin::Server,
                (Origin::Server, Ok(_)) => return Err(LookupError::UnavailableOrigin),
                (Origin::Server, Err(LookupError::UnknownAction)) if available == Some(true) => {
                    Origin::Server
                }
                (_, Err(error)) => return Err(error),
            };
            let transport = match origin {
                Origin::Host => self.host.as_deref(),
                Origin::Server => self.server.as_deref(),
            };
            let structured =
                origin == Origin::Host || advertised.as_ref().is_some_and(|caps| caps.structured);
            let stream_id = match origin {
                Origin::Host => self.stream_id,
                Origin::Server => advertised
                    .as_ref()
                    .map(|caps| caps.stream_id)
                    .filter(|id| *id != 0)
                    .unwrap_or(self.stream_id),
            };
            Ok((
                origin,
                transport.ok_or(LookupError::UnavailableOrigin)?,
                structured,
                stream_id,
            ))
        }
    
        /// Check that a callback names Rust code installed on this core.
        ///
        /// # Errors
        /// Rejects server routes, missing handlers, and unavailable local transports.
        pub fn require_local_handler(&self, reference: &str) -> Result<(), LookupError> {
            let action = ActionRef::parse(reference)?;
            if action.origin != Origin::Host || self.host.is_none() {
                return Err(LookupError::UnavailableOrigin);
            }
            self.registry
                .get(Origin::Host, action.name, self.surface)
                .map(|_| ())
        }

        /// Sends the hello. A transport can deliver capabilities later through `receive_capabilities`.
        ///
        /// # Errors
        /// Returns a transport error or an invalid capability reply.
        pub async fn connect(&self) -> Result<(), ManagerError> {
            let request = client_hello(&self.caps);
            if let Some(reply) = self.transport.send(request).await? {
                self.receive_capabilities(&reply)?;
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    
        /// Replaces the server action list after a complete capability reply arrives.
        ///
        /// # Errors
        /// Returns the frame error or the required version update.
        pub fn receive_capabilities(&self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), ManagerError> {
            let caps = server_capabilities(bytes, self.writer.wire_limits(), self.caps.mount)?;
            self.manager.apply_caps(&caps);
            if caps.status != foundation_ui_wire::CapsStatus::Ok {
                return Err(invalid("The server requires a client update"));
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    
        /// Sends the action to its owner and validates any immediate reply.
        ///
        /// # Errors
        /// Returns the lookup, transport or frame error.
        pub async fn trigger(
            &self,
            reference: &str,
            event: TriggerEvent,
        ) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, ManagerError> {
            let reply = self.manager.trigger(reference, event).await?;
            if let Some(bytes) = &reply {
                reply_message(bytes, self.writer.wire_limits(), self.caps.mount)?;
            }
            Ok(reply)
        }
    }

    impl crate::PendingStorage for FileStorage {
        async fn load(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
            let path = self.0.clone();
            blocking::unblock(move || match std::fs::read(path) {
                Ok(bytes) => Ok(bytes),
                Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(vec![]),
                Err(error) => Err(error.to_string()),
            })
            .await
        }
    
        async fn save(&self, contents: Vec<u8>) -> Result<(), String> {
            let path = self.0.clone();
            blocking::unblock(move || -> std::io::Result<()> {
                let parent = path
                    .parent()
                    .ok_or_else(|| std::io::Error::other("Missing outbox directory"))?;
                std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
                let mut file = tempfile::NamedTempFile::new_in(parent)?;
                file.write_all(&contents)?;
                file.as_file().sync_all()?;
                file.persist(&path).map_err(|e| e.error)?;
                std::fs::File::open(parent)?.sync_all()
            })
            .await
            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())
        }
    }

        }
    }
    
    impl Sender {
        fn publish(&self, context: Context) -> Result<(), CoreError> {
            let messages =
                prepare_messages(&self.ctx, context.into_receiver().drain()).map_err(failed)?;
            if messages.is_empty() {
                return Ok(());
            }
            let operations = messages
                .into_iter()
                .map(|message| {
                    message
                        .operation
                        .map(|op| *op)
                        .ok_or_else(|| failed("A pending preview requires a view operation"))
                })
                .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
            self.core
                .get()
                .and_then(Weak::upgrade)
                .ok_or_else(|| failed("The Todo screen closed"))?
                .push_ops(operations)?;
            Ok(())
        }
    }

    impl HostTransport for Sender {
        async fn send(&self, original: Vec<u8>) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, CoreError> {
            let context = Context::for_render_on(self.ctx.clone(), MountSurface::Native);
            let plan = outbox::prepare(&context, original).await.map_err(failed)?;
            self.publish(context)?;
            let Some(request) = plan.request else {
                return Ok(None);
            };
            let result = self.transport.send(request).await;
            let failure = match &result {
                Err(_) => Some(None),
                Ok(Some(bytes)) => match read_frame(bytes, &WireLimits::default()) {
                    Err(_) => Some(None),
                    Ok(frame) => frame
                        .kind_as_frame_message()
                        .and_then(|body| body.messages())
                        .and_then(|messages| {
                            messages.iter().find_map(|message| {
                                let error = message.control()?.error()?;
                                Some(
                                    (error.code() == foundation_ui_wire::ErrorCode::InvalidInput).then(
                                        || error.message().unwrap_or("Check the title").to_owned(),
                                    ),
                                )
                            })
                        }),
                },
                Ok(None) => None,
            };
            if let (Some(key), Some(validation)) = (plan.key, failure) {
                let context = Context::for_render_on(self.ctx.clone(), MountSurface::Native);
                outbox::failed(&context, &key, validation)
                    .await
                    .map_err(failed)?;
                self.publish(context)?;
            }
            result
        }
    }

        ///
        /// # Errors

        pub async fn trigger_structured<E: serde::Serialize>(
            &self,
            reference: &str,
            mut event: TriggerEvent,
            value: &E,

        /// Send one request. A socket can accept it before a reply exists.
        ///
        /// # Errors
        ///
        /// Returns a lookup error before submission for an invalid route.
        /// Reports encoding, sequence and transport failures separately.
        pub async fn trigger(
            &self,
            reference: &str,
            event: TriggerEvent,
        ) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, ManagerError> {
            let reference = ActionRef::parse(reference)?;
            let (origin, transport, structured, stream_id) = self.route(&reference)?;
            if event.input.json.is_some() {
                if event.input.value.is_some() {
                    return Err(ManagerError::InvalidInput(
                        "The event supplied two input encodings".into(),
                    ));
                }
                if !structured {
                    return Err(ManagerError::UnsupportedInput);
                }
            }
            let prefix = match origin {
                Origin::Host => "host:",
                Origin::Server => "server:",
            };
            let limit = self
                .limits
                .frame_bytes()
                .min(self.limits.action_request_bytes());
            let content_len = [
                prefix.len(),
                reference.name.len(),
                event.state.len(),
                event.input.event_name.as_deref().unwrap_or_default().len(),
                event.input.value.as_deref().unwrap_or_default().len(),
                event.input.json.as_deref().unwrap_or_default().len(),
            ]
            .into_iter()
            .fold(0usize, usize::saturating_add);
            check_size(content_len, limit)?;
    
            let mut action = ActionRequestT::default();
            action.action = Some(format!("{prefix}{}", reference.name));
            action.input = Some(Box::new(event.input));
            if !event.state.is_empty() {
                action.state = Some(event.state);
            }
            action.node_id = event.node_id;
            let mut request = FrameRequestT::default();
            request.action = Some(Box::new(action));
            let mut frame = FrameT::default();
            frame.schema_version = SCHEMA_VERSION;
            frame.stream_id = stream_id;
            frame.kind = FrameKindT::FrameRequest(Box::new(request));
    
            let reply = {
                let mut last = self
                    .last_sequence
                    .lock()
                    .map_err(|_| ManagerError::SubmissionPoisoned)?;
                frame.sequence_id = last.checked_add(1).ok_or(ManagerError::SequenceExhausted)?;
                let bytes = finish_frame(&frame).map_err(ManagerError::Wire)?;
                check_size(bytes.len(), limit)?;
                *last = frame.sequence_id;
                transport.send(bytes)
            };
            reply.await
        }
    }
    
    fn check_size(actual: usize, limit: usize) -> Result<(), ManagerError> {
        if actual > limit {
            return Err(ManagerError::Wire(WireError::TooLarge { actual, limit }));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

        /// Sends a complete local update to the current listener.
        ///
        /// # Errors
        /// Returns an error if the listener is absent, the sequence is exhausted, or the writer rejects an operation.
        pub fn push_ops(&self, ops: Vec<OperationT>) -> Result<u64, CoreError> {
            let push = self.prepare_push(ops)?;
            Ok(self.publish(push))
        }
    
        pub(crate) fn limits(&self) -> &foundation_ui_wire::WireLimits {
            self.writer.wire_limits()
        }
    
        pub(crate) fn prepare_push(&self, ops: Vec<OperationT>) -> Result<Push, CoreError> {
            let listener = self
                .listener
                .lock()
                .unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
                .clone()
                .ok_or(CoreError::NoListener)?;
            let messages = ops
                .into_iter()
                .map(foundation_ui_wire::ops::message)
                .collect();
            // A nonzero placeholder reserves the generated sequence field in this owned buffer.
            let header = FrameHeader {
                stream_id: 0,
                sequence_id: 1,
                ack: 0,
            };
            let (bytes, _) =
                write_messages(messages, &self.caps, header, &self.writer).map_err(CoreError::write)?;
            let frame = read_frame(&bytes, self.limits()).map_err(CoreError::write)?;
            let sequence_offset = frame._tab.loc()
                + usize::from(
                    frame
                        ._tab
                        .vtable()
                        .get(foundation_ui_wire::Frame::VT_SEQUENCE_ID),
                );
            let mut delivery = self.delivery.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner);
            if delivery.tickets.last() == u64::MAX {
                return Err(CoreError::write("No push identifiers remain"));
            }
            delivery.tickets.next();
            Ok(Push {
                #[cfg(feature = "app")]
                ticket: delivery.tickets.last(),
                sequence_offset,
                listener,
                bytes,
            })
        }
    
        pub(crate) fn publish(&self, mut push: Push) -> u64 {
            let sequence = {
                let mut delivery = self.delivery.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner);
                // Every publication owns one unique ticket. A cancelled ticket consumes no sequence.
                let sequence = delivery.sequence.next();
                let offset = push.sequence_offset;
                push.bytes[offset..offset + 8].copy_from_slice(&sequence.to_le_bytes());
                delivery.queue.push_back(push);
                if delivery.draining {
                    return sequence;
                }
                delivery.draining = true;
                sequence
            };
            let mut panic = None;
            loop {
                let next = {
                    let mut delivery = self.delivery.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner);
                    if let Some(next) = delivery.queue.pop_front() {
                        next
                    } else {
                        delivery.draining = false;
                        break;
                    }
                };
                let callback = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
                    next.listener.on_frame(next.bytes);
                }));
                if let Err(payload) = callback {
                    panic.get_or_insert(payload);
                }
            }
            if let Some(payload) = panic {
                std::panic::resume_unwind(payload)
            }
            sequence
        }
    }

    async fn local_services_and_remote_capabilities_share_one_client() {
        for immediate in [false, true] {
            let (ctx, _) = super::support::test_ctx(super::support::WALL);
            ctx.store(AtomicUsize::new(0));
            let mut actions = ActionRegistry::new();
            actions.register(count).unwrap();
            let sender = Arc::new(Sender::default());
            let app = NetworkApp::builder(
                ctx.clone(),
                actions,
                ClientCaps::web_current(),
                MountSurface::Web,
            )
            .with_server_transport(sender.clone())
            .build();
            assert!(app.trigger("server:save", event()).await.is_err());
            app.trigger("host:count", event()).await.unwrap();
            assert_eq!(ctx.get::<AtomicUsize>().unwrap().load(Ordering::Relaxed), 1);
            assert!(sender.requests.lock().unwrap().is_empty());
            if immediate {
                *sender.next.lock().unwrap() = Some(advertised());
            }
            app.connect().await.unwrap();
            {
                let sent = sender.requests.lock().unwrap();
                assert_eq!(sent.len(), 1);
                let frame = read_frame(&sent[0], &WireLimits::default()).unwrap();
                assert!(frame.kind_as_frame_request().unwrap().hello().is_some());
            }
            if !immediate {
                assert!(app.receive_capabilities(b"broken").is_err());
                assert!(app.trigger("server:save", event()).await.is_err());
                app.receive_capabilities(&advertised()).unwrap();
            }
            let bytes =
                include_bytes!("../../foundation_ui_wire/fixtures/frame_ops_counter.bin").to_vec();
            *sender.next.lock().unwrap() = Some(bytes.clone());
            assert_eq!(
                app.trigger("server:save", event()).await.unwrap(),
                Some(bytes)
            );
            assert!(app.trigger("server:save", event()).await.unwrap().is_none());
            *sender.next.lock().unwrap() = Some(vec![0]);
            assert!(app.trigger("server:save", event()).await.is_err());
            assert_eq!(sender.requests.lock().unwrap().len(), 4);
        }

    pub fn reply_message<'a>(
        bytes: &'a [u8],
        limits: &WireLimits,
        surface: MountSurface,
    ) -> Result<FrameMessage<'a>, ManagerError> {
        let frame = read_frame(bytes, limits).map_err(invalid)?;
        if frame.schema_version() != SCHEMA_VERSION {
            return Err(invalid("Unsupported frame schema"));
        }
        let body = frame
            .kind_as_frame_message()
            .ok_or_else(|| invalid("Expected a message frame"))?;
        for msg in body.messages().into_iter().flatten() {
            let fields = u8::from(msg.operation().is_some())
                + u8::from(msg.control().is_some())
                + u8::from(msg.data().is_some());
            if fields != 1 {
                return Err(invalid("A message must have exactly one body"));
            }
            if let Some(op) = msg.operation().filter(|_| surface == MountSurface::Native) {
                validate_native(op)?;
            }
        }
        Ok(body)
    }
    
    fn validate_native(op: Operation<'_>) -> Result<(), ManagerError> {
        if op.web_type() != WebOperation::NONE {
            return Err(invalid("Web operation on a native mount"));
        }
        let children = op
            .ui_as_replace_subtree()
            .and_then(|tree| tree.operations())
            .or_else(|| op.ui_as_place().and_then(|tree| tree.operations()));
        for child in children.into_iter().flatten() {
            validate_native(child)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

                registry: Arc::new(registry),
                platform: NativePlatform::Ios,

        );

    pub(super) enum Failure {

        Expired,
        UpdateRequired(u16),

    impl Failure {
        pub(super) fn bad_request() -> Self {
            Self::Error(ActionError::new(ErrorCode::BadRequest, "bad request"))

        pub(super) fn encode(self, header: FrameHeader, config: &WriterConfig) -> Vec<u8> {
            let mut control = ControlT::default();
            match self {
                Self::Expired => control.state_expired = Some(Box::new(StateExpiredT::default())),
                Self::UpdateRequired(client_version) => {
                    let mut update = UpdateRequiredT::default();
                    update.client_schema_version = client_version;
                    update.server_schema_version = SCHEMA_VERSION;
                    control.update_required = Some(Box::new(update));
                }
                Self::Error(error) => {
                    let mut wire = ActionErrorT::default();
                    wire.code = error.code;
                    if error.message.len() <= config.wire_limits().frame_bytes() {
                        wire.message = Some(error.message);
                    }
                    control.error = Some(Box::new(wire));
                }
            }
            let mut message = MessageT::default();
            message.control = Some(Box::new(control));
            // Control messages use only schema fields. They work before vocabulary negotiation.
            let caps = ClientCaps::web_current();
            if let Ok((bytes, _)) = write_messages(vec![message.clone()], &caps, header, config) {
                return bytes;
            }
            if let Some(error) = message
                .control
                .as_mut()
                .and_then(|control| control.error.as_mut())
            {
                error.message = None;
            }
            // This scalar-only protocol reply fits the default limit even when the configured limit is one byte.
            write_messages(vec![message], &caps, header, &WriterConfig::default())
                .expect("one scalar control message fits the default frame limit")
                .0
        }
    }

                LookupError::UnknownAction => "unknown action",
                LookupError::UnsupportedAction => "action not supported on this surface",

## Assistant

You’re right. **When a Todo screen uses WebSocket, its server actions share one action connection.** Add, Complete, and Delete each send a message through that connection. Opening the Add dialog runs locally and sends nothing.

Commit `43ac84755` adds an **optional** way for Rust code to open another socket explicitly. For example, a game can open one connection to its game server and reuse it throughout the session.

The test opened two sockets on purpose. It closed the game-style socket, then requested the Todo count through the original action connection. That confirmed the two connections have independent lifetimes.

                    }

                UiOperationT::Place(tree) => {
                    for child in tree.operations.unwrap_or_default() {
                        collect(child.ui, found);
                    }
                }
                UiOperationT::LiveMount(_) => panic!("Unexpected live subscription"),
                _ => found.push(op),
            }
        }
        let frame = read_frame(frame, &WireLimits::default()).unwrap();
        let body = frame.kind_as_frame_message().unwrap().unpack();
        let mut found = Vec::new();
        for message in body.messages.unwrap() {
            assert!(message.control.is_none(), "{:?}", message.control);
            if let Some(op) = message.operation {
                collect(op.ui, &mut found);
            }
        }
        found
    }
    
    fn shows(ops: &[UiOperationT], text: &str) -> bool {
        ops.iter()
            .any(|op| matches!(op, UiOperationT::SetText(value) if value.text.as_deref() == Some(text)))
    }
    
    fn shows_control(ops: &[UiOperationT], kind: NodeKind) -> bool {
        ops.iter()
            .any(|op| matches!(op, UiOperationT::CreateNode(node) if node.kind == kind))
    }
    
    fn binding(ops: &[UiOperationT], action: &str) -> (u32, EventId) {
        let found = ops.iter().find_map(|op| match op {
            UiOperationT::BindAction(binding) if binding.action.as_deref() == Some(action) => {
                Some((binding.node_id, binding.event))
            }
            _ => None,
        });
        found.unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("Missing action {action}"))
    }
    
    fn state(ops: &[UiOperationT], node: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
        ops.iter()
            .find_map(|op| match op {
                UiOperationT::AttachState(attach) if attach.root_node == node => attach.state.clone(),
                _ => None,
            })
            .unwrap_or_default()
    }
    
    async fn trigger(
        core: &NativeCore,
        ops: &[UiOperationT],
        action: &str,
        value: &str,
    ) -> Vec<UiOperationT> {
        let (node_id, event) = binding(ops, action);
        let update = core
            .trigger(
                action.into(),
                EventInput {
                    node_id,
                    event_name: event.variant_name().unwrap().to_ascii_lowercase(),
                    value: value.into(),
                    checked: false,
                    parent_node: 0,
                    state: state(ops, node_id),
                },
            )
            .await
            .unwrap()
            .unwrap();
        operations(&update)
    }
    
    #[valtron_test]
    async fn dialogs_use_one_server_binding_and_cancel_without_transport() {
        for platform in [NativePlatform::Ios, NativePlatform::Android] {
            let ctx = Ctx::host();
            install_view_services(&ctx, foundation_ui_runtime::action::Origin::Host).unwrap();
            install_cache(&ctx);
            let transport = Arc::new(FailTransport::default());
            let core = NativeCore::new(
                CoreConfig {
                    platform,
                    registry: Arc::new(host_registry().unwrap()),
                    ctx,
                    writer: WriterConfig::default(),
                },
                Some(transport.clone()),
            );
            let first = operations(&initial_todo_frame(core.clone()).await.unwrap());
            assert!(shows(&first, "0 open todos"));
            assert!(shows_control(&first, NodeKind::NAVIGATION_TITLE));
            assert!(shows_control(&first, NodeKind::SEGMENTED_CONTROL));
    
            let sheet = trigger(&core, &first, "host:open_add_dialog", "").await;
            for expected in [NodeKind::MODAL, NodeKind::BOTTOM_SHEET] {
                assert_eq!(
                    sheet
                        .iter()
                        .filter(
                            |op| matches!(op, UiOperationT::CreateNode(node) if node.kind == expected)
                        )
                        .count(),
                    1,
                );
            }
            let _ = binding(&sheet, "server:add_todo");
            let closed = trigger(&core, &sheet, "host:close_dialog", "").await;
            assert!(!shows_control(&closed, NodeKind::MODAL));
            assert_eq!(transport.0.load(Ordering::Relaxed), 0);
            let independent = create_local_todo_core(platform).unwrap();
            let other = operations(&initial_todo_frame(independent).await.unwrap());
            assert!(shows(&other, "0 open todos"));
        }
    }

    #[cfg_attr(not(target_family = "wasm"), async_trait::async_trait)]
    pub trait ChildActionCaller: Send + Sync {
        /// Submit a structured payload and deliver any immediate reply to the view.
        ///
        /// # Errors
        /// Returns the routing, transport, or reply error.
        async fn call(&self, reference: &str, json: Vec<u8>) -> Result<(), ActionError>;
    }
    
    /// Services, render target and output for one call.
    pub struct Context {
        inner: Ctx,
        surface: MountSurface,
        state_root: Option<u32>,
        is_action: bool,
        pub(crate) child_caller: Option<Arc<dyn ChildActionCaller>>,
        receiver: ActionReceiver,
    }
    
    impl Context {
        /// Starts a web render with the supplied host services.
        #[must_use]
        pub fn for_render(inner: Ctx) -> Self {
            Self::for_render_on(inner, MountSurface::Web)
        }
    
        /// Starts a render on the selected surface.
        #[must_use]
        pub fn for_render_on(inner: Ctx, surface: MountSurface) -> Self {
            Self {
                inner,
                surface,
                state_root: None,
                is_action: false,
                child_caller: None,
                receiver: ActionReceiver::default(),
            }
        }
    
        /// Starts an action with the component root supplied by the host.
        #[must_use]
        pub fn for_action(inner: Ctx, surface: MountSurface, state_root: Option<u32>) -> Self {
            Self {
                inner,
                surface,
                state_root,
                is_action: true,
                child_caller: None,
                receiver: ActionReceiver::default(),
            }
        }
    
        /// Call an action for this view with a new payload and no inherited component state.
        ///
        /// # Errors
        /// Returns a routing, encoding, transport, or immediate reply error.
        pub async fn trigger_structured<T: Serialize + ?Sized>(
            &self,
            reference: &str,
            input: &T,
        ) -> ActionResult {
            let caller = self.child_caller.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| {
                ErrorTrace::new(ActionError::new(
                    ErrorCode::UnavailableOrigin,
                    "This view has no action caller",
                ))
            })?;
            let json = serde_json::to_vec(input).map_err(|cause| {
                ErrorTrace::new(ActionError::new(ErrorCode::InvalidInput, cause.to_string()))
            })?;
            caller.call(reference, json).await.map_err(ErrorTrace::new)
        }
    
        pub(crate) fn is_action(&self) -> bool {
            self.is_action
        }
    
        }
    
        pub(crate) fn prepare_push(&self, ops: Vec<OperationT>) -> Result<Push, CoreError> {
            let listener = self
                .listener
                .lock()
                .unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
                .clone()
                .ok_or(CoreError::NoListener)?;
            let messages = ops
                .into_iter()
                .map(foundation_ui_wire::ops::message)
                .collect();
            // A nonzero placeholder reserves the generated sequence field in this owned buffer.
            let header = FrameHeader {
                stream_id: 0,
                sequence_id: 1,
                ack: 0,
            };
            let (bytes, _) =
                write_messages(messages, &self.caps, header, &self.writer).map_err(CoreError::write)?;
            let frame = read_frame(&bytes, self.limits()).map_err(CoreError::write)?;
            let sequence_offset = frame._tab.loc()
                + usize::from(
                    frame
                        ._tab
                        .vtable()
                        .get(foundation_ui_wire::Frame::VT_SEQUENCE_ID),
    struct CoreCaller(std::sync::Weak<NativeCore>);
    
    #[async_trait::async_trait]
    impl foundation_ui_runtime::action::ChildActionCaller for CoreCaller {
        async fn call(
            &self,
            reference: &str,
            json: Vec<u8>,
        ) -> Result<(), foundation_ui_runtime::action::ActionError> {
            use foundation_ui_runtime::action::{ActionError, ManagerError, TriggerEvent};
            use foundation_ui_wire::ErrorCode;
    
            let core = self.0.upgrade().ok_or_else(|| {
                ActionError::new(ErrorCode::UnavailableOrigin, "The calling view closed")
            })?;
            let mut event: TriggerEvent = EventInput::receiving_view().into();
            event.input.value = None;
            event.input.json = Some(json);
            let reply = core
                .manager
                .trigger(reference, event)
                .await
                .map_err(|cause| {
                    let code = match &cause {
                        ManagerError::Lookup(error) => error.code(),
                        ManagerError::InvalidInput(_) => ErrorCode::InvalidInput,
                        ManagerError::UnsupportedInput => ErrorCode::UnsupportedAction,
                        _ => ErrorCode::ActionFailed,
                    };
                    ActionError::new(code, cause.to_string())
                })?;
            if let Some(bytes) = reply {
                core.deliver_action_reply(bytes)?;
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    }

    pub trait ChildActionCaller: Send + Sync {
        /// Submit a structured payload and deliver any immediate reply to the view.
        ///
        /// # Errors
        /// Returns the routing, transport, or reply error.
        async fn call(
            &self,
            reference: &str,
            json: Vec<u8>,

    /// Services, render target and output for one call.
    pub struct Context {
        inner: Ctx,
        surface: MountSurface,
        /// # Errors
        /// Returns a routing, encoding, transport, or immediate reply error.
        pub async fn trigger_structured<T: Serialize + ?Sized>(
            &self,
            reference: &str,
            input: &T,
        ) -> ActionResult {
            let caller = self.child_caller.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| {
                ErrorTrace::new(ActionError::new(
                    ErrorCode::UnavailableOrigin,
                    "This view has no action caller",
                ))
            })?;
            let json = serde_json::to_vec(input).map_err(|cause| {

            let items = std::mem::take(
                &mut *self
                    .receiver
                    .items
                    .lock()
                    .unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner),
            );
            let preview = prepare_messages(self.inner(), items)?;
            caller
                .call(reference, json, preview)
                .await
                .map_err(ErrorTrace::new)
        }

      assert.equal(reloads.length, 1);
    });
    
    test("a declared web host action can call a global function", async () => {
      let calls = 0;
      const {manager, registry, errors} = setup({scope: {notify() {calls++;}}});
      registry.declare("host", "notify", "web");
      await manager.trigger("host:notify", element(2));
      assert.equal(calls, 1);
      assert.deepEqual(errors, []);
    });
    
    test("a remount can replace the callback owned by its node", () => {
      const registry = new JsActionRegistry();
      const next = () => {};
      registry.registerHost("notify", () => {}, element(2));
      registry.registerHost("notify", next, element(2));
      assert.equal(registry.hostFunction("notify"), next);
      assert.throws(() => registry.registerHost("notify", next, element(3)));
    });

      manager.applyCaps({streamId:80n, actions:[]});
      assert.equal(el["data-ewe-unavailable"], true);
      await manager.trigger("server:save", el);
      assert.deepEqual(errors, ["UnavailableOrigin"]);

      assert.equal(el["data-ewe-unavailable"], false);

      registry.declare("server", "save");

      assert.equal(count, 1);

      button.classList = {contains: name => name === "ewe-submit-button"};
      button.closest = selector => selector === ".ewe-bottom-sheet" ? sheet : null;
      button.parentElement = sheet;

      assert.equal(structured.value(), null);

          receive: (_, origin) => destinations.push(origin.viewMount),
        },
        server: { send: () => new Promise(resolve => { finish = resolve; }) },
      });
      const pending = manager.trigger("server:save", clicked);
      clicked.parentElement = null;

        use super::{take_request, BTreeMap, RefCell, Vec};
        use alloc::string::{String, ToString};

        };
        
        pub(super) struct BrowserCaller(pub u64);
        type Reply = Result<(), ActionError>;
        
        std::thread_local! {
            static NEXT: Cell<u64> = const { Cell::new(0) };
            static WAITING: RefCell<BTreeMap<u64, async_channel::Sender<Reply>>> = const { RefCell::new(BTreeMap::new()) };
        }
        
        struct Pending(u64);
        impl Drop for Pending {
            fn drop(&mut self) {
                WAITING.with_borrow_mut(|calls| calls.remove(&self.0));
            }
        }
        
        fn failure(message: impl Into<String>) -> ActionError {
            ActionError::new(ErrorCode::ActionFailed, message)
        }
        
        #[async_trait::async_trait(?Send)]
        impl ChildActionCaller for BrowserCaller {
            async fn call(&self, reference: &str, json: Vec<u8>, preview: Vec<MessageT>) -> Reply {
                let bytes = if preview.is_empty() {
                    Vec::new()
                } else {
                    let header = FrameHeader { stream_id: 0, sequence_id: 0, ack: 0 };
                    write_messages(preview, &ClientCaps::web_current(), header, &WriterConfig::default())
                        .map_err(|error| failure(error.to_string()))?.0
                };
                let id = NEXT.with(|next| {
                    let id = next.get().checked_add(1)?;
                    next.set(id);
                    Some(id)
                }).ok_or_else(|| failure("Child request identifiers exhausted"))?;
                let (send, receive) = async_channel::bounded(1);
                WAITING.with_borrow_mut(|calls| calls.insert(id, send));
                let _pending = Pending(id);
                #[link(wasm_import_module = "env")]
                extern "C" {
                    fn ewe_ui_child(parent: u64, id: u64, name: *const u8, name_len: usize,
                        json: *const u8, json_len: usize, preview: *const u8, preview_len: usize);
                }
                // The browser copies all three slices before the import returns.
                unsafe { ewe_ui_child(self.0, id, reference.as_ptr(), reference.len(), json.as_ptr(), json.len(), bytes.as_ptr(), bytes.len()) };
                receive.recv().await.map_err(|_| failure("The browser action service closed"))?
            }
        }
        
        /// Complete one child call. Consume the error slot even when the caller has closed.
        #[no_mangle]
        pub extern "C" fn ewe_ui_child_done(id: u64, code: i32, slot: u64) {
            let result = if code < 0 { Ok(()) } else {
                let message = take_request(slot).and_then(|bytes| String::from_utf8(bytes).ok())
                    .unwrap_or_else(|| "Browser action failed".into());
                Err(ActionError::new(ErrorCode(u16::try_from(code).unwrap_or(ErrorCode::ActionFailed.0)), message))
            };
            if let Some(sender) = WAITING.with_borrow_mut(|calls| calls.remove(&id)) {
                // A cancelled action has already dropped its receiver.
                let _ = sender.try_send(result);
            }
        }
